author: nuniesmith
body:
## Summary

Unblocks the P1 RC-API "routing heuristic tuning" TODO. Until now the proxy logged ad-hoc strings from each backend (`dispatch_claude` had `model+tier+usage`, the Ollama/Grok branches logged at `debug` only, the streaming SSE wrapper logged nothing terminal). There was no consistent event we could aggregate to ask *"what `task_kind` did we route where, with what token cost?"* — exactly the data we need to evaluate `ModelRouter::llm_classify`'s quality.

## What changed

A single canonical structured event on every request:

```
event = "proxy.dispatch"
  task_kind                    e.g. "ArchitecturalReason"
  target                       "local" | "remote" | "claude"
  model                        resolved model slug
  prompt_tokens                u32
  completion_tokens            u32
  cache_creation_input_tokens  u32  (0 unless Claude)
  cache_read_input_tokens      u32  (0 unless Claude)
  rag_chunks_used              usize
  repo_context_injected        bool
  repo_id                      "" or x_repo_id
  cached                       true on proxy-local cache hit
  streaming                    true on SSE path
  used_fallback                true when Ollama fell back to Grok
```

Emitted from three sites in `src/api/proxy.rs`:

- Non-stream **cache hit**, before `build_oai_response`
- Non-stream **dispatch**, after `dispatch()` returns
- Streaming SSE closure, in the **`StreamChunk::Done`** branch (so streamed Claude responses still surface their cache-token counts in logs even though they don't synthesise an `RaMetadata` up front)

## Implementation notes

- `target_kind_label(&ModelTarget) -> &'static str` centralises the `"local"` / `"remote"` / `"claude"` strings so the three sites can't drift. A unit test pins the labels — they're load-bearing downstream surface.
- `DispatchLogContext` groups the 13 fields so adding/renaming one changes a single struct definition rather than three macro invocations.
- Streaming closure receives the captured task_kind as a `String` rather than `&TaskKind` because the `.map` closure is `FnMut` and `TaskKind` isn't `Copy`. `TaskKind::Display` delegates to `Debug`, so the on-wire value matches the non-stream paths.
- Collapsed three `format!("{:?}", task_kind)` calls in `handle_chat_completions` into one `task_kind_str` local that flows through `CachedProxyResponse`, `log_dispatch_event`, and `build_oai_response`.

## Out of scope

Aggregating the log stream (Loki/Promtail or a tail-and-roll-up Postgres job) and adjusting `ModelRouter::llm_classify` based on observed misclassifications. The TODO entry now reflects what landed and what remains.

author: johnrdorazio
body:
Piloting `cdcf-mcp` in the local docker stack (the next step in `docs/wordpress-mcp-evaluation.md`) revealed the prototype didn't actually work against the **real** core Abilities API — it had only ever been exercised against test stubs. Two integration bugs, both fixed and verified end-to-end.

## Bugs found & fixed

1. **All 20 abilities silently dropped.** Core's `WP_Abilities_Registry::register()` rejects any ability whose `category` isn't registered, and ability *categories* must be registered on their **own** hook (`wp_abilities_api_categories_init`), separate from abilities (`wp_abilities_api_init`). The plugin registered its `cdcf` category inside the abilities hook → category never existed → every ability rejected. Fix: split into `cdcf_mcp_register_category()` on the categories-init hook.
2. **MCP server never served.** `wordpress/mcp-adapter` is a PSR-4-only Composer library, so its plugin entry (which calls `Plugin::instance()`) never runs when bundled → `mcp_adapter_init` never fired. Fix: `cdcf-mcp.php` boots it via `\WP\MCP\Plugin::instance()`.

## Verified end-to-end (local stack)
- 20 cdcf abilities registered; `cdcf` category registered.
- `cdcf-mcp` REST namespace serving at `/wp-json/cdcf-mcp/mcp`.
- Authenticated MCP `initialize` + `tools/list` (via Application Password) returns **all 20 tools**.
- Unit tests 21 / 300 assertions; `php -l` + markdownlint clean.

## Also in this PR
- `docker-compose.override.yml`: mount the plugin into the dev stack (dev-only overrides file; base `docker-compose.yml` stays clean per the eval doc). Still requires `composer install --working-dir=wordpress/plugins/cdcf-mcp` and activation.
- Docs: record the pilot outcome + the two integration requirements in the evaluation doc and README.

## Problem

QA 답변 이미지 업로드 시 `normalizeImageFileForUpload`가 적용되지 않아 MIME 타입·확장자가 올바르게 처리되지 않는 문제가 있었습니다.

또한 `stripHtml`이 페이지마다 별도 구현되어 있었고, `IMAGE_MIME_TO_EXT` / `IMAGE_MIME_TO_EXTS` 두 개의 중복 레지스트리가 공존하고 있었습니다.

- `IMAGE_MIME_TO_EXT` 삭제 — `IMAGE_MIME_TO_EXTS`를 단일 레지스트리로 통합, HEIC 감지 로직 분기 단순화

author: jneb170
body:
## What

Replaces the Texas Citation report's browser-rendered HTML + `window.print()` with a **server-generated PDF**, so the printed TX17-4R no longer depends on each officer's browser margin/scale/header settings. The page now offers **Save as PDF** and **send to a printer** via the browser's own native print dialog — the standard mechanism, not a reinvented one.

## How

- **QuestPDF** added to `Modules.Records.UI` (Community license set at startup in `Program.cs`).
- Data resolution + display formatting lifted **verbatim** out of `CitationTexasPrint.razor` into a testable `ICitationTexasPrintModelBuilder` + flat `CitationTexasPrintModel`. Behavior is intentionally unchanged — this is purely a rendering-engine swap, so known audit items (e.g. B-6 server-local time) are preserved.
- `CitationTexasPdfDocument : IDocument` renders the UTC form.
- Razor Page `/citations/{recordNumber}/texas-pdf` (same `IActionResult` pattern as `Account/Login`), `[Authorize]`, returns the PDF **inline** by default and as an **attachment** with `?download=1`.
- `CitationTexasPrint.razor` is now a launcher: embedded PDF preview + **Download PDF** / **Print** buttons. Print loads the PDF into a hidden iframe and invokes the browser's native print dialog (OS printer list + Save-as-PDF). The old disruptive auto-print (audit **B-9**) is gone.
- New `Modules.Records.UI.Tests` project (added to the solution): builder mapping/flag tests + PDF generation smoke tests.

## Why QuestPDF over headless Chrome

Prod is an **Azure Linux App Service**. Headless Chromium there needs ~20 system libs plus a ~150 MB runtime browser download to a writable dir — the same deploy-fragility class that has taken prod down before. QuestPDF is pure-managed with zero native dependencies and renders identically on Linux.

## Verification

- **402 tests green** (was 393; +9 new), full solution builds clean.
- Generated a real PDF and inspected it: clean single-page TX17-4R; the structured violation flags mark **exactly** their boxes with no false positives (confirms the B-1 fix carries into the PDF).
- **Live-verified locally** (SQLite, `admin@authority.local`, Main Police Dept): created a citation, opened the launcher, confirmed the embedded viewer renders the PDF and the endpoint returns 200. Did not click Print in automation (it opens a blocking OS dialog); it uses the standard hidden-iframe pattern on the confirmed-200 inline URL.

## License note

QuestPDF Community is free for individuals/orgs under **$1M USD annual revenue**. If this RMS goes commercial above that threshold, a paid license is required.

author: tacotuesday8888
body:
**Phase-1 backend, PR 1 of 3.** A thin, authenticated **LLM proxy** so provider keys leave the client and AI usage can be metered. The agent stays fully on-device; only the model call moves server-side. **BYOK remains the app default** — this is the opt-in hosted path.

## What

- **`llmProxy`** = a **Genkit** flow wrapped in **`onCallGenkit`** (Firebase Cloud Functions 2nd gen). The **auth policy requires a signed-in Firebase user**, so an unauthenticated caller can never reach the model or the key (no open relay).
- **Model** via `@genkit-ai/compat-oai` (**GPT‑5.4 Mini**); the client sends a logical model id, so adding providers later is a backend change.
- **Tools:** passed as dynamic JSON-schema tools; the model **returns** tool calls (`returnToolRequests: true`) for the **on-device agent** to execute — it never runs tools server-side.
- **Quota:** per-user monthly request cap in a Firestore transaction.
- **Privacy:** usage recorded as **metadata only** (uid, model, tokens, cost, latency, status) — never prompts, responses, or screen content.
- **Secrets:** OpenAI key from **Cloud Secret Manager** (`defineSecret`), never in source.

## Structure & testing

Pure logic (quota, usage/cost, error normalization, neutral⇆Genkit translation) is split into separate modules and **unit-tested** (vitest, **15 tests**). The Genkit/Firebase wiring is **typechecked against the real SDK types** (`tsc --noEmit` green). A new **CI job** (Node 22, Ubuntu) runs typecheck + tests + build, parallel to the existing Swift job.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck`: clean. `npm test`: **15 pass**. `npm run build`: emits.
- Live deploy is **user-side** (Firebase project, `OPENAI_API_KEY` secret, `firebase deploy`) — steps in `backend/README.md`.

## Not in this PR (next)
- **PR‑2:** client `HostedProvider` (calls `llmProxy` with the user's ID token).
- **PR‑3:** Google Sign-In in the macOS app.
- Deferred: billing/RevenueCat, rich quotas, dashboards, multi-provider routing.

author: fujacob
body:
## Summary Adds a `workflow_dispatch` workflow (`republish-pages.yml`) that re-deploys the Sparkle appcast to GitHub Pages with a configurable custom domain input. This lets us change the Pages CNAME (e.g. from `updates.tabbyapp.dev` to a new domain) without cutting a full release. ## Validation Workflow syntax validated — uses the same `configure-pages`, `upload-pages-artifact`, and `deploy-pages` actions as the existing release workflow. Cannot be end-to-end tested until merged to a branch with Actions enabled. ## Linked issues Refs #202 ## Risk / rollout notes - No impact on existing release workflow or appcast content. - The workflow downloads `appcast.xml` from the latest successful release run's artifacts, so at least one prior release must exist. - Custom domain input defaults to `updates.tabbyapp.dev` (current production value).

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a `workflow_dispatch` workflow (`republish-pages.yml`) that re-deploys the Sparkle appcast to GitHub Pages without cutting a new release, useful when the Pages custom domain changes. - The workflow downloads `appcast.xml` from the latest successful `release.yml` run's artifacts, then prepares and deploys a Pages artifact with a configurable CNAME — but two logic bugs mean every run would fail or produce wrong output: the artifact extraction path check looks at `artifacts/appcast.xml` instead of `artifacts/build/appcast.xml` (matching how `upload-artifact` preserves the `build/` prefix), and the subdirectory is named `Cotabby` instead of `tabby` (as used in `release.yml`), which would drop the `/tabby/appcast.xml` path from Pages. - The `inputs.custom_domain` value is also interpolated directly into shell in the Summary step rather than passed via an environment variable.

Confidence Score: 2/5

Not safe to merge as-is — two bugs in the new workflow guarantee it either always errors out or deploys a Pages structure that diverges from every prior release. The artifact path check (`artifacts/appcast.xml`) will never match the actual extracted location (`artifacts/build/appcast.xml`), so the workflow will always exit with an error and never publish. Additionally, the subdirectory name `Cotabby` differs from `tabby` used by the release workflow; if the path check were fixed, running this workflow would still produce a Pages deployment missing the `/tabby/appcast.xml` path that existing release artifacts establish. Both issues are on the sole code path this workflow exercises. .github/workflows/republish-pages.yml — the artifact extraction path and subdirectory name both need correction before this workflow can function correctly.

Security Review

 - **Shell injection via `inputs.custom_domain`** (`.github/workflows/republish-pages.yml`, Summary step): the user-supplied domain input is expanded directly into the shell script by GitHub Actions template substitution before Bash parses it. A value containing shell metacharacters would be executed as code. Risk is bounded to repository collaborators who can trigger `workflow_dispatch`, but the fix (passing the value through an `env:` variable) is straightforward.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | .github/workflows/republish-pages.yml | New manual republish workflow; has two logic bugs (wrong artifact extraction path and mismatched subdirectory name vs release.yml) that would cause every run to fail or produce divergent Pages content, plus a minor shell injection surface in the Summary step. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Operator participant GHA as GitHub Actions participant GHAPI as GitHub API participant Pages as GitHub Pages Operator->>GHA: trigger workflow_dispatch (custom_domain input) GHA->>GHAPI: "gh run list (release.yml, status=success, limit=1)" GHAPI-->>GHA: latest release run ID GHA->>GHAPI: gh run download release-artifacts GHAPI-->>GHA: artifact zip (build/appcast.xml inside) Note over GHA: check artifacts/appcast.xml ❌ actual path: artifacts/build/appcast.xml GHA->>GHA: mkdir pages/Cotabby ⚠️ should be pages/tabby GHA->>GHA: write CNAME with custom_domain GHA->>Pages: configure-pages → upload-pages-artifact → deploy-pages Pages-->>GHA: page_url GHA->>GHA: write GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY ```

body:
## Summary Wires the three read endpoints that back the `/explore` landing page, building on PSY-835's `featured_slots` schema. Anonymous and authenticated callers see identical content (locked decision). - `GET /explore/upcoming-shows` — approved shows with `event_date >= NOW()`, ordered `(event_date ASC, id ASC)` for deterministic offset pagination. **No trending formula, no min_saves threshold, no recently-added fallback** — chronological-only per the locked decision; ranking algorithms remain a separate spike if/when justified. City filter intentionally deferred to PSY-840. - `GET /explore/featured` — currently-active bill + collection from `featured_slots`. Both fields nullable. Defensive read: stale referents (deleted, status-flipped non-approved, privacy-flipped collection) collapse to `null` for that slot rather than 500-ing. - `GET /explore/shuffle-target` — one random artist from the ±90-day qualifying pool. Empty pool returns all-`null` fields with HTTP 200. ### `save_count` — omitted from v1 The ticket called for `save_count` from `show_saves`, but **`show_saves` does not exist** as a table. Shows are saved via the polymorphic `user_bookmarks` table (`entity_type='show', action='save'`). Per the no-speculative-implementation policy, the field is omitted from the v1 response shape (not silently re-keyed to a different table). Follow-up: file a separate ticket once product clarifies whether to surface `user_bookmarks`-derived counts on the /explore tile, and what additional aggregates (going / interested) belong there. Closes PSY-836 ## Test plan - [x] `cd backend && go build ./...` — clean - [x] `cd backend && go generate ./... && git diff --exit-code` — mocks_gen.go is idempotent after re-run - [x] `cd backend && go vet ./...` — clean - [x] `cd backend && go test ./internal/api/handlers/explore/...` — passes (0.40s) - [x] `cd backend && go test ./internal/services/explore/...` — passes (2.81s) - [x] `cd backend && go test ./internal/services/admin/... ./internal/api/handlers/admin/...` — passes (PSY-835 not regressed) - [x] Manual repro on isolated dispatch stack (see below) ### Test coverage Service integration suite (real Postgres testcontainer): - Upcoming Shows: empty, chronological ordering, excludes past, excludes non-approved, deterministic pagination on event_date tie, headliner + venue hydration, limit clamping, offset paginates without overlap. - Featured: empty (both slots nil), populated bill + collection with curator notes, deleted-referent collapses to nil (NOT 500), private-collection excluded, non-approved bill excluded. - Shuffle: empty pool returns nil fields, repeated picks are pool members, non-approved shows are excluded. author: breathesulfur
body: ## Resumo Corrige bug onde a notificação **\"🌙 Título desbloqueado: Caminhante Serena\"** (e demais títulos místicos) aparecia **DUAS vezes** em sequência ao desbloquear. ## Motivação — QA > \"As notificações de títulos estão sendo exibidas em duplicidade. > Ajuste isso e amanhã testo todos os prs no localhost.\" ## Causa raiz \`Dashboard.jsx\` tem um \`useEffect\` que detecta títulos místicos desbloqueáveis e dispara \`notifyAchievement\`: \`\`\`js useEffect(() => { const newTitles = Object.values(MYSTIC_TITLES).filter(t => canUnlockMysticTitle(currentUser, t.id) ) if (newTitles.length === 0) return ... newTitles.forEach((title, i) => { setTimeout(() => notifyAchievement(\`Título desbloqueado: \${title.name}\`...), 300 + i * 600) }) }, [currentUser.essencias_disponiveis]) \`\`\` \`main.jsx\` envolve a árvore em \`\`, que **double-invoca intencionalmente** todos os \`useEffect\` em desenvolvimento para surface side effects. Cada execução agenda seu próprio \`setTimeout\` → notification aparece 2x. (O bônus de marco já tinha defesa via \`processedMilestonesRef\`. Os títulos não.) ## Fix Novo ref \`notifiedTitlesRef\` rastreia IDs de títulos cuja notification já foi disparada. **Idempotência** no effect: \`\`\`diff + const notifiedTitlesRef = useRef(new Set(user.unlockedMysticTitles || [])) useEffect(() => { const newTitles = Object.values(MYSTIC_TITLES).filter(t => - canUnlockMysticTitle(currentUser, t.id) + canUnlockMysticTitle(currentUser, t.id) && + !notifiedTitlesRef.current.has(t.id) ) if (newTitles.length === 0) return + newTitles.forEach(t => notifiedTitlesRef.current.add(t.id)) ... }, [currentUser.essencias_disponiveis]) \`\`\` **Por que funciona:** - Inicializa com títulos já desbloqueados (evita re-notificar após F5) - Marca IDs como notificados ANTES de agendar — na 2ª passagem do StrictMode, o filtro encontra os IDs já no Set e retorna array vazio, sem disparar notifications duplicadas ## Como testar - [x] \`https://inclusivchat-dx07t2ckw-inclusivchat.vercel.app\` - [x] Logar com usuário próximo do threshold de um título (teste.beta@teste.com.br)/(teste@123) (ex.: 30+ essências mas sem \"Caminhante Serena\" (35) desbloqueado) - [x] Ganhar essência via ação (criar post, entrar em grupo) - [x] Ao cruzar o threshold: - Notificação \"🌙 Título desbloqueado: Caminhante Serena\" aparece **uma única vez** - [x] Reproduzir o mesmo para múltiplos títulos cruzados juntos: - Ex.: ganhar essência suficiente para liberar 2 títulos de uma vez - Cada um aparece **uma única vez**, com espaçamento de 600ms entre eles - [x] Após F5 / re-login, títulos JÁ desbloqueados não re-notificam ## Checklist - [x] Build passa (\`npm run build\`) - [x] Mesma estratégia que \`processedMilestonesRef\` (consistente) - [x] Sem regressão: títulos novos continuam sendo notificados normalmente - [x] Testado manualmente no preview ## Arquivos alterados (1) - \`src/components/Dashboard.jsx\` (+13/-1)

author: franciscoparrao
body:
## Summary

- `surtgis hydrology fill-sinks` was silently corrupting reprojected DEMs: NaN-cell curtains (typical of WGS84→UTM rotated grids) blocked drainage paths and left interior valid cells stuck at `f64::MAX / 2.0 ≈ 8.99e307`, contaminating every downstream stage (flow-dir, flow-acc, χ, ksn, knickpoints).
- Fix: NaN/nodata cells now act as drainage exits in the Planchon-Darboux init — interior cells 8-adjacent to a NaN neighbour are initialised to their DEM value. NaN cells themselves are preserved. Matches the `priority_flood` contract.
- Output nodata metadata normalised to `Some(f64::NAN)` regardless of input sentinel.
- `examples/smugglers_notch_validation/` no longer needs the defensive `surtgis clip` step.

## Surfacing

Sprint 7 Smugglers Notch validation against Perron & Royden (2013) — commit `f7da94e`. The workaround was a hard-coded `clip --bbox` step. Now removed; pipeline runs end-to-end on the raw reprojected DEM and produces R² = 0.82 on the main basin (vs 0.82 with the clip).

This is the 6th real-data bug caught by validation against a published workflow (joining #87 vector reprojection, stream-network handler, bps=15 decoder, GeoJSON CRS, and the original sighting of this fill-sinks bug). The CONTRIBUTING.md meta-lesson is now overdue.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p surtgis-algorithms --lib hydrology::fill_sinks` — 8/8 pass (5 existing + 3 new)
- [x] `cargo test -p surtgis-algorithms --lib hydrology` — 82/82 pass
- [x] `cargo check --workspace` — clean
- [x] End-to-end: `bash examples/smugglers_notch_validation/run_validation.sh` (without clip step) — completes, R²=0.8217, zero `inf` or `big_value` cells in `filled.tif`
- [ ] CI green

## What is NOT in scope

- `priority_flood.rs` — already correct
- CLI warning when input has NaN — handled correctly now, warning would be noise
- Refactor / parallelisation of Planchon-Darboux — separate concern
- CONTRIBUTING.md meta-lesson capture — separate PR

author: dickeyf
body:
## What

Host the operator-approved Privacy Policy + Terms of Service (GDPR + Quebec Law 25). Markdown is embedded in the binary and rendered to sanitized HTML behind a public GET /api/v1/legal/{slug}. SPA adds /privacy + /terms pages, footer links, and consent microcopy at the registration entry point. Consent is enforced by Keycloak's TERMS_AND_CONDITIONS required action.

## Why this PR (not PR #301)

PR #301 was closed because the Keycloak auth smoke CI check failed. Root cause: the `TERMS_AND_CONDITIONS` required action was configured with `default_action=true`, which Keycloak applies to **all** users created through the Admin API — including CI seed users. The ROPC (direct-grant) password flow cannot complete a pending required action and returns 400 "Account is not fully set up".

## Fix

- **`terraform/keycloak/dev-seed.sh`**: Added `clear_required_actions()` function that sends `PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{id}` with `{"requiredActions":[]}` after creating each seed user. Idempotent — no-op on re-runs where users already have no pending actions.
- **`.github/workflows/pr.yml`**: The "Default-shaped user" provisioning step now also clears requiredActions for `smoke-default@localhost` after creation.
- **`docs/design/registration-consent.md`**: Documents the bypass rationale — seed/CI users bypass the consent gate intentionally; human self-registrants through the browser flow remain unaffected.
- **`frontend/src/lib/api/openapi.json` + `schema.d.ts`**: Regenerated to include both the legal endpoint (this PR) and the account deletion endpoint (already merged in #304).

## Acceptance criteria (from bead mi-97kr)

- [x] `/privacy` and `/terms` pages render the approved markdown, reachable from footer + signup
- [x] Registration surfaces ToS+Privacy consent (Keycloak TERMS_AND_CONDITIONS required action as default action)  
- [x] Keycloak auth smoke passes (seed/CI users bypass the required action)
- [x] No PII/secrets added

author: vyntechs
body:
## Why

You're posting on social media right now, traffic is incoming, and four agents just finished auditing the codebase. Headline: no committed secrets, no SQL injection, no XSS — but there were 4 Tier-1 issues a stranger could hit from the open internet. This PR closes 3 of them. The 4th (curator role scoping) is **deliberately deferred** — see below.

**Not merging.** Standing rule: you validate, you merge.

## What's in the PR

### 1. Rate limiting on the expensive LLM endpoints

`/api/sessions` and `/api/intake/submit` each fire Anthropic + Voyage + Tavily + 6 retrieval adapters on every call. An authenticated user in a tight `curl` loop could drain API budgets in hours.

- New migration `drizzle/migrations/0017_rate_limit_buckets.sql` — a tiny 3-column table.
- New helper `lib/rate-limit.ts` — fixed-window per-minute counter. Single Postgres upsert per check; `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` with a `CASE` that either increments the current window or rolls over to a fresh one. One DB round-trip.
- Wired into both routes at the **same** key (`intake:<userId>`) so an attacker can't double their burn by alternating endpoints. Cap: 10/min — real techs create 1–3 sessions/hour.

**Why Postgres, not Upstash/Vercel KV:** lowest merge risk. No new vendor signup. No new env vars. No new package. Runs in the existing pglite test harness so every test that uses `createTestDb` already covers the new table.

### 2. Artifact extraction IDOR (`/api/artifacts/[id]/extract`)

Before this PR, the route auth-checked and paywall-checked the caller but did **no ownership check**. Any logged-in user could `POST /api/artifacts/<some-uuid>/extract` and trigger vision extraction on another tenant's photo.

After: load the artifact → load its session → load the caller's profile → require `session.shopId === profile.shopId`. Returns **404 (not 403)** on every failure path so the endpoint can't be used to probe artifact existence.

### 3. `/api/health` reconnaissance leak

Before:
```json
{ "nodeEnv": "...", "databaseUrlHost": "...", "databaseUrlDirectHost": "...",
  "supabaseUrl": "...", "voyageKeyPresent": true, "anthropicKeyPresent": true,
  "pingOk": true, "pingError": null }
```

After:
```json
{ "ok": true }   // or { "ok": false } with status 503
```

Liveness checks still work. Reconnaissance gets nothing.

## What I deferred and why

**Tier 1 #3 — Curator role scoping.** The audit flagged that `canCurate` grants curator access to any `role === 'owner'` profile, with no shop scoping — so a new shop's owner could see every other shop's curator queue. The simple "founder-only" fix is a 1-line change, BUT:

- There are **two conflicting tests already shipped on `main`**:
  - `tests/unit/curator-role-gate.test.ts:65` asserts non-founder owners SHOULD have curator access ("Mac and Angel both run as Admins of their shops and curate alongside Brandon").
  - `tests/unit/calibration-manual-trigger.test.ts:88` asserts they SHOULD NOT ("PR 6 tightening: role==='owner' alone no longer grants curator access"). This is the test that's been failing on `main` since I noticed it during PR #92.
- Locking to founder-only would break Mac and Angel's day-to-day access — that's a product decision, not just a security fix. You said "low merge risk."
- The actual exposure today is "any new shop owner gets curator." That's next-month risk, not tonight-traffic risk.

Coming back to you separately with three options: (a) explicit `is_curator` flag column with Mac & Angel seeded, (b) hardcoded email allowlist, (c) founder-only with manual promotion tool to follow.

## What was clean

- No committed secrets in the repo. `.env` is in `.gitignore`, `.env.example` has no real values.
- No `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` leaking sensitive keys.
- All Drizzle queries are properly parameterized — no SQL injection.
- React handles XSS — no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere in the active surface.
- Existing security headers (X-Frame-Options, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy) are good. CSP and Permissions-Policy still missing — they're in Tier 2.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/rate-limit.test.ts tests/unit/artifact-extract-route.test.ts tests/unit/health-route.test.ts` — **10/10 pass**.
- `pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/intake-submit-route.test.ts tests/unit/intake-submit-pick-existing.test.ts tests/unit/intake-submit-tech-id.test.ts` — **17/17 pass** (the route tests for the endpoints we changed).
- Full suite running in the background; will push a follow-up commit if any regression surfaces.

## Manual test plan

- [ ] Apply the migration on prod (`drizzle-kit migrate`) before merging — the `rate_limit_buckets` table must exist or both intake routes will start 500ing.
- [ ] Hit `/api/health` while signed out — confirm response is exactly `{"ok":true}`.
- [ ] As a normal tech, create a real session via the app — should work.
- [ ] As an attacker (Postman, any signed-in user), `POST /api/sessions` 11 times in a minute — eleventh should return 429 with a `Retry-After` header.
- [ ] As a different shop's tech, try `POST /api/artifacts/<other-shop-artifact-id>/extract` — must return 404.

## Tier 2 / 3 still open

Tier 2 (CSP header, Permissions-Policy, Stripe webhook replay protection, rate-limit team invite, founder email timing-safe) and Tier 3 (open-redirect tightening, magic-byte file validation, Supabase storage RLS check, HSTS preload) are queued for follow-up PRs once you've validated this one.

author: copilot
body:
Windows CMake configure was failing in CI because the workflow forced `cl` via `CMAKE_C{,XX}_COMPILER` while using Ninja, leaving CMake unable to identify the compiler in that job context. This change moves Windows to a native MSVC configure path and keeps existing Ninja behavior for non-Windows targets.

- **Problem scope**
  - Windows MSVC matrix entry depended on explicit `cl` injection (`cc/cxx`) plus `-G "Ninja"`, which is brittle in GitHub Actions.
  - Configure fallback reran CMake without correcting compiler/generator selection.

- **Workflow changes**
  - Removed `cc: cl` and `cxx: cl` from the Windows matrix config.
  - Split configure into OS-specific steps:
    - **Windows**: `Visual Studio 17 2022` generator with `-A x64`.
    - **Non-Windows**: unchanged intent—explicit `CC/CXX` and `CMAKE_C{,XX}_COMPILER` with `Ninja`.
  - Eliminated the prior failure-based fallback configure path.

- **Resulting behavior**
  - Windows now lets CMake resolve MSVC through the Visual Studio generator instead of requiring `cl` resolution from the shell environment.
  - Linux/macOS compiler selection remains explicit and matrix-driven.

```yaml
- name: Configure CMake (Windows)
  if: runner.os == 'Windows'
  run: >
    cmake -B build
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=${{ matrix.config.build_type }}
    -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"
    -A x64
```

💡 **What:** Eliminated an inefficient iteration over all checkpoints in `DebtSummary.tsx` to find the latest account balances, instead leveraging pre-computed `startingBalance` data from `result.accountSummaries`.

🎯 **Why:** Scanning over thousands of mock checkpoints on every re-render is an unnecessary overhead. Using the already mapped `accountSummaries` drops the complexity to O(A) where A is the number of accounts. This solves the "Redundant loop for finding latest checkpoint in DebtSummary" issue.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
Using a benchmark test with 100 iterations on 100 accounts & 5,000 checkpoints:
* Baseline render time: ~426ms
* Improved render time: ~10ms
* Change: ~42x faster execution for this component.

author: adamtday
body:
## Summary

First test of the Phase 2.5 reference-ingestion workflow against real sources. Twenty references ingested across the target source list, four deep cluster analyses extracted, `visual_reference_analysis.md` updated with cross-links and recurring cross-cluster mechanisms. The workflow held; two sources were blocked at fetch and are logged as founder-capture-pending stubs without fabrication.

## Workflow validation outcome

The five-stage workflow (capture, attribute, classify, link, review) survived first contact with real-source load. Specifically:

- **Capture stage** worked for 18 of 20 sources via WebFetch. Two sources (Cercle Odyssey, Pitchfork) blocked at the network or CDN layer; logged as pending-capture stubs with founder-capture briefs. The workflow's pending-capture discipline is the right behaviour and is now documented in practice.
- **Attribute stage** held: every companion `.md` carries full attribution (source, creator, URL, date captured, capture context, license considerations).
- **Classify stage** held: every companion `.md` carries primary category, secondary categories, and reference class. Multi-category tagging worked cleanly.
- **Link stage** held: every companion `.md` cross-links to canonical anchors via `related:` frontmatter and the relationship-to-canonical-thesis field.
- **Review stage** is the founder's. Companion files at `status: draft` are reviewable; cluster analyses at `status: draft` are reviewable.

The biggest workflow gap surfaced: WebFetch cannot capture screenshot binaries from a headless sandbox environment. Every companion `.md` documents this honestly with `screenshot_binaries_pending: true`; binaries are a manual founder-capture step. The analysis content does not depend on the binaries to be valid.

## Files created

### Per-reference companion files (20 total)

**`10_source_material/references/visual_references/crossover_aesthetic/`** (9 files)
- Apple Vision Pro marketing page
- Apple AirPods Max marketing page
- Apple MacBook Pro marketing page
- Apple TV+ marketing page
- Netflix Tudum homepage
- Teenage Engineering homepage
- Teenage Engineering EP-133 product page
- Cirque du Soleil homepage
- Cirque du Soleil O show page

**`10_source_material/references/visual_references/scene_credible_electronic/`** (8 files)
- Resident Advisor homepage
- RA Magazine
- RA Reviews
- RA Podcast
- Cercle homepage
- Boiler Room homepage
- Cercle Odyssey (pending capture stub)
- Pitchfork (pending capture stub)

**`10_source_material/references/visual_references/prestige_unscripted/`** (3 files)
- Formula 1 homepage
- Formula 1 drivers page
- Box to Box Films homepage

### Deep cluster analyses (4 total)

| Cluster | File | Mechanisms extracted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Apple Marketing Pages | `04_competitive_landscape/references/apple_marketing_pages.md` | held-then-reveal scroll pacing; single-display-family typography; restraint as confidence; depth-on-demand interaction; partnership-as-credibility |
| Resident Advisor | `04_competitive_landscape/references/resident_advisor.md` | assumed-knowledge editorial voice; location-as-first-class entity; parallel-pillar information architecture; archive-as-asset |
| Cercle Platform | `04_competitive_landscape/references/cercle_platform.md` | experience-type taxonomy; artistic-movement positioning; single-image-per-card register; cinematic-format-earned authority |
| Formula 1 Editorial Ecosystem | `04_competitive_landscape/references/formula1_editorial.md` | result-as-hero; verbatim-cast-quote headlines; roster-as-permanent-page; partnership-as-credibility; work-as-credential |

### Updates

- `04_competitive_landscape/visual_reference_analysis.md`: added Phase 2.5 Ingestion Sprint Additions section enumerating all new references plus six recurring cross-cluster mechanisms. Updated frontmatter (related-files, retrieval-tags) and Change Log.

## Strongest cross-cluster mechanisms

Reading the four cluster analyses together surfaces six mechanisms that recur across reference families and warrant codification in subsequent brand-world or website-strategy work:

1. **Result-as-hero / cycle-as-hero pacing.** Home page resets at the latest meaningful event; calm between events.
2. **Verbatim-cast-quote editorial voice.** The cast carries the headline language; marketing voice stays invisible.
3. **Single-image-per-card brand register.** Single defining image per card across navigation systems.
4. **Restraint at the brand-world layer; motion lives in the experiences.** The brand surface is calm; the work itself carries the motion.
5. **Partnership-as-credibility framing.** Named partnerships do credibility work that copy cannot.
6. **Work-as-credential discipline.** The work itself is the credibility signal; copy explains it minimally.

These should inform future iterations of `07_brand_world/visual_principles.md` and `07_brand_world/visual_positioning.md`.

## Honest gaps and unresolved items

- **Screenshot binaries** for all 18 captured references are pending founder manual capture. The companion `.md` content is grounded in direct WebFetch observation and does not depend on binaries to be valid, but the curated reference assets are incomplete until binaries land.
- **Cercle Odyssey** is the most strategically interesting single source in the sprint and could not be captured. Founder capture from a desktop browser is required; the stub at `20260525_cercle_odyssey_pending_capture.md` carries the capture brief.
- **Pitchfork** is blocked at the CDN layer; the editorial-publication-architecture analysis remains partial until founder capture lands.
- **Drive to Survive proper** is paywalled on Netflix; this sprint captures the parent brand world (F1, Box to Box) instead. The existing `04_competitive_landscape/drive_to_survive.md` carries the DTS-specific analysis.
- **The eighteen captured references represent 50-60% of the strategically useful source set** for the surfaces the user named. Subsequent ingestion sprints should add: Tomorrowland and Awakenings (festival visual language), label visual identities (Hyperdub, Warp, KNTXT, Drumcode), club identities (Berghain, fabric), additional Cercle properties (Festival, MOMENT, RECORDS), additional RA surfaces (Festival, Exchange, Tickets).

## Recommendations

1. **Founder capture pass.** Manually capture screenshot binaries for the 18 fetched references plus the 2 pending stubs from a desktop browser. Aim for 4-6 frames per reference covering hero, mid-page, footer, and any interaction sequences. Drop binaries into the same paths as the companion `.md` files; the existing companion files reference expected filenames.
2. **Cluster-analysis review.** Founder reviews the four cluster analyses against the cross-cluster-mechanism observations. Confirm which mechanisms become inputs to `07_brand_world/visual_principles.md` audit dimensions.
3. **Workflow refinement.** Two practical workflow gaps surfaced and should be addressed before the next ingestion sprint:
   - Browser-extension or manual capture tooling for screenshot binaries.
   - Fallback capture method for CDN-blocked sources (likely manual founder capture).
4. **Next sprint scope.** Festival visual identities (Tomorrowland, Awakenings, Time Warp), label visual identities, club identities, and the additional Cercle and RA surfaces.

## Discipline preserved

- Em dashes: zero across all sprint files (verified after a targeted fix pass; 6 em-dashes originated in WebFetch-quoted text and were converted to semicolons or restructured).
- Source-vs-output separation: companion files in `10_source_material/`; cluster analyses in `04_competitive_landscape/references/`; `visual_principles.md` and other brand-world files unchanged.
- Honest capture discipline: blocked sources logged as pending-capture stubs, never fabricated.
- No screenshot binaries fabricated.
- Founder thesis untouched.
- No new meta-framework files introduced (per explicit user direction: "no more new me

author: copilot
body:
The Aegis 150 upgrade left one gap in lane-based dispatch: background workers could still consider premium-agent tasks when `freeModelOnlyMode` was disabled. This change aligns runtime behavior with the active Aegis policy and removes a few lingering governance ambiguities in the docs.

- **Dispatch policy enforcement**
  - Updated `scripts/orchestrator/dispatch-lane.ps1` so lane workers only claim tasks assigned to agents in `modelRouting.freePlanningAgents`.
  - This makes background dispatch consistent with the Aegis 150 contract: free workers stay free-only regardless of the policy warning mode.

- **Queue mutation hardening**
  - Switched lane dispatch task stamping to `Add-Member -Force` for `startedAt`, `attempts`, and `claimedBy`.
  - This avoids failures when queue entries are incomplete or missing optional runtime fields.

- **Governance clarity**
  - Updated `plans/CUSTOM_AGENTS_PLAN.md` header/status to reflect Aegis 150 as the active baseline.
  - Added a short note in `AGENTS.md` clarifying that the older V3 sections are retained as legacy detail and do not override active Aegis 150 policy.

```powershell
$eligible = $tasks | Where-Object {
  ($_.status -eq "queued" -or $_.status -eq "retrying") -and
  ($lane -eq "any" -or $_.lane -eq $lane) -and
  (Test-IsFreePlanningAgent -Policy $policy -AgentName $_.agent)
}
```

## Summary

Small infrastructure PR — first step of Path A2 (wire-in 170 coverage candidates with verified SIS URLs). The refingerprint sweep was throwing away the most actionable field on `FingerprintResult`: the specific course-search URL the probe actually hit.

## Why this matters

The 170 wire-in candidates from [PR #532](../../pull/532) need the specific SIS URL per college to actually plug into existing `scripts/{state}/scrape-{platform}.ts` files. The conventional `selfservice.<rootdomain>` pattern works for some but **fails for many**:

| College | Marketing host | Actual SIS URL |
|---|---|---|
| Central Ohio Technical | `cotc.edu` | `https://self-service.cotc.edu:8183/Student/courses` (hyphen, port 8183, lowercase) |
| Washington State CC Ohio | `wscc.edu` | `https://selfservice.wsco.edu/Student/Courses` (different root domain) |
| Fresno City | `fresnocitycollege.edu` | `https://selfservice.scccd.edu/Student/Courses` (system-wide) |

Without the persisted `courseSearchUrl`, every wire-in would be a guess. With it, wire-ins become deterministic: read the field, paste into the scraper's `HOSTS` map.

## Two files changed

- **`scripts/lib/refingerprint-sweep.ts`** — `CollegeEntry` interface gains `courseSearchUrl: string | null`. Both success and error paths set it explicitly.
- **`scripts/lib/coverage-expansion.ts`** — `BaselineEntry` mirrors the field as optional (`courseSearchUrl?: string | null`). Optional so we don't break reads of older baselines that lack it.

## What this does NOT do

- **Doesn't re-run refingerprint** to backfill the existing baseline. That's a manual re-run after merge (~25 min local).
- **Doesn't change the coverage-expansion rolling issue body.** The field is now in the JSON output, but markdown table rendering can be a follow-up. The immediate consumer is the wire-in workflow.

## Next steps after merge

1. Re-run refingerprint locally — re-fingerprints all 652 colleges to capture `courseSearchUrl` for each, ~25 min wall time
2. Commit the refreshed baseline (separate small PR)
3. Bulk wire-ins per (state, platform) cluster — 18 PRs each adding verified SIS URLs to the existing scraper's `HOSTS` map

- [ ] Smoke test in this PR already verified: fingerprint on `cotc.edu` returns `courseSearchUrl: https://self-service.cotc.edu:8183/Student/courses`. Pre-fix that field was discarded; post-fix it persists into the baseline.

author: phaware-artie
body:
## Problem

The merge processor's automated "review-fix" dispatch failed with `exit 4: MR missing review_pr field`. `gt refinery pr create` opened the PR but never recorded the PR number (`review_pr`) onto the merge-request bead, so the later `dispatch-review-fix` step — which reads `review_pr` from that bead to know which PR to act on — had nothing to read and bailed out.

This is the second of two breakages in the automated review-fix loop (the first, the sling-parser exit-1, was `gt-o4z`). Until both land, a human has to hand-patch `review_pr` onto the bead for every reviewer-flagged PR (done on #74, #77, #78, #79, and #12).

## Solution

- `gt refinery pr create` gains an `--mr <bead-id>` flag. When given, after the PR is opened it persists the PR number as `review_pr` onto the MR bead (new `writeReviewPRToMR`, backed by a `SetMRFields`-style helper in `internal/beads/fields.go`). Re-running is idempotent — it rewrites the same `review_pr`.
- The refinery patrol formula (`mol-refinery-patrol.formula.toml`) is updated to pass `--mr` at PR-create time so the field is populated automatically.
- Failure to persist `review_pr` is surfaced as an error rather than swallowed.

Together with `gt-o4z`, this fully restores automated `dispatch-review-fix` (no more manual `review_pr` patching).

## Test plan

- [ ] `go test ./internal/beads/ ./internal/formula/` (verified green — includes the new `fields` round-trip tests and the PR-workflow integration test).
- [ ] `go test ./internal/cmd/ -run 'TestReviewFixSlingArgs|TestExtractDescField|TestPolecatNameFromAssignee'` (verified green).
- [ ] End-to-end: `gt refinery pr create --mr <id> ...` writes `review_pr` to the bead; `dispatch-review-fix` no longer exits 4.

Note: a full `go test ./internal/cmd/` fails on this macOS host with the "SIGKILL unsigned binaries — use `make build`" harness constraint for tests that exec the built binary; unrelated to this change.

author: jmonsalverivero-ai
body:
## Problem

When Claude.app spawns `gbrain serve` from `claude_desktop_config.json` AND
its claude-code-spawn child sessions also pass `--mcp-config '...gbrain
serve...'`, each invocation tries to acquire the same PGLite lock. PGLite
is single-process-per-data-dir, so the losers die on contention and their
MCP clients end up without `mcp__gbrain__*` tools.

Real-world impact (this PR's origin): Claude.app's main chat window has
gbrain working, but every claude-code-spawn child session opened from
inside the app has no gbrain tools — even though gbrain is "configured"
there via `--mcp-config`.

## Solution — fan-in over a Unix socket

The first `gbrain serve` to win the lock becomes the **owner** and also
listens on a Unix socket alongside the lock dir. Subsequent `gbrain serve`
invocations detect the lock-held-by-another-serve condition via the new
`readLockInfo()` helper, and become **stdio proxies** that bidi-pipe their
stdin/stdout to the owner's socket. Each proxied client lands as a
per-connection MCP `Server` on the owner side, sharing the single PGLite
engine.

```
Owner process (first serve):
  - StdioServerTransport on real stdin/stdout (primary client)
  - net.createServer at <dataDir>/.gbrain-lock/serve.sock
    → per-connection: new Server() + StdioServerTransport(socket, socket)

Proxy process (every subsequent serve):
  - readLockInfo() + process.kill(pid, 0) detect lock-by-live-serve
  - runProxy() bidi-pipes stdin/socket/stdout (no JSON-RPC parsing)
```

**Trust boundary preserved verbatim**: the proxy does pure byte forwarding
(can't modify messages even if it wanted to), and the owner's
per-connection `Server` uses the existing `startMcpServerWithTransport`
that always dispatches with `remote: true`.

## Commits (5)

- `feat(pglite): preventive concurrent-process detection in connect()` —
  surfaces a clear error on collision instead of letting PGLite corrupt
  itself with a second WASM connection.
- `feat(pglite): expose dataDir + readLockInfo helper` — two read-only
  helpers downstream consumers need.
- `refactor(mcp): pluggable transport in startMcpServer + drop duplicate
  shutdown` — extracts `startMcpServerWithTransport`; removes a shutdown
  handler that raced with `installStdioLifecycle` (manifested as `PGlite
  is closing` cleanup errors on `stdin-end`).
- `feat(serve): multi-client MCP via Unix socket multiplexer + stdio proxy` —
  the feature: `multiplexer.ts` + `proxy.ts` + wire in `serve.ts` +
  pre-connect branch in `cli.ts`.
- `test(serve-proxy): roundtrip, multi-client, stale socket, readLockInfo` —
  9 tests / 26 expects covering happy path + multi-client concurrency +
  stale-socket recovery + helper edge cases. R3+R4 isolation compliant.

## Validation

- `bun run verify` clean (19 checks + typecheck)
- `bun test test/serve-proxy.test.ts` — 9/9 pass
- Smoke test against `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite` with two real `gbrain serve`
  processes: owner accepts proxy on socket, proxy forwards `initialize`,
  owner returns valid `serverInfo` JSON-RPC result, both clean shutdown
  via SIGTERM with no zombie lock.
- Live in production locally: Claude.app's main chat + the authoring
  claude-code-spawn session both have working `mcp__gbrain__*` tools
  through the multiplexer right now.

## Test plan

- [ ] Reviewer reproduces lock-collision pre-patch: open Claude.app, open
      a claude-code-spawn child session, observe missing `mcp__gbrain__*`
      tools and `Cannot open PGLite database` errors in
      `~/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp-server-gbrain.log`.
- [ ] Apply this branch, restart Claude.app so it relaunches `gbrain
      serve` with the new code, open a claude-code-spawn child session,
      observe `mcp__gbrain__*` works in BOTH places.
- [ ] `bun test test/serve-proxy.test.ts` passes locally.
- [ ] `bun run verify` clean.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- `serve --http` unaffected — HTTP supports multi-client natively.
- Owner-crash recovery: proxies currently exit on socket close; their
  parent MCP client retries and a new owner is elected by `acquireLock`'s
  atomic `mkdir`. "Convert me to owner" in-place inside the proxy would
  avoid the parent-reconnect round-trip but doubles complexity for
  marginal gain.
- Per-connection metrics on the multiplexer.

body:
## Summary

Remove duplicated default background `xtask test` argument serialization and route it through the shared `nextest_invocation_args` helper.

## Problem

The default background test path had its own flag serialization block separate from `nextest_invocation_args`. That drift caused the `--no-reuse --bg` bypass leak fixed in #1478: semantic args included the bypass, but spawn args did not, and the coordinator checks spawn args before deciding whether fresh reuse is allowed.

Keeping two serializers means every future test flag can repeat the same bug.

## Solution

The default background nextest branch now calls `self.nextest_invocation_args(false)`. The helper now includes non-balanced `--impact-mode` as well as reuse and selection flags, so background child args and the normal nested/foreground serializer share one path.

A focused regression pins that the shared path carries `--no-reuse`, `--impact-mode=aggressive`, package scope, and test filter flags.

## Summary
- Client-side caching of the parsed `publicKey` in `passkey_controller.js` broke the server's single-use nonce semantics: `WebauthnPendingStore` mints a fresh nonce on every `/session/options` and consumes it on every `/session/verify`. Reusing a cached `publicKey` after any prior `/verify` (success redirect, error state, or a conditional-mediation ceremony that already burned the nonce) produced "No login in progress" on the next attempt.
- Always re-POST `/session/options` for each ceremony attempt — the cost is sub-100ms and matches the server's single-use semantics.

Cherry-picked from a feature branch where it sat alongside unrelated permissions/groups work; sending it on its own so it can land independently.

- [ ] Trigger conditional mediation, then click sign-in button — second ceremony succeeds (previously failed with "No login in progress")

- **BuddyTab**: Hub showing buddy status, evolution progress, trophies, and entry points to battle and shop
- **BuddyBattle**: Turn-based word-matching battle system where correct answers damage monsters; critical hits trigger when the picked word is already mastered
- **BuddySprite**: Original inline SVG buddy designs (four species × four evolution stages) that visibly grow as mastery increases
- **MunchToMaster**: Multi-tap feed interaction triggered when a word is newly mastered; plays rising-pitch chomps and celebrates with sparkles
- **EvolutionCelebration**: Full-screen celebration when buddy crosses an evolution threshold
- **BuddyShop**: Cosmetic-only shop where trophies purchase hats and auras (word learning is never gated)
- **StarterSelect**: Initial species picker shown on first buddy setup

### New Data & Utilities
- **data/buddies.js**: Four original creature species (Spark, Ember, Splash, Sprout) with four evolution stages each, element definitions, and stage thresholds
- **data/cosmetics.js**: Cosmetic catalog (hats, auras) with costs and metadata
- **utils/buddy.js**: Pure selectors for buddy state (knownWords, masteredCount, isCriticalHit, evolutionStage, currentLearningSet, pickBattleRound)
- **utils/buddyStorage.js**: Per-kid localStorage persistence for buddy state
- **utils/buddySfx.js**: Lightweight WebAudio synthesis for chomps (rising pitch crescendo), chimes, and battle SFX; respects mute state and iOS audio unlock requirements
- **buddy.test.js**: Comprehensive test suite for buddy selectors and state invariants

### Integration Points
- **App.jsx**: Wires buddy reducer, loads/saves buddy state per kid, detects newly-mastered words and triggers feed/evolution overlays, manages pending evolution state
- **BottomNav.jsx**: Adds "Buddy" tab (🐾) to main navigation

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Invariant**: A buddy's known words are always exactly the set of mastered words in progress.mastered—never stored separately, preventing drift
- **Critical Hits**: When a word already in the buddy's vocabulary is correctly matched in battle, it deals extra damage (1 + bonus) and plays a special sound
- **Battle Rounds**: Reuse the same matching contract as FindItGame (target + 3 distractors) via shared selectors; dispatch MARK_CORRECT/MARK_WRONG to progress
- **Trophies**: Earned only in battle (2 per monster defeated, +1 for critical hits); purely cosmetic currency, never gates learning
- **Audio**: WebAudio synthesis with envelope control; unlocked on first user gesture for iOS Safari compatibility; fully mutable
- **Sprite Scaling**: Buddy size and visual features grow with evolution stage (e.g., Spark gains bolts at stage 2, crown at stage 3)
- **Persistence**: Buddy state (starter, trophies, cosmetics, pending feeds) saved per kid to localStorage; evolution state tracked to avoid replaying past celebrations

body:
Port `shdeps` to Rust while preserving the existing CLI and Bash compatibility surface.

Summary

This branch replaces the runtime implementation with a Rust binary and keeps the current `shdeps` command line contract intact. The Bash implementation is preserved as `shdeps-legacy.sh` for parity tests and reference behavior, while `shdeps.sh` becomes the sourceable compatibility wrapper that delegates mutating helper APIs to the Rust binary.

Key points:
- preserves the existing CLI commands, exit codes, output shapes, hook ABI, config parsing, manifest/stamp state, and install/prune behavior
- keeps method-transition cleanup ownership-aware, with the explicit `pkg` exception that clears shdeps tracking without uninstalling system packages
- adds Rust API modules with documented boundaries for config, runtime roots, dependency paths, update, prune, status, release installs, and self-update
- adds release archive packaging and smoke tests modeled on the shared Rust release workflow platforms: `linux-x86_64-musl`, `linux-aarch64-musl`, `macos-x86_64`, and `macos-aarch64`
- adds installer migration paths for source checkouts, bundled release archives, and curl-pipe installs, including private release asset credentials via `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`gh auth token`

Performance

Benchmarked locally with `target/release/shdeps` against the preserved Bash CLI using isolated fixtures:
- `version`: Rust 0.64 ms vs Bash 18.9 ms
- `dep-file` across 201 configured deps: Rust 3.4 ms vs Bash 157 ms
- warm `check` for a manifest-backed cargo dep: Rust 24.1 ms vs Bash 130.9 ms
- warm no-op `update --quiet` across 100 cargo deps: Rust 8.3 ms vs Bash 2.34 s

Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo build --release --locked`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D missing-docs' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`

- `SHDEPS_RUST_CLI=target/debug/shdeps ./test/shdeps-wrapper-test`
- `scripts/package-release.sh x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu linux-x86_64-gnu-local`

body:
## Summary

Per CC2's PR #910 risk note: \`callAutonomicReward\` is fire-and-forget
and swallows transport errors, so wrong URL / wrong payload keys /
wrong Content-Type silent failures show up only as a deferred
\`logger.warn\` line in production. This test pins the request shape
the Python handler expects.

Catches:
- Path drift (must be \`/monkey/autonomic/reward\`)
- camelCase leakage in payload (Python uses snake_case: \`instance_id\`,
  \`realized_pnl_usdt\`, \`margin_usdt\`, \`kappa_at_exit\`)
- Missing \`Content-Type: application/json\` (FastAPI won't parse without)
- Optional-field encoding (\`symbol\` / \`kappaAtExit\` undefined → safe)
- Fire-and-forget invariant on non-2xx and network errors

Does NOT replace organic close-event verification (that requires
wall-clock + a real close), but it catches the most common
boundary-failure shapes before they ship.

## Test plan

- [x] \`yarn vitest run autonomicRewardBoundary\` — 6 passed
- [ ] CI green on the PR

author: joemooney
body:
**Architecture doc:** [`docs/aida/2026-05-25-claude-charts-arch.md`](docs/aida/2026-05-25-claude-charts-arch.md)
**Screenshots:** [`docs/aida/2026-05-25-claude-charts-screenshots/`](docs/aida/2026-05-25-claude-charts-screenshots/) — 5 charts × 2 substrates = 10 SVGs

## Summary

End-to-end agile-metrics charting for aida-chat. Five hand-crafted SVG charts ported from `aida-web-react`: status distribution (donut), sprint burn-down, sprint burn-up, velocity, feature progress. Charts render inline in chat responses when the model invokes `chart_status` / `chart_sprint` / `chart_feature`. Backend reads `.aida-store/objects/**/*.yaml` directly (richer than `aida list --json` — gives us `history`, `relationships`, `custom_fields`); algorithms ported 1:1 from `sprint-utils.ts`; SVG generators render to a dark-theme-native palette via `var(--text)` / `var(--accent)` / `var(--bg)`. Renders against both aida-chat's own substrate AND aida core's substrate without code changes — verified by running `charts_smoke` against both.

## Rendering surface (option 1: server-side SVG)

```
chart tool ──► reads YAML ──► computes data ──► renders SVG ──► returns:
                                                                  • summary text (to model)
                                                                  • Vec<ChartArtifact> (out-of-band)
                                                                                       │
                            anthropic loop ──► AgentEvent::ChartArtifact ──► SSE event:chart ──► browser
                                          └──► persists into ChatTurn.chart_artifacts (for /history)
```

Token-efficient: model sees only the summary text; the SVG bytes never round-trip through the LLM.

## Time-series investigation finding

True burn-down works — `.aida-store/objects/**/*.yaml` already contains per-item `history` arrays with status-change journals. `computeBurndownData` ports verbatim from sprint-utils.ts. **No fallback synthesis required.** Falls back to `modified_at` only for items that were `Completed` before AIDA started journaling (matches React reference). Full investigation + future-work hook in the architecture doc §2.

## Acceptance evidence

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| All V1 charts render against aida-chat's own substrate | `AIDA_CHAT_REPO_ROOT=/home/joe/ai/aida-chat cargo run --example charts_smoke` produces 5 SVGs; sprint-based charts hit empty-state branches gracefully (no sprints in this substrate) |
| All V1 charts render against aida core's substrate | `AIDA_CHAT_REPO_ROOT=/home/joe/ai/aida cargo run --example charts_smoke` produces 5 populated SVGs across 1463 reqs, SPRINT-3, 140 features |
| Dark-theme consistency | All SVGs use `var(--text-dim)` / `var(--text)` / `var(--accent)` / `var(--bg)` with hex fallbacks; zero foreign tokens |
| Empty states render gracefully | Every chart has an explicit empty branch with a dashed-border placeholder + muted italic message (see `burndown-aida-chat.svg`, `burnup-aida-chat.svg`, `velocity-aida-chat.svg` in the screenshots) |
| `cargo test --features ssr --lib` green | 57/57 pass — 36 baseline + 21 new (4 store + 7 data + 9 svg + 1 tool integration) |
| ssr + hydrate + cargo leptos builds clean | All three green |
| `cargo run --example charts_smoke` works | Runs end-to-end; reports `→ loaded N requirements` and `✓` per chart |

## Self-evaluation against the 6 brief criteria

| # | Criterion | Stars | Justification |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visual quality | ★★★★☆ | Polished dark-theme native, proper SVG arc math for donut, gridlines at right opacity, muted empty-states. Nit: rounded line caps on bars not yet matched to React |
| 2 | Code quality | ★★★★★ | 57 tests including real-fixture YAML parse smoke. Pure-Rust SVG (no HTML-escape leak). Clean store → data → svg → tool → SSE → UI separation |
| 3 | Faithfulness to aida-web-react | ★★★★★ | Algorithms ported verbatim with source function names preserved (`computeBurndownData`, `computeBurnupData`, etc.). React colors identical. One unavoidable divergence (sprint-membership direction) supports BOTH directions |
| 4 | Investigation depth | ★★★★★ | True burn-down landed via history journals (not a fallback). Sprint-membership direction discovered and handled bidirectionally. AIDA-core MCP-enhancement future-work hook documented |
| 5 | Brief discipline | ★★★★★ | All 5 V1 charts shipped, both substrate targets verified, empty states everywhere, ssr + hydrate + cargo leptos green, smoke example works end-to-end. Backend tools + SSE + frontend + history persistence all in |
| 6 | Trace discipline | ★★★★★ | Every new file has `// trace:EPIC-29 \| ai:claude`. Inline markers at every cross-cutting touchpoint (SSE event, ChatTurn field, system prompt) |

**One thing I'd do with another night:** Scale the donut center label with the legend density — at 7+ segments the fixed 22px feels visually weak. ~30min of design polish.

## Diff at a glance

- New module `src/server/charts/` (~1320 LOC): store + data + svg
- New tools module `src/server/tools/charts.rs` (~270 LOC): three chart tools
- Backend wiring: `AgentEvent::ChartArtifact`, SSE event `chart`, `ChatTurn.chart_artifacts` persistence
- Frontend: `<ChartArtifactView>` component, `live_charts` signal, SSE listener
- `examples/charts_smoke.rs` for end-to-end testing
- 10 screenshots demonstrating both substrate targets

## Test plan

- [ ] Pull this branch, `AIDA_CHAT_REPO_ROOT=/home/joe/ai/aida cargo leptos serve`, ask the model "show me the status breakdown" — confirm a status donut renders inline
- [ ] Same session, ask "what's the sprint progress" — confirm 3 charts (burn-down + burn-up + velocity) render in a stack
- [ ] Switch `AIDA_CHAT_REPO_ROOT` to aida-chat's own root, restart, repeat — confirm sprint charts show empty states instead of crashing
- [ ] Reload page mid-conversation — confirm chart artifacts persist via `/history`
- [ ] Open the SVGs in `docs/aida/2026-05-25-claude-charts-screenshots/` directly in a browser to compare aida core vs aida-chat output side-by-side

author: rsasaki0109
body:
## Summary

GPU 3D pose-graph SLAM with **dynamic switchable constraints**. This is the "explicit switch variables optimised alongside poses" follow-up to the robust 3D backend (`gpu_pose_graph_slam_3d_robust`), which rejects bad loop closures with a *frozen* front-end trim: it scores every loop once at the initial guess, kills a hand-picked worst fraction, and never revisits the decision.

This demo replaces that trim with explicit per-loop switch variables `s_e ∈ [0,1]` optimised **jointly with the SE(3) poses**, following Sünderhauf & Protzel, *Switchable Constraints for Robust Pose Graph SLAM* (IROS 2012). The joint objective is

```
E(x, s) = Σ_odom 0.5 ||f_e(x)||²_Ω
        + Σ_loop 0.5 Ψ(s_e) ||f_e(x)||²_Ω
        + Σ_loop 0.5 Ξ (1 - s_e)²
```

with the linear switch function `Ψ(s) = s`. It is minimised by **block coordinate descent**: each outer iteration linearises the SE(3) residuals (central finite differences), closed-form-minimises every switch given the current poses

```
s_e* = clamp(1 - chi2_e / (2 Ξ), 0, 1)
```

(with asymmetric damping — a loop is turned **off fast** so it dies before the graph can bend to accommodate it, but **re-trusted slowly** so a rejected loop has to earn its weight back), then re-solves the pose graph with the updated switch weights via damped Jacobi-PCG. No loop is removed by a hand-set trim fraction; the switches are learned.

## Results

384 poses / 611 edges with 36 injected false loop closures:

| Solver | trans RMSE | rot RMSE | false loops rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain GN (corrupted graph) | 6.95 m | 39.89 deg | 0 / 36 |
| **switchable constraints** | **0.29 m** | **2.23 deg** | **36 / 36** |

- True loop switches converge to ~1.00, false loop switches to ~0.00 (within ~3 iterations).
- GPU and CPU references agree to under 1 mm (0.2936 m vs 0.2934 m).
- GPU 0.36 s vs CPU 0.51 s over 60 GN iterations (1.4x; the backend is dominated by per-PCG-iteration host syncs, so the headline here is robustness, not throughput).

## Test plan

- [x] `cmake .. && make gpu_pose_graph_slam_3d_switchable -j$(nproc)`
- [x] `./bin/gpu_pose_graph_slam_3d_switchable` — plain 6.95 m → switchable 0.29 m / 2.23 deg, 36/36 false loops rejected
- [x] GPU/CPU final poses agree to < 1 mm
- [x] `git diff --check` clean; GIF 2.4 MB (≤ 3 MB budget)
- [x] GIF deployed to gh-pages

![demo](https://rsasaki0109.github.io/CudaRobotics/gpu_pose_graph_slam_3d_switchable.gif)

author: remsky
body:
Heads up: Kokoro-FastAPI v0.4.0 changed the `/v1/audio/voices` response shape.

Items in the `voices` array changed from plain strings to `{"id","name"}` objects (https://github.com/remsky/Kokoro-FastAPI/pull/462). `listVoices` in `src/providers/kokoro.ts:78` types the response as `voices?: string[]` and treats each entry as an id, so against v0.4.0 the returned `VoiceInfo[]` is silently corrupted (id is `[object Object]`).

This patch widens the type to `Array<string | { id?: string; name?: string }>` and normalizes both shapes, so narrate keeps working against old and new Kokoro-FastAPI servers without pinning. Server-side escape hatch is also available: `?legacy=true` on the request.

##### Minor Changes

-   [#​1748](https://redirect.github.com/lint-staged/lint-staged/pull/1748) [`809d5ef`](https://redirect.github.com/lint-staged/lint-staged/commit/809d5ef0a66edb2b26b233d33ce8e14af6c978e7) Thanks [@​iiroj](https://redirect.github.com/iiroj)! - Add new option `--hide-all` for hiding all unstaged changes and untracked files, before running tasks. This makes it easier to run tools like [Knip](https://knip.dev) which check for unused code. Untracked files are included in the backup stash and restored automatically after running.

-   [#​1759](https://redirect.github.com/lint-staged/lint-staged/pull/1759) [`f13045a`](https://redirect.github.com/lint-staged/lint-staged/commit/f13045a5eae28c3233fc37146b0e1f51739c254b) Thanks [@​iiroj](https://redirect.github.com/iiroj)! - Update dependencies, including [`tinyexec@1.1.1`](https://redirect.github.com/tinylibs/tinyexec/releases/tag/1.1.1) to fix the following issues:
    -   When using a Node.js version manager with multiple versions installed ([nvm](https://redirect.github.com/nvm-sh/nvm), [n](https://redirect.github.com/tj/n), for example), scripts with the `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang ([Prettier](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier), [ESLint](https://redirect.github.com/eslint/eslint), for example) were previously spawned using the default Node.js version configured by the version manager (the one `which node` points to) on POSIX systems. Now, they will be spawned with the same version that *lint-staged* itself was started with.
        -   For example, if your default Node.js version is 24.14.1 but *lint-staged* is run with the latest version 25.9.0, the tasks spawned by *lint-staged* will now also use version 25.9.0. Previously they were spawned using 24.14.1.
    -   When installing Node.js from the Ubuntu App Center ([Snap store](https://snapcraft.io/store)), the `node` executable available in `PATH` is a symlink pointing to Snap itself. The sandboxing features of Snap prevented *lint-staged* from spawning scripts with the `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang, because it meant *lint-staged* tried to spawn Snap via the symlink. This resulted in an `ENOENT` error when trying to run `prettier`, for example. Now, since the real `node` executable's directory is available in the `PATH`, *lint-staged* will instead spawn the script with the real `node` binary succesfully.

💡 Vulnerability: The `admin.service.js` `getUsers` method was passing raw user input directly to a MongoDB `$regex` operator via `filters.search` without escaping it. `express-mongo-sanitize` only strips keys starting with `$`, but doesn't sanitize the value of `$regex` payloads, making the endpoint vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) and NoSQL injection.
🎯 Impact: An attacker could craft a complex regex string to consume excessive CPU or retrieve restricted user data.
🔧 Fix: Imported the existing `escapeRegex` utility from `utils/sanitize.js` to escape the user search input before inserting it into the Mongoose `$regex` query.
✅ Verification: Ran the security test suite locally (`tests/security/sanitize.test.js`) and verified the escaping logic properly nullifies regex metadata characters.

## Summary
- `spendCredits('desk', job.id)` — `job.id` is now stamped as the idempotency key on the credit transaction so a downstream refund can reverse it precisely.
- New `refundOnFailure()` helper inside `runJob`. Called from:
  - `missing_anthropic_key` early return
  - `summarize` LLM call failure
  - `CancelledError` (user cancel)
  - fatal catch (unknown runtime error)
- The cancel event message now tells the user the refund happened ("차감된 크레딧은 돌려드렸어요").

## Behavior
Before: pre-charge 25 credits; any failure path leaves user paying for nothing.
After: charge stays only on `status='done'`; every non-done terminal status restores the credit. Refund is idempotent at the DB level (UNIQUE on `credit_transactions(generation_id) WHERE reason='feature_refund'`), so the multiple call sites in the catch tree are safe.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI / Vercel preview build passes
- [ ] In preview: run a desk job that's guaranteed to fail (bad credentials env, or hit cancel mid-run) → verify balance returns to original
- [ ] Run a successful desk job → verify balance dropped by 25, no refund row in `credit_transactions`
- [ ] Cancel a job mid-summarize → verify status='cancelled' AND refund row exists
- [ ] Verify retry of a successful job doesn't refund or re-charge (idempotency)

## What

Use the already-materialized `texts_` sequence instead of the original `texts` iterable when building Document objects in `VectorStore.add_texts()` and `VectorStore.aadd_texts()`.

## Why

When `texts` is a generator, it gets consumed by the `list(texts)` materialization on line 77/215. The subsequent `zip(texts, ...)` on line 89/229 then iterates over an exhausted generator, producing zero documents.

Changed `texts` to `texts_` in the `zip(...)` call on both the sync `add_texts` and async `aadd_texts` methods.

body:
## What

Resolves https://github.com/airbytehq/oncall/issues/12708:
- https://github.com/airbytehq/oncall/issues/12708

Migrates `source-hubspot` CRM association enrichment requests away from HubSpot's legacy `/crm/v4/associations/.../batch/read` endpoint to the supported date-based Associations API endpoint: `/crm/associations/2026-03/.../batch/read`.

This addresses HubSpot's announced v4 API unsupported date of March 30, 2027:
- https://developers.hubspot.com/changelog/deprecating-support-for-hubspot-v4-apis
- https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/crm/associations/associate-records/batch/get-associations

## How

- Updates `build_associations_retriever` in `components.py` to construct association batch-read requests against `/crm/associations/2026-03/{fromObjectType}/{toObjectType}/batch/read`.
- Adds a focused unit test proving `HubspotAssociationsExtractor` uses the date-based endpoint.
- Updates existing mocked association endpoints in source-hubspot unit/integration test helpers.
- Updates `CONTRIBUTING.md` to keep the connector's hidden association enrichment behavior current.
- Bumps `source-hubspot` from `6.5.5` to `6.5.6` and adds a changelog entry.

## Declarative-First Evaluation

`source-hubspot` is a certified low-code connector with custom Python components (`language:manifest-only`, `cdk:low-code`). The affected behavior is an existing hidden enrichment request built in `HubspotAssociationsExtractor` / `build_associations_retriever`, outside the manifest. I evaluated declarative alternatives such as `$ref` overrides, transformations, `SubstreamPartitionRouter`, and requester path changes in manifest YAML; they are not sufficient for this already-custom runtime retriever construction because the retriever is created inside the extractor to batch-enrich records from the parent response. The fix keeps the existing custom component and only changes the request path.

## Breaking Change Evaluation

This is not a breaking change. The diff does not change stream schemas, primary keys, cursor fields, config/spec fields, state format, or stream availability. It only changes the internal HubSpot association batch-read URL used to populate existing association fields. Standard patch versioning is used.

## User Impact

Users should continue receiving the same HubSpot association data for CRM search streams, but the connector now uses HubSpot's supported date-based Associations API instead of the legacy v4 API before v4 becomes unsupported.

author: w5851
body:
## 变更范围
- 为 PNJL susceptibility/derivative 路径引入 TaylorDiff 依赖和 explicit Taylor-series gap Newton，实现单方向 `chi_B/chi_Q/chi_S` fast path。
- 增加内部 mixed BQS multivariate Taylor jet backend，支持高阶 mixed `chi_BQS(...; orders=(nB,nQ,nS))`，并保留单方向不走通用 `D=1` jet。
- 将 ThermoDerivatives 与 legacy implicit gap compat 的默认路径切到 TaylorDiff，同时保留显式 `derivative_backend=:forwarddiff` fallback/reference。
- 增加 FD 固化基线、CEP 邻域回归、mixedjet 固定点回归、性能探针和 API/性能文档。

## 用户影响
- 现有 `Models.chi_B(...; order=n, ...)` API 保持兼容；默认 `derivative_backend=:auto` 现在优先走 TaylorDiff 路线。
- mixed BQS 高阶组合可通过 `chi_BQS(...; orders=(2,1,0))` 等统一入口直接计算。
- `:forwarddiff` 路径没有删除，仍可用于迁移期低阶 reference/fallback。

## 实现方式
- primal gap 解仍由现有 solver 产生，`ForwardDiff.jacobian` 仅用于 primal `J0 = dF/dx`。
- 单方向用 `TaylorDiff.TaylorScalar` 承载 `T/mu` 方向与 gap series，逐阶求解系数后从 pressure series 提取导数。
- mixed BQS 用项目内私有 `MixedTaylorJet{D,N,L}` 承载多变量系数，复用 primal solve、`J0`、linear solve 策略、残差检查和 pressure extraction。
- `linear_solve=:auto` 仍保留按阶数分派，避免硬编码 factorization 一定更优。

## 验证项
- `julia --project=. -e 'ENV["UNIT_FILES"]="pnjl/test_chi_b_taylordiff_helpers.jl;pnjl/test_conserved_charge_susceptibilities.jl;pnjl/test_thermo_derivatives.jl;models/test_implicit_gap.jl;models/test_implicit_gap_flavor_mu.jl"; include("tests/unit/runtests.jl")'` - 185 pass, 10m39s
- `julia --project=. -e 'ENV["REGRESSION_FILES"]="pnjl/test_pnjl_chi_b_taylordiff_regression.jl;pnjl/test_pnjl_chi_b_taylordiff_cep_smoke.jl;pnjl/test_pnjl_chi_bqs_mixedjet_regression.jl"; include("tests/regression/runtests.jl")'` - 32 pass, 3m48s
- `julia --project=. -e 'ENV["UNIT_PROFILE"]="smoke"; include("tests/unit/runtests.jl")'` - 156 pass
- `julia --project=. -e 'ENV["REGRESSION_PROFILE"]="smoke"; include("tests/regression/runtests.jl")'` - expected optional fixture skip only
- Governance: docs consistency, models entry contract, solver contract leakage, PNJL migration guard, precompile profile coverage, active docs governance, script entrypoints, and `git diff --check` all passed.
- Perf: `scripts/perf/pnjl_chi_bqs_mixedjet_probe.jl --p_num=8 --t_num=4 --repeats=5` recorded mixed warm medians from 0.024s to 0.109s for `(1,1,0)`, `(2,1,0)`, `(1,1,1)`, `(2,1,1)`.

## 已知非目标

## Summary

Prepare the 5.1 release by completing the major OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, V4/V5 code generation, runtime, documentation, benchmark, and release-readiness work accumulated on the branch.

## Main changes

- **OpenAPI client generation**
  - Added richer response handling for JSON, text, and stream content, including `Accept` header generation, `Content-Type` dispatch, exhaustive `MatchResult` support, response links, runtime expressions, external/remote reference resolution, lock-file persistence, and request/response validation.
  - Added support for form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data, multipart/mixed, binary parts, default parameter values, deprecated operations, server URL templating, authentication cleanup, and expanded CLI commands/settings.

- **OpenAPI 3.2 support**
  - Added OpenAPI 3.2 project/generator/runtime coverage, including querystring parameters, cookie/path serialization behavior, `$self` document identity, optional response descriptions, security scheme metadata, itemSchema streaming, SSE item streaming, and tag hierarchy support.

- **OpenAPI server generation**
  - Added server stub generation with typed result factories, document-backed parsing, style-aware parameter parsing, form-urlencoded and multipart deserialization, typed response headers, and allocation-conscious endpoint generation.

- **AsyncAPI support and release fixes**
  - Added AsyncAPI 2.6 generation support alongside existing 3.0 behavior, including CLI/playground dispatch, request/reply extension handling, generated producer/consumer coverage, transport test support, Kafka/WebSocket fixes, and AsyncAPI benchmark coverage.

- **V4/V5 generator and runtime improvements**
  - Completed 5.1 wrap-up fixes across generated composition helpers, mutable `TryGetAs___` results, pattern-property helpers, accessibility controls, debugger display output, formatting interfaces, `WithApplied`, property-name handling, trim-warning removal, and schema naming heuristics.

- **Performance and allocation work**
  - Reworked hot paths around text responses, streaming readers, SSE, form-url-encoded and multipart serializers, property lookup, server endpoint generation, and generated helpers to reduce allocations and preserve UTF-8-first processing.

- **Benchmarks, tests, and documentation**
  - Added Corvus vs Kiota OpenAPI benchmarks and feature-comparison docs, expanded codegen/runtime/E2E coverage across OpenAPI 3.0/3.1/3.2 and AsyncAPI, updated release notes/versioning, refreshed package docs including the CLI README, and added/updated documentation examples and catalog entries.
