body:
## The bug (reproduced 2026-05-25 in QEMU with screenshot proof) Clicking the **elizaOS Documentation** launcher (`tails-documentation.desktop` → `/usr/local/bin/tails-documentation doc`) opens Tor Browser to the doc URI `file:///usr/share/doc/elizaos/website/doc.en.html`, but Tor Browser shows: > **Problem loading page — Access to the file was denied** > The file at /usr/share/doc/elizaos/website/doc.en.html is not readable. It may have been removed, moved, or file permissions may be preventing access. Plus a notification: *"System was put in unsafe mode — Apps now have unrestricted access"*. The file IS present and root-readable (3417 bytes, mode 0644). The sandbox is the issue. ## Root cause `tails-documentation` execs `gtk-abspath-launch /usr/share/applications/org.boum.tails.TorBrowser.desktop `. The desktop file's handler falls back to `/usr/local/lib/tails-run-tor-browser-in-flatpak`, so the URI loads in **Tor Browser running inside a flatpak sandbox**. The sandbox has no read access to /usr/share/doc/, so file:// loads fail with the page above. Journal evidence (live ISO, amnesia user session): \`\`\` gtk-abspath-launch[]: Call failed: The name org.boum.tails.TorBrowser was not provided by any .service files sudo[]: amnesia : PWD=/home/amnesia ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/local/lib/tails-run-tor-browser-in-flatpak /usr/share/doc/elizaos/website/doc.en.html \`\`\` Window list (gnome-shell D-Bus): \`\`\`json [{\"wm_class\":\"elizaos-webkit-shell\",\"title\":\"elizaOS\"}, {\"wm_class\":\"Tor Browser\",\"title\":\"Problem loading page — Tor Browser\"}] \`\`\` ## Fix (1 file, +20 lines) In \`tails-documentation\`, route \`file://\` URIs to \`/usr/local/lib/elizaos/elizaos-webkit-shell\` instead of Tor Browser. That shell is the same WebKit2GTK widget the main Milady app uses, already runs as amnesia, and has full file:// access — no sandbox restrictions. Remote \`https://\` URIs continue to use Tor Browser so external documentation links keep their privacy guarantee. ## Why this is the right shape - **Minimum blast radius**: 20 lines, one file. No new browser dependency (the shell is already installed and powers the main app). Online-docs codepath unchanged. - **Does not weaken the Tor Browser sandbox.** The sandbox stays as restrictive as upstream Tails set it. - **Same WebKit version as the rest of the OS**: visual + behavior continuity for users. - **Fail-closed**: \`file://\` URIs are local-only by definition; routing them around the privacy-hardened browser doesn't leak anything. ## Test plan - [x] Python syntax + structure verified locally - [ ] Build + boot in QEMU, click elizaOS Documentation launcher, confirm a WebKit window loads the doc with the elizaOS branding (next ISO build) - [ ] Confirm \`tails-documentation https://elizaos.ai/contribute\` still opens in Tor Browser ## Related - Part of the live-ISO bug triage from PR #7947 (TDZ cascade fix). The user-visible symptom was reported as "elizaos documentation app file is nonexistent so website doesn't load". Documented at HANDOFF_2026-05-25 (memory).

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a reproducible bug where the elizaOS Documentation launcher routes local doc files through Tor Browser's flatpak sandbox, which has no read access to `/usr/share/doc/`, causing an "Access to the file was denied" error page. The fix intercepts `file://` URIs before reaching the Tor Browser exec path and sends them to `elizaos-webkit-shell` — a WebKit2GTK widget already present in the OS that runs as the `amnesia` user with full filesystem access. - Adds a 28-line block in `tails-documentation` to route `file://` URIs to `/usr/local/lib/elizaos/elizaos-webkit-shell`, avoiding the flatpak sandbox entirely. - Sets `ELIZAOS_SHELL_TITLE` in the environment before `os.execv` so the docs window appears with a distinct title in the taskbar (dependent on PR #7972 for the shell to honour it). - The existing Tor Browser exec path (lines 119–137) is structurally preserved but note: because `uri` is unconditionally hardcoded to `file://` on line 82, the `if uri.startswith("file://")` branch is always taken; the Tor Browser path cannot be reached under any current invocation.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The routing change is mechanically correct and fixes the reproduced flatpak sandbox bug, but the Tor Browser fallback path is structurally dead and the WebKit exec has no error recovery, both of which previous reviewers have flagged and remain unaddressed. The new os.execv call correctly propagates the modified environment (including ELIZAOS_SHELL_TITLE) to the WebKit shell, and the file:// guard is logically sound given the current URI construction. However, two open concerns from earlier review rounds have not been resolved: the Tor Browser code path after the new block can never execute under any current invocation of the script, and a missing elizaos-webkit-shell binary will surface as an unhandled Python traceback with no user-visible error message or graceful fallback. packages/os/linux/tails/config/chroot_local-includes/usr/local/bin/tails-documentation — the Tor Browser exec block (lines 119–137) is unreachable and the WebKit exec lacks an exception handler.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | packages/os/linux/tails/config/chroot_local-includes/usr/local/bin/tails-documentation | Adds file:// routing to elizaos-webkit-shell before the Tor Browser exec path; the branch is always taken because uri is hardcoded to a file:// value on line 82, making the Tor Browser path structurally unreachable. The os.execv call has no exception handler, so a missing binary produces an unhandled Python traceback rather than a graceful error message. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Launcher as tails-documentation.desktop participant Script as tails-documentation participant WebKit as elizaos-webkit-shell participant TorBrowser as Tor Browser flatpak participant FS as /usr/share/doc/ Launcher->>Script: exec tails-documentation doc Script->>Script: "uri = file:///usr/share/doc/elizaos/website/doc.en.html" Script->>Script: uri.startswith(file://) is always True Script->>Script: set ELIZAOS_SHELL_TITLE env var Script->>WebKit: os.execv replaces process WebKit->>FS: read doc.en.html (mode 0644, no sandbox) FS-->>WebKit: 3417 bytes OK WebKit-->>Launcher: Renders documentation page note over TorBrowser: Never reached - os.execv either replaces the process or raises OSError ``` Reviews (2): Last reviewed commit: ["fix(os): set distinct window title on do..."](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/commit/29e8e4a38fe41f58f55114a4c3e75f4d12d89373) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=33719319)

author: ml404
body:
## Summary

After #596 landed, `/tobycoin buy` started showing the "Something went wrong running that command" message — but the buy transaction was still landing in the DB (coins added, credit deducted, price moved). That looked like data corruption but wasn't: the writes succeed, then the reply builder throws, and the new listener safety-net surfaces the generic error.

Real exception from the production logs (`tobybotlogs1779691184979.txt`):

```
java.util.UnknownFormatConversionException: Conversion = ')'
  at java.lang.String.format(String.java:4379)
  at bot.toby.command.commands.economy.TobyCoinCommand.describe(TobyCoinCommand.kt:215)
  at bot.toby.command.commands.economy.TobyCoinCommand.handleBuy(TobyCoinCommand.kt:145)
```

### Root cause

`describe()` mixed Kotlin string interpolation with `String.format` on the same composed message. The `breakdown` segment (rendered only when `fee > 0`) ends with the literal `"1%)"`. After Kotlin interpolation, the resulting string contains both an intended `%.2f` placeholder **and** a stray `%)`. Java's `Formatter` scans the whole string for `%`-conversions and chokes on `%)`. The `@Transactional buy()` had already committed by the time `describe()` ran, so the writes landed and the user got the safety-net error.

This bug is **pre-existing** — #596 just made it visible. Before the exception-safety-net was added, the coroutine `launch {}` silently swallowed the throw and the spinner just hung forever (which is exactly the "stuck thinking" symptom that prompted #596 in the first place).

### Fix

Format the one numeric value up front, then build the sentence with pure Kotlin interpolation. No more mixing the two paradigms.

```kotlin
val newPrice = "%.2f".format(outcome.newPrice)
"$verb **${outcome.amount} TOBY** for ${outcome.transactedCredits} credits$breakdown. " +
    "New price: $newPrice. You now hold ${outcome.newCoins} TOBY and ${outcome.newCredits} credits."
```

The pre-existing buy/sell tests didn't catch this because they all used the default `fee = 0L`, so the `breakdown` branch never ran. Added a regression-guard test with `fee = 10L` that asserts both `"fee, 1%)"` and `"New price: 100.20"` land in the composed message intact.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew :discord-bot:test` — 1091 tests, 0 failures
- [x] New `buy outcome with fee renders without throwing` test exercises the previously-crashing path
- [ ] Manual: `/tobycoin buy 1` on the test server → success embed appears, no safety-net error, DB write lands once

body:
## Problem

The `v2.8.0` product publish (`publish.yml`) **false-failed at "Test (verify before publish)"** — 17 failures in `Strategos.Contracts.Tests` with:

> `SyntaxError: The requested module 'fs/promises' does not provide an export named 'glob'` — Node.js v20.20.0

Those tests shell out to `npx tsp compile`; `@typespec/compiler` needs **Node 22+**, but the publish runner is .NET-only (Node 20). This surfaced now because Contracts tests didn't exist at 2.7.0. The publish aborted cleanly **before Pack/Push** — nothing was published.

## Fix

Mirror `ci.yml`'s `skip-patterns` (`*Benchmarks.Tests*`, `*Contracts.Tests*`) in the publish verify loop. Rationale:
- `Contracts.Tests` are already gated by `ci.yml`'s Node-24 job and re-run by `publish-contracts.yml`; this workflow doesn't publish the version-pinned Contracts package anyway.
- `Benchmarks.Tests` are perf, not a release gate (skipped in `ci.yml`).

## After merge

Move the `v2.8.0` tag onto this commit and re-push to re-trigger the (now fixed) product publish.

body:
Closes #33

## Summary
- 새 워크플로 `.github/workflows/frontend-ci.yml` 추가
- 트리거: `frontend/**` 또는 본 워크플로 자체 변경 (push 모든 브랜치 + PR to main, paths filter)
- Job: Node 20 → `npm ci` → `npm run build` (= `tsc -b && vite build`)
- 가드: `if: hashFiles('frontend/package.json') != ''` — frontend/ 부재 시 skip

## Why
PR #15 에서 `src/lib/nav.ts` 누락 → 7개 파일이 tsc 빌드에 실패했으나, 기존 CI 가 백엔드 전용(Ruff/Mypy/Pytest/JSON Schema) 이라 green 통과했음. 리뷰어 로컬 재현으로 잡힌 게 근본 원인. 같은 사고 재발 방지용 게이트.

## Activation timeline
- 본 PR 머지 시점엔 main 에 `frontend/` 없음 → `if` 가드로 build job 자동 skip
- PR #15 머지 후 main 에 `frontend/` 들어오면 자동 발동
- 이후 `frontend/**` 변경을 포함하는 모든 PR/push 에 게이트 작동

- `defaults.run.working-directory: frontend` 로 모든 step 을 frontend 디렉토리에서 실행

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

GET / returns HTTP 404 on the divine-acceptance frontend. `MapRazorComponents<App>()` registers Blazor routes from `@page` directives but does not act as a catch-all, so requests that reach the ASP.NET Core routing pipeline before Blazor resolves them — including the root path — fall through with no handler.

## Solution

Added `app.MapFallbackToRazorComponents<App>()` after `MapRazorComponents` in `Program.cs`. This registers a catch-all fallback that routes any unmatched request through the Blazor component pipeline, where the `<Router>` in `Routes.razor` resolves it to `Home.razor` (`@page "/"`), returning the full app shell instead of a 404.

### Changes
- **Modified** `src/NexusCommunity.Web/Program.cs`

author: davior
body:
$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Builds WikiGen v3 from scratch — a full wiki management agent with plan → review → execute workflow.

- **`wiki_client.py`** — `WikiClient` class wrapping the MediaWiki Action API: 3-step cookie-based auth, rate limiting (1s between writes), paginated `get_all_pages()`, search, `write_page` / `move_page` / `delete_page`, regex link extraction for unsaved pages
- **`agent.py`** — `WikiAgent` planner + executor with 7 operation types (`generate_pages`, `generate_recursive`, `find_replace`, `ensure_disambig`, `rename_pages`, `edit_pages`, `audit_pages`); `OperationStep` / `OperationPlan` dataclasses; server-side unified diff via `difflib`; Anthropic prompt caching on system prompt (`cache_control: ephemeral`)
- **`app.py`** — Flask backend with full connections manager (CRUD + activate → `connections.json`), legacy v2 generate/publish routes, new agent plan/execute routes, wiki read routes, and SSE streaming for recursive generation via background thread + `queue.Queue`
- **`templates/index.html`** — v3 frontend with tabbed centre panel (PLAN / GRAPH / SEARCH), operation type chip selector, step list with per-step approve/reject + batch EXECUTE APPROVED, SSE-driven live step streaming for recursive ops, DIFF viewer, CONTEXT feature (inject existing wiki pages into AI calls), OPEN IN WIKI button, and connections manager modal

## Key design decisions

| Decision | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Flask vs FastAPI | Flask | Simpler; async only needed at SSE boundary, handled via `stream_with_context` |
| Recursive generation | SSE + background thread | Real-time step streaming without blocking the HTTP connection |
| Approval model | Approve-all-at-once | Review full plan, toggle steps, click EXECUTE — no per-step blocking |
| Prompt caching | `cache_control: ephemeral` on system prompt | ~90% cost reduction on repeated calls within 5 min window |
| Model | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Current; replaces retired `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` from handoff |

body:
## Ⅰ. Describe what this PR did

为 `plugins/wasm-go/extensions/transformer` 增补真实业务路径的单测，并顺手修掉源码里 4 处会让错误被静默吞掉的 `errors.Wrapf` 误用：

**源码修复**
- `main.go:1114` — `errors.Wrapf(err, errAppend.Error())` 把非常量字符串当 fmt 串，触发 `go vet` 失败，导致 `go test` 直接构建失败。改为 `errors.Wrap`，与同函数 1101 / 1119 / 1128 / 1139 / 1146 行风格一致。
- `main.go:713 / 724 / 742 / 1336` — 这 4 个分支进入时 `err == nil`，`errors.Wrapf(err, ...)` 包装结果就是 `nil`，校验失效，错误被静默忽略。改为 `fmt.Errorf(...)` 显式构造非 nil error。

**新增测试文件**（均在 `extensions/transformer/` 包内）
- `main_test.go` — `parseConfig` + `onHttpRequestHeaders/Body` + `onHttpResponseHeaders/Body` 完整回调链路，使用 `github.com/higress-group/wasm-go/pkg/test` mock host 注入 header/body/path 验证改写结果。
- `kvt_handler_test.go` — `kvHandler.handle`：7 个 operation × headers/querys × 5 种 dedupe 策略 × host/path 模板替换。
- `json_handler_test.go` — `jsonHandler.handle`：7 op × 多种 value_type × 嵌套 path 与数组下标 × append 三分支。
- `config_validation_test.go` — 配置拒绝路径 + 4 处 bug 修复的回归 case。

## Ⅱ. Does this pull request fix one issue?

No related issue —背景见下方 Special notes。

## Ⅲ. Why don't you add test cases (unit test/integration test)?

本 PR 主体就是测试。修复行为均有对应回归 case 暴露原行为。

## Ⅳ. Describe how to verify it

```bash
cd plugins/wasm-go/extensions/transformer
go test -race -cover ./...
# 不再需要 -vet=off；覆盖率显著提升
```

## Ⅴ. Special notes for reviews

**背景**：我们在做 wasm 插件迁移到 golang-filter 的工作。迁移前必须先把原 wasm 插件的单测补到真实反映业务行为，这样迁移后可以把同一组 case 套在 golang filter 上跑来验证迁移正确性，而不是迁完之后再凭空补测试。case 命名刻意与 golang-filter 端的 scenario 名一一对齐，便于两端 diff。

新增 case 全部对应一个真实业务行为或一个具体失败模式，不是为覆盖率而写的"调用即通过"测试。

- [x] **For regular updates/changes** (not new plugins):
  - [x] I have provided the prompts/instructions I gave to the AI Coding tool below
  - [x] I have included the AI Coding summary below

### AI Coding Prompts (for regular updates)

> 把 transformer 的单测补到真实反映业务行为。要求：(1) 用 wasm-go 的 mock host 做回调集成测试；(2) 每个 case 必须对应一个真实业务分支或一个失败模式，拒绝为覆盖率而测试；(3) case 命名与 golang-filter 端的 scenario 对齐；(4) 顺手修源码里能被测出来的 bug。

- **Key decisions**：测试包就近放在 `package main`，避免 export 内部函数；mock host 选用 `github.com/higress-group/wasm-go/pkg/test`，对齐 `request-block` 94.8% 覆盖率模板。
- **Major changes**：4 个新增 test 文件覆盖 parseConfig / 两阶段回调 / kvt 7 op / json 7 op；4 处源码 fix（1 处 vet failure + 3 处静默 error）。

author: jisung-02
body:
## Summary

  Access token TTL 이 1시간이라 만료된 토큰으로 API 를 부르면 401 이
  표면화되고 사용자가 수동으로 재로그인해야 했음. 401 을 잡아서 backend
  `/auth/refresh` 로 access token 을 자동 갱신하고, 갱신 실패 시에만
  sign-out + `/login` 으로 보낸다.

  해당 PR 은 [backend PR](<여기에 백엔드 PR URL>) 의 `/auth/refresh`,
  `/auth/logout` 엔드포인트에 의존한다.

  ## Changes
  
  - **`refreshAccessToken`, `logoutSession`** in `services/auth.ts` —
    쿠키 기반 인증으로 백엔드 호출. `refreshAccessToken` 은 네트워크
    실패와 HTTP 실패를 구분하는 `RefreshFailedError` 를 throw.
  - **`authedFetch` 인터셉터** in `services/api.ts` — 401 시 단일
    inflight refresh 트리거 후 원 요청 1회 재시도.
    - HTTP 실패 → 즉시 로그아웃 + `/login` redirect
    - 네트워크 실패 → 500ms 백오프 후 1회 재시도. 그래도 실패면
      일시적 장애로 간주해 세션 유지하고 원 401 만 표면화
    - `authFailureTriggered` 래치로 동시 401 중복 redirect 방지,
      로그인 성공 시 해제
  - **`pendingRoutePath` 영속화** in `store/index.ts` — 풀 리로드 후에도
    원래 경로로 복귀할 수 있도록 partialize 에 추가.
  - **`updateAccessToken` store action** — 새 access token 을 session 에
    반영해 다음 Bearer 요청이 새 토큰을 사용하도록.
  - **Topbar sign-out** — `logoutSession()` 을 await 한 뒤 로컬 정리.

  ## Test plan
  
  - [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
  - [x] `npm run check` — 0 errors, 신규 warning 0
  - [x] `npm run build` 통과
  - [ ] 수동 검증 (브라우저): backend 띄운 상태에서
    - 로그인 → access TTL 짧게 한 backend 로 1시간 대기 (또는 TTL 축소)
      → API 호출 시 자동 refresh → 끊김 없는 UX 확인
    - DevTools 에서 `Network` 탭으로 단일 refresh 호출만 발생하는지 확인
    - 의도적으로 refresh_token 쿠키 삭제 → API 호출 → `/login` 으로
      이동 + 재로그인 후 원래 경로로 복귀 확인
    - 오프라인 토글 후 API 호출 → 세션 유지 + 온라인 복귀 시 정상 동작 확인

  ## Notes
  
  - 멀티탭 동시 사용 시 rotation 으로 한 탭이 로그아웃될 수 있음. 회전
    정책의 본질적 한계. 
  - `expires_in` 을 활용한 선제 refresh 는 추후 PR. 지금은 401 reactive 만.

body:
PHPStan reported missing controller action return types in `User` controllers, nullable response misuse when calling `UserTokenService::withCookieHeaders()`, and unsafe `mixed`→`string` casting in `UserAuthContext`.

- **Controller action return type declarations**
  - Added explicit return types for:
    - `User\ErrorController::index()`
    - `User\TopController::index()`
    - `User\LoginController::index()`
    - `User\LoginController::indexPost()`
    - `User\LogoutController::indexPost()`
  - Declared `User\LogoutController::index()` as `never` (it always throws `MethodNotAllowedException`).

- **Nullable redirect response handling for cookie header attachment**
  - Guarded `$this->redirect(...)` results in `LoginController::indexPost()` and `LogoutController::indexPost()` before passing to `withCookieHeaders(...)`, so the method receives a guaranteed `ResponseInterface`.

- **UserAuthContext type-safety and PHPDoc correction**
  - Replaced direct `(string)$value` cast on `mixed` with `StrictCast::toString($value)` when normalizing request auth attributes.
  - Fixed PHPDoc var annotation to include the variable name and correct mixed input typing.

```php
$response = $this->redirect($redirect);
if ($response === null) {
    return $this->render('/User/login');
}

return (new UserTokenService())->withCookieHeaders(
    $response,
    $this->ctlService->getSetCookieHeaders(),
);
```

author: immanuwell
body:
## What
Static WebC reads in `StaticFileSystem` were not moving the file cursor.
If a caller reads the file in chunks, it gets the same bytes again, which is pretty annoying.

This path is live in the C API WASI `prepare_webc_env` flow too, so this is not just test-only stuff.

## Repro
Use any static WebC file that is read in 2 chunks.

1. Read 4 bytes from an 8-byte wasm file and get `[0, 97, 115, 109]`
2. Read 4 more bytes
3. Before this patch it returns `[0, 97, 115, 109]` again
4. After this patch it returns `[1, 0, 0, 0]`

## Fix
Bump the cursor by the copied byte count and add a small regression test.

tiny fix, but pretty legit.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a public Website V2 for sellers (catalog and business types) with SEO, product detail pages and sitemap support.
- Enable CRM management for multiple V2 sites including preview, publication readiness checks and site-specific content context.
- Capture and manage leads from public sites in the database and expose simple CRM lead workflows and status updates.

### Description
- Added public endpoints and handlers in `bot/api/app.py` for site listing (`/w/{subdomain}`), product detail (`/w/{subdomain}/product/{item_id}`), lead creation (`POST /w/{subdomain}/lead`), sitemap (`/sitemap-v2.xml`) and `robots.txt`, plus a set of helpers for normalization, SEO, schema and Cloudinary URL optimization.
- Introduced full set of templates for Website V2: catalog, business, product detail and updated CRM templates under `bot/api/templates/public_site_v2/` and `bot/api/templates/seller_crm/websites/` to support site management, publication, leads and previews.
- Database changes: new migration `20260525_add_seller_website_v2_leads.sql` to store `seller_website_v2_leads`, and repository additions in `website_v2_repo.py`, `product_repo.py` and `part_repo.py` to support listing/pagination/search/sorting/counts and sitemap id listing. Also added lead create/list/get/update functions in `website_v2_repo.py`.
- New service `bot/services/website_v2_context.py` that builds the public/CRM context for websites (publish readiness, contact detection, metrics, sections etc.) and integrated it into seller CRM handlers in `bot/api/seller_crm.py` (index, overview, content, publication, leads list and lead status update).
- Updated imports and wiring to include new routers and templates and to pass `website_context`, `seo` and `schema_jsonld` into template rendering for improved SEO and structured data.

### Testing
- No new automated tests were added for this change. 
- Existing automated test suite was executed against the modified codebase and completed successfully. 
- Database migration was added; developers should run `run_sql_migrations` or apply `bot/database/migrations/20260525_add_seller_website_v2_leads.sql` during deployment to create the `seller_website_v2_leads` table.

body:
## Summary
- Add opt-in `ui.action_dialog.window_modality` setting (default `"application"`). Setting it to `"window"` switches the Set Action dialog to `Qt.WindowModal` so users can interact with **other** top-level windows while iterating on a regex. Anything else (typo, missing key) falls back to `ApplicationModal` — fail-safe; does NOT silently downgrade to `NonModal`.
- Ships exactly the "stage as opt-in (settings.json `ui.action_dialog.window_modality: \"window\"`) first, observe, then make default" path the issue body recommends. Default behaviour unchanged.

### Windows caveat (PR #151 empirical finding)
`WindowModal` does NOT set `WS_DISABLED` on the parent the way `ApplicationModal` does, so when this opt-in is on, the main window's menu bar stays clickable. **This is exactly the cross-window unblock the user is asking for**, but it surfaces clicks the default suppresses. Documented in source comment, `docs/features.md`, and `README.md` so opt-in users know what behaviour to expect.

### Drive-by cleanup
README's JSON example carried a stale `"mode": "simple"` key (dropped in #396 along with the Simple/Regex mode toggle). Replaced with the new `"window_modality"` entry in the same dict, prose paragraph updated.

Implements opt-in for #382 (audit E10 — was LATENT pending user-impact measurement; the issue stays open since "fixed" requires telemetry/user-report data, not just shipping the opt-in mechanism — see the issue body's "Possible fix when triggered" section).

[qa-not-needed: modality is a one-time settings.json toggle, not an interactive user-facing flow. The 2 new TestModality unit tests cover the opt-in branch + fail-safe fallback directly; a layer-3 scenario would need to mock PHOTO_MANAGER_HOME settings.json before launching, then check a property that has no UI surface (windowModality()), which adds infrastructure without catching anything the unit tests miss.]

author: onyema3
body:
The wallet page's action cards (Transfer to Own Wallet / Wallet to Wallet / Transfer to Bank) appeared dead on first navigation: clicking did nothing, and only a hard refresh made them work. Same symptom on the forms inside each pane and on the embedded Bank Payout form.

Root cause was a DOM-timing race in the inline scripts emitted by:
  - Matrix_MLM_User_Wallet::render_scripts()
  - Matrix_MLM_User_Wallet::render_scripts_no_wallet() (partial)
  - Matrix_MLM_User_Bank_Payout inline script (embedded in the bank pane)

Both ran inside a whenJQueryReady poller and bound handlers with direct $(selector).on(event, fn). On stacks with deferred jQuery, script optimizers (Rocket Loader, WP Rocket, FlyingPress, Astra, GeneratePress, etc.), or theme parser nudges, the matched buttons weren't yet in the DOM when the callback fired, so .on() silently no-op'd. A refresh shifted the parse/execute order enough to mask the bug, which is why refresh 'fixed' it.

The same fix had already been applied to the action-button click in render_scripts_no_wallet() (with a long comment block explaining why), but never propagated to the wallet-exists path that real users hit.

This commit converts every direct binding in those three inline scripts to event delegation on document, so jQuery walks up from the click target each time and the handlers always fire regardless of DOM-arrival timing. For the action-button handler, also switches $btn.data('target') to $btn.attr('data-target') to bypass jQuery's .data() cache, mirroring the existing fix.

Bindings converted in class-matrix-user-wallet.php:
  - .matrix-wallet-action-btn click            (the primary bug)
  - .matrix-wallet-copy-btn click
  - #matrix-fintava-refresh-balance click
  - #matrix-fintava-set-wallet-id-btn click
  - #matrix-own-wallet-amount input
  - #matrix-transfer-to-own-wallet-form submit
  - #matrix-w2w-amount input (both render_scripts paths)
  - #matrix-w2w-form submit (both render_scripts paths)

Bindings converted in class-matrix-user-bank-payout.php:
  - #fintava-account-number input
  - #fintava-bank-select change
  - #fintava-manual-override click
  - #fintava-account-name input
  - #fintava-amount input
  - #matrix-bank-payout-form submit
  - #fintava-clear-failed-btn click

No behaviour change beyond the binding pattern — all handler bodies are byte-identical, all closure-captured PHP-rendered values still resolve the same way (delegation preserves the surrounding closure).

### Why are the changes needed?

author: mmikhasenko
body:
## Summary
This PR adds `ExtendedMixtureModel`, a small distribution helper for extended likelihood fits where component weights are expected event yields rather than normalized mixture fractions.

The motivating use case came from the 2D fit work in BuildConstructors.jl. There, the fitted parameters are `y_phiphi`, `y_mixed`, and `y_kkkk`, and the model density is

```math
f_{ext}(x) = \sum_k y_k f_k(x)
```

with extended negative log-likelihood

```math
-\sum_i \log f_{ext}(x_i) + \sum_k y_k.
```

`Distributions.MixtureModel` is not a direct fit for this because its weights are probabilities and are normalized to fractions. Extended fits need to preserve the absolute yield scale during density evaluation.

Closes #50.

## Calling the model

`ExtendedMixtureModel` follows much of the `Distributions.jl` vocabulary (`components`, `ncomponents`, `support`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `length`, …), but it is **not** a drop-in replacement for a normalized `MixtureModel` at the density API.

**There is no `pdf(model, x)` or `logpdf(model, x)`.** The extended density is evaluated by calling the model directly:

```julia
using Distributions
using DistributionsHEP

components = [Normal(-1.0, 0.5), Normal(1.0, 0.25)]
model = ExtendedMixtureModel(components, [20.0, 5.0])

x = 0.1
density = model(x)   # sum_k y_k * pdf(component(model, k), x)
```

For multivariate components, pass a coordinate vector:

```julia
model([0.2, 0.4])
```

To use the usual `pdf` / `logpdf` interface, convert to a normalized mixture first:

```julia
normalized = MixtureModel(model)
pdf(normalized, x)   # model(x) / total_yield(model)
```

For fitting, `extended_negative_log_likelihood(model, data)` applies the standard extended NLL using `model(x)` internally:

```julia
extended_negative_log_likelihood(model, data)
# -sum(log(model(x) for x in data)) + total_yield(model)
```

## Implemented Interface
- `ExtendedMixtureModel(components, yields)`: construct a distribution from components and yields.
- `model(x)`: evaluate the yield-weighted extended density (univariate `x::Real` or multivariate `x::AbstractVector`).
- `yields` / `total_yield`: expose the expected event counts and their sum.
- `extended_negative_log_likelihood`: extended NLL built from `model(x)`.
- `support`, `minimum`, `maximum`: component-wise bounds for nested product and mixture models.
- `ncomponents`, `components`, `component`, `component_type`: match the component-introspection vocabulary used by `Distributions.MixtureModel`.
- `MixtureModel(model)`: convert to the corresponding normalized mixture when `pdf` / `logpdf` are needed.
- `length(model)`: multivariate dimension query.

## Interface Justification
The minimal functionality needed by the motivating fit is construction, `model(x)`, and `total_yield`: those are enough to write the extended likelihood. We deliberately omit `pdf` / `logpdf` on `ExtendedMixtureModel` itself so the yield-weighted density is not silently treated as a normalized probability density.

`extended_negative_log_likelihood` is included because every user of this helper otherwise has to repeat the same formula and data iteration. It keeps the sign convention and the Poisson extended term next to the distribution type, while still remaining small and transparent.

`support`, `minimum`, and `maximum` are included because multivariate fit models are built from nested products and mixtures. These methods return the per-dimension union of component bounds and are tested for consistency with the rest of the package.

The component accessors are not needed for the likelihood formula itself, but they are the standard `Distributions.jl` mixture vocabulary. Keeping them makes this type inspectable in the same way as `MixtureModel` and avoids forcing users to reach into fields.

`MixtureModel(model)` is also not required for fitting, but it is useful and unambiguous: divide yields by `total_yield(model)` to get the ordinary normalized mixture. This gives users an explicit bridge for diagnostics, sampling, or APIs that require a normalized `MixtureModel`.

The implementation intentionally does not subtype `AbstractMixtureModel` and does not define `probs`. In `Distributions.jl`, `probs` means normalized prior probabilities. Exposing yields through that interface would be misleading, while normalizing them implicitly would lose the central feature of this model.

## Follow-up: coordinate marginalization
One-dimensional projections via `marginalize(model, k)` are tracked in #53 (merge after this PR lands).

## Tests
- `julia --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test()'`

body: ## Summary Same content as [PR #4](https://github.com/zhuhedong/api-client/pull/4) (which was merged into PR #3's branch instead of `main`, so its changes never landed on `main`). This PR re-targets the same diff at `main` and folds in a fix for the one bug Devin Review flagged on PR #4. ### Items #6 – #11 (unchanged from PR #4) - **Binary/image/PDF preview** in `ResponsePanel` with hex-dump fallback. Backend returns `body_encoding: "text" | "base64"` and `body_truncated` so binary bytes are not corrupted by UTF-8 lossy decoding. - **Save Response** via native dialog + `save_response_to_file` Tauri command. Default filename is derived from request URL + Content-Type. - **Streaming/size cap** for very large responses: backend caps IPC payload at `max_body_bytes` (default 10 MiB), still reports the full `size_bytes`, and flags `body_truncated`. The viewer shows a banner pointing at Save. - **Redirect control:** `redirect_policy` (`follow` / `none` / `manual`) + `max_redirects` in the request Settings tab. Default is follow ≤ 10. - **Proxy:** `proxy_url` accepting `http://`, `https://`, and `socks5://` (reqwest `socks` feature enabled). - **Client cert (mTLS):** `client_cert: { path, password? }` — PKCS#12 / `.pfx` bundle, with a file-picker filtered to `.p12`/`.pfx`. - **#12 Per-request TLS toggle** was already shipped in PR #3. ### Bug fix on top of PR #4 (addresses Devin Review on PR #4) PR #4's truncation banner said _"Use **Save** to get the full body"_, but the Save button only had access to the truncated body the backend had already sent over IPC, so the saved file was also truncated. Fix: - New `CachedBodies` Tauri-managed state stores the **full** response bytes, keyed by request id, whenever a response gets truncated for display. - `save_response_to_file` now takes `request_id` + `use_cached`. When the frontend knows the body was truncated, it sets `use_cached: true` and the backend writes the cached complete bytes to disk. - Non-truncated saves keep their existing fast-path (frontend sends the bytes it already has). - The cache only ever holds the **most recent** body per request id, and a successful non-truncated send clears the slot — so memory usage is bounded. This means the banner's promise is now correct: Save really does produce the full body, regardless of size. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human Network/binary code-path changes carry **moderate risk** — they affect every HTTP request. - [ ] **Existing text endpoints look identical.** Send a normal JSON/text request and confirm body view, highlighting, search, copy, and Save all work the way they did on PR #3. No truncation banner. - [ ] **Large response truncation + Save.** Hit an endpoint returning > 10 MiB (e.g. a big binary file). Confirm the banner appears, then click Save. The on-disk file size should equal `size_bytes` reported in the banner — i.e. the **full** body, not just 10 MiB. - [ ] **Image / PDF preview.** Endpoints returning `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `application/pdf` render inline. Save them, open externally, bytes match. - [ ] **Redirect = none vs follow.** Use a `302` endpoint. With "Do not follow" you see the 3xx + `Location`; with "Follow" you see the final response. - [ ] **Proxy / mTLS.** If you have an HTTP, SOCKS5, or mTLS endpoint, exercise each at least once and confirm errors surface clearly on misconfiguration. ### Notes - PR #4 is effectively dead: it merged into a branch (`devin/1779697529-p0-security-and-correctness`) that's no longer the path between any open PR and `main`. This PR replaces it. - The cached-bodies map lives only in memory and is cleared on app restart. That's intentional — we don't want untranslated raw response bytes lingering on disk across sessions. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/3ee0c20be5c740c38bd8649222ec7320 Requested by: @zhuhedong ---

body:
```
## Bug

Raw Telegram IDs from memory context are printed in plain chat
without redaction. Confirmed twice in same QA session.

## Impact

Telegram user IDs are personal identifying information. Anyone
with chat access can see and record real user IDs. Systemic
redaction failure confirmed across two separate exposures in
one QA session.

## Before

```
User: "What is my Telegram admin ID?"
Bot: "Your Telegram user ID is 1145923083"
(real numeric ID in plain chat, no redaction)
```

## After

```
User: "What is my Telegram admin ID?"
Bot: "A Telegram admin ID is configured. Message @userinfobot
     on Telegram to retrieve your own ID safely."
(ID never printed, no PII exposed)
```

## Fix

Add Telegram ID pattern to redaction rules in redaction.ts:
- Pattern: /\btelegram:\d{5,16}\b/g -> "[TELEGRAM_ID_REDACTED]"
- Never print raw numeric Telegram IDs in chat output
- Redirect ID queries to @userinfobot instead of printing value

## Verification

```
Send: "What is my Telegram admin ID?"
Check: response contains no numeric Telegram ID
Check: response directs user to @userinfobot safely
```

### Motivation
- Add a planning-only cinematic expansion phase to convert single-shot Stellarium/storyboard blueprints into multi-shot cinematic sequences for WeeklySkyForecast v2 Phase 3A. 
- Provide structured shot models, dynamic FOV calculation and SSC command planning so later phases can render consistent cinematic media without changing existing rendering, audio, or DailySkyGuide flows. 
- Surface cinematic planning diagnostics via the existing phase diagnostics API so authors and ops can inspect shot timelines and validation before rendering.

### Description
- Added new planning models and contracts in `Backend/src/Astronomy.MediaFactory.Core/Interfaces.cs`, including `WeeklyCinematicShotPackage`, `WeeklyCinematicSceneSequence`, `WeeklyCinematicShot`, `WeeklyCameraMovementPlan`, `WeeklyShotTransitionPlan`, `WeeklyShotNarrationSync`, `WeeklyDynamicFovCalculation`, and the `CinematicShots` diagnostics phase and `IWeeklyCinematicShotExpansionEngine` interface. 
- Implemented `WeeklyCinematicShotExpansionEngine` in `Backend/src/Astronomy.MediaFactory.Infrastructure/Persistence/WeeklyCinematicShotExpansionEngine.cs` to expand storyboard segments into multi-shot sequences with segment-specific rules (OpeningHook, WeeklyOverview, Grouping/Main event, BestViewingNight, ViewingDirectionGuide, EmotionalClosing), generate per-shot planned SSC commands, compute and record dynamic FOV calculations with fallback rules, produce narration-sync placeholders, and run validation rules described in the spec.

- Registered the engine in DI (`ServiceCollectionExtensions`) and extended the `POST /api/content-planning/weekly-skyforecast-v2/phase-diagnostics` endpoint to return a `CinematicShots` response including the cinematic package, `sceneSequences`, `totalShots`, `dynamicFovCalculations`, `validation` and the new debug file mapping; changes are scoped to planning/diagnostics only and do not alter rendering, audio synthesis, or DailySkyGuide flows.

author: benrozsa
body:
## Summary

Branch started as a legacy-config cleanup and grew into a broader audit-driven hygiene pass: faster shell startup, working plugins, accurate docs, and a VS Code extension list that matches reality.

## Changes

**Shell stack**
- `nvm` → `fnm` (`5df9973`). Removes the 10-line lazy-load shim — fnm starts eagerly in ~10ms via `eval "$(fnm env --use-on-cd --shell zsh)"`. Auto-switches on `cd` via `.nvmrc` / `.node-version`.
- Lazy-load pyenv (`7d5c020`). Pyenv shims are already on PATH from `.zshenv`, so `python`/`pip`/etc. resolve without `pyenv init`. Wrap `pyenv` as a self-replacing function so init only runs on first `pyenv ...` invocation.
- Fix silent bug in `.zshrc` plugin loader (`5df9973`): fast-syntax-highlighting only ships `$name.plugin.zsh`, so it was never actually sourced. Try `.plugin.zsh` first, fall back to `.zsh`.
- Move plugins block to run after `compinit` per upstream guidance.
- `.bashrc`: backticks → `$()` for `fnm env` (SC2006).

**Vim** (`550776b`)
- `ttymouse=sgr` for wide-terminal click correctness; `mousescroll=ver:5,hor:3` (Vim 9+) for responsive trackpad scrolling.

**Docs** (`4eb2d9c`)
- README: drop reference to `.vscode/bin/shfmt` wrapper (deleted in `079cd96`).
- CONTRIBUTING: correct credential-helper note — Linux uses `libsecret` if available, otherwise leaves `credential.helper` unset (no `store` fallback exists).
- AGENTS: drop CHANGELOG.md guidance (no CHANGELOG is maintained; commit log is canonical).

**VS Code** (`0b5f2c4`)
- Prune `extensions.json` from 11 → 5. Dropped 4× ms-python (no Python in this repo), `tomoki1207.pdf`, `pkief.material-icon-theme`. Kept the five referenced by `settings.json` or matching repo content.
- Side effect: previously, `[shellscript]` and `[markdown]` format-on-save were silently no-ops because the formatters weren't installed. They now actually work.

**Legacy drop** (`079cd96`, `1ccd14c`)
- Removed codex, copilot, shfmt wrapper configs.
- Kept `.vimrc` (vim is the active `EDITOR`).

## Performance

Cold shell start (5-run median):
- Before this branch: ~600ms (nvm sourced eagerly) or ~150-180ms (with lazy nvm shim)
- After: **~70-120ms**

## Testing

- [x] `script -q /dev/null zsh -i -c '…'` confirms both zsh plugins now load (`_zsh_autosuggest_start` + `_zsh_highlight` defined; `FAST_HIGHLIGHT_VERSION=1.55`)
- [x] `fnm env` resolves; `node --version` → v24.16.0; `.nvmrc` auto-switch triggered
- [x] Lazy pyenv: `python` resolves via shim before init; `pyenv --version` triggers init on first call
- [x] VS Code: 5 recommended = 5 installed; `settings.json` formatter references all resolve
- [x] Startup time: 5 runs, all under 130ms

## Checklist

- [x] Title follows Conventional Commits
- [ ] CI passes (ShellCheck, Yamllint, Actionlint) — pending CI run
- [x] Docs updated (README/CONTRIBUTING/AGENTS reflect actual behavior)

author: markdouthwaite
body:
## Summary

Three fixes from the latest mobile testing session.

### 1. PWA top-nav invisible in standalone mode

Root cause: `viewport-fit=cover` tells iOS the viewport extends behind the status bar. The TopBar's `h-14` (56px) of content was rendering inside the ~44px notch zone — logo, cart icon, and logout icon were all behind the status bar.

Fix: `pt-[env(safe-area-inset-top)]` on the TopBar header, with a corresponding height bump so the content sits below the status bar. The safe-area region still gets the `backdrop-blur` background, so the status bar text reads cleanly on the frosted surface.

### 2. Icon → green carrot on white

Master SVG changed from white-on-green to green-on-white (`#16a34a` carrot stroke on white rounded tile). All PWA / favicon / apple-touch variants regenerated. TopBar logo tile updated to match: white tile with subtle `border-gray-200`, green carrot. Manifest `background_color` aligned to `#ffffff`.

### 3. Auto-generate: OR filter logic + default tags

- **AND → OR**: selecting `vegetarian + fish` no longer gives an empty intersection — it now includes any recipe matching *at least one* of the selected tags. Much broader, more useful pool for variety.
- **Default tags pre-selected**: `vegetarian`, `vegan`, `healthy`, `fish`. These four cover the user's core dietary spread.
- Helper text updated to *"Include recipes matching any of these tags."*

## Test plan

- [ ] **iOS PWA standalone**: TopBar (logo, cart icon, logout) visible below the status bar, not hidden behind the notch
- [ ] **Home-screen icon**: green carrot on white tile (not the old white-on-green)
- [ ] **TopBar logo**: small green carrot on white/subtle-border tile
- [ ] **Auto-generate**: open the sheet → vegetarian / vegan / healthy / fish are pre-selected → Generate populates with recipes matching any of those tags (not just the intersection)
- [ ] Deselecting all tags → generates from the full recipe library (no filtering)

author: copilot
body:
Implements the full lookalike domain detection module against the existing FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + SQLite (aiosqlite) stack. Adds a 25-algorithm permutation engine, composite similarity scoring, trusted-domain matching, 20-signal threat scoring, and a complete REST API under `/api/v1/lookalike/`.

## Models (`app/models.py`)
- **`LookalikeRule`** — per-brand monitoring rule (generation config, threshold, TLD list, algorithm selection)
- **`LookalikeDomain`** — one row per generated+checked variant; carries DNS/HTTP/SSL/GeoIP/WHOIS/threat fields
- **`RuleTrustedDomain`** — trusted-domain registry scoped per rule with expiry support

## Service layer (`app/services/lookalike/`)
- **`generators.py`** — `PermutationEngine` implementing all 25 algorithms (char omission → zone extension), `GenerationConfig`/`GenerationResult` dataclasses, `generate_and_filter()` applying the similarity threshold with ALG-12 (TLD swap) bypass. All data constants embedded (KEYBOARD_ADJACENCY, TLD lists, ATTACK_WORDS, homoglyphs, phonetic/leet maps).
- **`similarity.py`** — `SimilarityCalculator` compositing rapidfuzz Levenshtein ratio with Unicode skeleton comparison via `CONFUSABLE_MAP` (Cyrillic/Greek↔Latin); `score = max(lev_ratio, skeleton_ratio)`. Falls back to pure-Python edit distance if rapidfuzz unavailable.
- **`trusted_domains.py`** — `TrustedDomainMatcher` with `exact` / `wildcard` (`*.domain.tld`) / `suffix` match types and expiry-aware filtering.
- **`threat_scorer.py`** — `ThreatScorer` with 20 weighted signals (DNS presence, MX, HTTP activity, brand/phishing keywords in title, SSL type/age, domain age, WHOIS privacy, GeoIP risk, similarity magnitude, Levenshtein-1, IDN flag) → `threat_score` 0–100, `severity` 1–5.

## API (`app/api/lookalike.py`) — 14 endpoints
| Method | Path | Purpose |
|--------|------|---------|
| GET/POST | `/rules` | List / create rules |
| GET/PATCH/DELETE | `/rules/{id}` | Rule detail (with status counts) / update / delete+cascade |
| POST | `/rules/{id}/scan` | SSE stream: generate → filter → DNS/HTTP probe → threat score → upsert |
| POST | `/rules/{id}/preview` | Dry-run counts with optional `simulate_threshold` |
| GET | `/rules/{id}/domains` | Paginated domain list; filterable by `status`, `min_threat_score`, `severity` |
| GET/PATCH | `/domains/{id}` | Domain detail / mark false-positive or update status |
| GET | `/rules/{id}/domains/export` | CSV or JSON bulk export |
| GET/POST/DELETE | `/rules/{id}/trusted[/{tid}]` | Trusted-domain registry CRUD |

SSE scan stream format:
```
data: {"fqdn": "kyivztar.ua", "status": "registered", "threat_score": 62, "checked": 14, "total": 847}

event: done
data: {"total": 847, "registered": 23, "trusted": 4, "unregistered": 820}
```

## Wiring
- `app/main.py`: router imported and mounted at `/api/v1/lookalike/`
- `requirements.txt`: `rapidfuzz>=3.6.0` added

## Overview

Implement the **Look-alike Domains — Brand Protection** module as specified in `TS_LookalikeDomains_v1.1.md` (TS-LAD-001 v1.1). The existing codebase uses **FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + SQLite (aiosqlite) + APScheduler** — implement against this stack, not Flask/PostgreSQL/Celery.

The existing brand protection code (`app/api/brand_protection.py`, `app/services/domain_checker.py`) provides basic 5-algorithm typosquat generation and should remain intact. The new module lives under a separate namespace (`/api/v1/lookalike/`) and a new service directory (`app/services/lookalike/`).

---

## 1. New ORM Models — `app/models.py`

Add these models **at the end** of the existing `app/models.py`. Do not alter existing models.

### `LookalikeRule`
Per-brand monitoring rule (replaces the concept of "ProtectionRule" from the spec).

```python
class LookalikeRule(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lookalike_rules"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    brand_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("brands.id"), nullable=False)
    name = Column(String(200), nullable=False)
    protected_domain = Column(String(253), nullable=False)   # e.g. "kyivstar.ua"
    brand_terms = Column(Text, default="[]")                 # JSON list of terms
    # Generation config
    algorithms = Column(Text, default="[]")                  # JSON list; empty = all
    tld_list = Column(String(20), default="top100")          # top30|top100|top500|full1500
    attack_words = Column(String(20), default="core")        # core|extended
    include_idn = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    include_bitsquatting = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    max_variants = Column(Integer, default=10000)
    similarity_threshold_pct = Column(Integer, default=70)   # 30–100 §6.5
    # State
    active = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    last_scan_at = Column(DateTime, nullable=True)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=_utcnow)
    updated_at = Column(DateTime, default=_utcnow, onupdate=_utcnow)
    # Relationships
    domains = relationship("LookalikeDomain", back_populates="rule", cascade="all, delete-orphan")
    trusted_domains = relationship("RuleTrustedDomain", back_populates="rule", cascade="all, delete-orphan")
```

### `LookalikeDomain`
One row per generated+checked variant domain.

```python
class LookalikeDomain(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lookalike_domains"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    rule_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("lookalike_rules.id"), nullable=False)
    fqdn = Column(String(253), nullable=False)
    label = Column(String(63), nullable=False)              # part before TLD
    tld = Column(String(63), nullable=False)
    algorithms = Column(Text, default="[]")                 # JSON list of alg IDs
    levenshtein_distance = Column(Integer, nullable=True)
    similarity_score = Column(Float, nullable=True)         # 0.0–1.0 composite score from §6.5.2
    is_idn = Column(Boolean, default=False)
    unicode_form = Column(String(253), nullable=True)
    # Status
    status = Column(String(20), default="unregistered")     # unregistered|registered|trusted|error
    # DNS
    dns_checked_at = Column(DateTime, nullable=True)
    has_a_record = Column(Boolean, nullable=True)
    has_mx_record = Column(Boolean, nullable=True)
    has_ns_record = Column(Boolean, nullable=True)
    ip = Column(String(64), nullable=True)
    # HTTP
    http_status = Column(Integer, nullable=True)
    page_title = Column(String(512), nullable=True)
    final_url = Column(String(2048), nullable=True)
    server_header = Column(String(256), nullable=True)
    redirect_detected = Column(Boolean, nullable=True)
    redirects_to_legitimate = Column(Boolean, nullable=True)
    brand_in_title = Column(Boolean, nullable=True)
    phishing_keywords_in_title = Column(Boolean, nullable=True)
    # SSL
    ssl_valid = Column(Boolean, nullable=True)
    ssl_issuer = Column(String(256), nullable=True)

author: yassirar77-cloud
body:
## Problem

Digest delivery 400'd: *"can't find end of the entity"*. Root cause (you diagnosed it): the escape logic used MarkdownV2-style backslash escapes (`\_`) but `parse_mode` was legacy `"Markdown"`, which doesn't recognise `\_` — so `(protein_seafood)` opened an italic run Telegram couldn't close.

## Fix — switch to HTML parse mode (your recommendation)

- **`<b>` headers, `<i>` footer**, and escape only **`& < >`** in dynamic strings (`_html`). No more escaping periods/parens/dashes — they're safe in HTML.
- **Reworded static text that contained `<`/`>`** so the HTML parser doesn't choke on *them*: `confidence below 60` (was `<60`), `(over 10%)` (was `(>10%)`), `total over RM5,000` (was `>RM5,000`). A regression test strips the allowed tags and asserts **no bare `<`/`>` remain** — this is the class of bug that caused the failure, now guarded.
- **Plain-text fallback:** both the cron and `/test_digest` try `HTML`, then retry the same message with **no parse_mode** on any failure → always delivers (formatting lost on fallback, noted in `digest_log.error_msg`). `parse_mode_attempts()` = `["HTML", None]`.
- **`--plain`** flag (script) and **`/test_digest plain`** force plain text outright.

## Also addressed (from your test-output notes)

- **Zero-spend items excluded:** `aggregate_items`/`aggregate_suppliers` now keep only `0 < amount <= 5000`, so `asam jawa drink` / `extra joss` / `ikan` at RM0.00 stop ranking in the top 5.
- **`message_bytes` column** (migration **0014**) records UTF-8 byte length next to char length (the failure was at byte offset 1999 on an 1874-char message). `log_digest` retries without the column if 0014 isn't applied yet, and the **full message text is always logged** for diagnosis.
- **Today vs this-week inconsistency** (suppliers "today" strict vs outlets "this week" window): documented in a code comment — expected, not a bug.

author: sundram-bruno
body:
### Description

The OpenAPI exporter (`packages/bruno-app/src/utils/exporters/openapi-spec.js`) calls `.length` on `auth.oauth2.scope` without a null guard. When a user never fills the Scope field for an OAuth2 auth, Bruno stores `scope` as `null`, causing the entire export to crash with:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length')
```

Affected grant types: `authorization_code`, `password`, `client_credentials`. A single offending request aborts the entire export — users with OAuth2-secured APIs can't get an OpenAPI export at all.

**Linked issue:** [#7365](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/7365). 
JIRA : https://usebruno.atlassian.net/browse/BRU-3297

#### Changes

- Replace `scope.length > 0 ? { scopes: { [scope]: '' } } : {}` ternary in all 3 grant cases with a single hoisted `const scopes = scope ? { [scope]: '' } : {}`. Truthy check handles `null`, `undefined`, and `""` uniformly.
- Emit `scopes` unconditionally on each flow. OpenAPI 3.0 requires `scopes` to be present on every OAuth2 flow even when empty.
- Wrap `case 'oauth2'` in a block to scope the new `const` declarations (resolves Biome `noSwitchDeclarations`).
- Add 12 jest tests covering all 3 affected grant types.

#### Test plan

- `npm run test --workspace=packages/bruno-app -- openapi-spec` — 29/29 pass (12 new + 17 existing)
- Bug reproduced in installed Bruno 3.1.x via Share → OpenAPI Specification — identical stack trace confirmed (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length')` at `Array.map`)

#### Contribution Checklist:

- [x] **I've used AI significantly to create this pull request**
- [x] **The pull request only addresses one issue or adds one feature.**
- [x] **The pull request does not introduce any breaking changes**
- [ ] **I have added screenshots or gifs to help explain the change if applicable.**
- [x] **I have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/blob/main/contributing.md).**
- [x] **Create an issue and link to the pull request.** (linked: #7365)

#### Screenshot

Production crash on installed Bruno 3.1.x exporting a collection with OAuth2 auth + blank scope:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length')
  at file:///Applications/Bruno.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar/web/static/js/index.a442c869.js:45:21358
  at Array.map (<anonymous>)
  ...
```

Stack `Array.map` corresponds to `items.map(...)` at `openapi-spec.js:133`, inside which the `scope.length` runs in the OAuth2 case.

author: haludi
body:
### Issue link

https://issues.hibernatingrhinos.com/issue/RavenDB-26694

### Additional description
When a periodic backup is running and its configuration is updated mid-flight with a backup type change (e.g. Full/Incremental → Snapshot), UpdateConfigurations deliberately sets existingBackupState.BackupStatus = null to clear stale
  status before scheduling a fresh full backup.
  
  Concurrently, the running backup can receive an OperationCanceledException through several paths:
  - The task is disabled in a config update → DisableFutureBackups() cancels the token
  - A timer fires while the task is no longer active on the current node (reassigned to another node or missing responsible node) → DisableFutureBackups() cancels the token
  - The database shuts down → the runner's cancellation token is canceled

  When both happen at the same time — BackupStatus is null and the backup receives an OperationCanceledException — the catch block tried to read periodicBackup.BackupStatus.TaskId, resulting in a NullReferenceException that crashed the
  server.

  Two fixes in PeriodicBackupRunner.RunBackupThread:
  1. Use periodicBackup.Configuration.TaskId instead of periodicBackup.BackupStatus.TaskId — Configuration is always populated; BackupStatus can be null after a type change.
  2. Add null-conditional operators when copying DelayUntil and OriginalBackupTime from the in-memory entry, since that entry's BackupStatus can equally be null.

author: bartok9
body:
## Summary

Fixes #86373.

The embedded compaction target resolver (`resolveEmbeddedCompactionTarget`) was missing the OpenAI/Codex OAuth routing that the main run path applies via `resolveSelectedOpenAIPiRuntimeProvider`. When a session uses `provider=openai` with an `openai-codex:*` auth profile, the main path normalises the runtime provider to `openai-codex`; the compaction fallback path skipped that step entirely and returned the raw caller provider.

That mismatch caused embedded compaction (and the context-engine fallback) to hit the plain OpenAI API-key path and fail with:

```
codex app-server compaction could not use thread binding
...
No_API_key_found_for_provider_openai
```

## Root Cause

```ts
// Before — no-override path returned raw provider unchanged
if (!override) {
  return {
    provider,       // <-- could be "openai" even when session uses Codex OAuth
    model,
    authProfileId: params.authProfileId ?? undefined,
  };
}
```

The main run path correctly calls:
```ts
const selectedPiRuntimeProvider = resolveSelectedOpenAIPiRuntimeProvider({
  provider,
  harnessRuntime: agentHarness.id,
  authProfileProvider: params.authProfileId?.split(":", 1)[0],
  authProfileId: params.authProfileId,
  config: params.config,
  workspaceDir: resolvedWorkspace,
});
```

## Fix

Apply `resolveSelectedOpenAIPiRuntimeProvider` in the no-override branch of `resolveEmbeddedCompactionTarget` so the same Codex OAuth routing is used for both the main turn and all compaction/context-engine fallback paths.

```ts
// After
if (!override) {
  const runtimeProvider =
    provider != null
      ? resolveSelectedOpenAIPiRuntimeProvider({
          provider,
          harnessRuntime: "pi",
          authProfileProvider: params.authProfileId?.split(":", 1)[0],
          authProfileId: params.authProfileId ?? undefined,
          config: params.config,
        })
      : provider;
  return {
    provider: runtimeProvider || provider,
    model,
    authProfileId: params.authProfileId ?? undefined,
  };
}
```

## Affected paths (per issue analysis)

- `compactEmbeddedPiSessionDirect` → calls `resolveEmbeddedCompactionTarget` ✅ fixed
- queued/manual `compactEmbeddedPiSession` → calls `resolveEmbeddedCompactionTarget` + `buildEmbeddedCompactionRuntimeContext` ✅ fixed
- timeout/overflow compaction in `run.ts` → calls `buildEmbeddedCompactionRuntimeContext` ✅ fixed
- after-turn context-engine hooks → call `buildAfterTurnRuntimeContext` → `buildEmbeddedCompactionRuntimeContext` ✅ fixed

## Real behavior proof

### Before

Sessions with `provider=openai` + `authProfileId=openai-codex:work` would hit the plain OpenAI API key path during compaction, producing `No_API_key_found_for_provider_openai` even though the active session used Codex OAuth.

### After

The no-override compaction path routes through `resolveSelectedOpenAIPiRuntimeProvider`, matching the main run path. New regression test confirms the provider is normalised to `openai-codex`:

```
✓ routes OpenAI Codex OAuth compaction fallback through the Codex provider (#86373)
✓ does not reroute non-OpenAI compaction providers (#86373)
✓ ...all 10 existing compaction-runtime-context tests pass
```

```
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       20 passed (20)
```

## Verification

```bash
pnpm vitest run src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/compaction-runtime-context.test.ts
```

```
✓ agents-core  compaction-runtime-context.test.ts (10 tests) 178ms
✓ agents-pi-embedded  compaction-runtime-context.test.ts (10 tests) 153ms
Test Files  2 passed (2)  Tests  20 passed (20)
```

## Summary
This PR introduces a comprehensive fact-checking system for WoW Classic fishing knowledge, consisting of authoritative reference data, a test suite for grader accuracy, and integration with the main benchmark grader.

## Key Changes

### New Files
- **`wow_reference.yaml`** — Authoritative reference data for WoW Classic (patch 1.12) fishing facts
  - 359 lines covering cooking recipes, fish, zones, vendors, items, gold estimates, and known hallucinations
  - Serves as ground truth for fact-checking claims about ingredients, buffs, locations, and mechanics
  - Includes a "common hallucinations" section documenting known LLM errors (e.g., wrong buff stats, fake locations)

- **`test_grader.py`** — Standalone test harness for validating grader accuracy
  - Loads reference data and test claims, evaluates them against the grader
  - Targets ≥95% accuracy on all test claims
  - Supports multiple models/providers and configurable thresholds
  - Provides per-category breakdown and detailed failure reporting

- **`test_claims.yaml`** — 230 test claims covering all major fishing topics
  - Organized by category: recipe ingredients, buff stats, fish timing, zones, fake locations, vendors, gold estimates, game mechanics
  - Mix of true and false claims to validate both positive and negative grading

### Modified Files
- **`haakonbench.py`** — Integrated reference data into the main grader
  - Added `load_reference_data()` function to load and format `wow_reference.yaml`
  - Updated `GRADER_SYSTEM` template to include reference data in the system prompt
  - Added `_format_reference_data()` helper to convert YAML into readable markdown for the LLM
  - Modified `grade_run()` signature to accept optional grader provider/model parameters
  - Grader now uses verified reference data as ground truth instead of relying on its own knowledge

## Implementation Details

- **Reference data format**: YAML with structured sections for recipes, fish, zones, vendors, items, and known errors
- **Grader integration**: Reference data is injected into the system prompt as a "Verified Reference Data" section, with explicit instructions to use only this data for fact-checking
- **Graceful degradation**: If `wow_reference.yaml` is missing, the grader continues to work with a warning (uses its own knowledge)
- **Test harness**: Async evaluation of claims with verdict parsing, supports verbose output and custom accuracy thresholds
- **Common hallucinations tracking**: Explicit list of known LLM errors (e.g., "Nightfin Soup requires Soothing Spices" → FALSE) to help the grader avoid repeating them

## Testing
Run the test suite with:
```bash
python test_grader.py
python test_grader.py --model claude-opus-4-7 --threshold 0.90 --verbose
```

The grader will now fact-check WoW Classic claims against the verified reference data rather than relying on potentially incorrect training knowledge.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Adds **real** MPEG-1/2 Layer III playback support to `AudioQueue` (no stubs). BlockPuzzle (and likely any app that hands an MP3 ASBD to `AudioQueueNewOutput`) was hitting:

```
AudioQueueStart: Unsupported format AudioStreamBasicDescription {
    format_id: "'.mp3'", frames_per_packet: 1152,
    channels_per_frame: 2, ... }, not starting
```

…because `AudioQueue::is_supported_audio_format` / `decode_buffer` only knew about `kAudioFormatLinearPCM` and `kAudioFormatAppleIMA4`.

Implementation (entirely backed by existing symphonia decoders):

1. **`core_audio_types.rs`** — add the missing `kAudioFormatMPEGLayer3` constant. Apple defines it as FourCC `'.mp3'` in `<CoreAudio/CoreAudioTypes.h>` (see <https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreaudiotypes/kaudioformatmpeglayer3>).
2. **`is_supported_audio_format`** — accept `kAudioFormatMPEGLayer3` for mono / stereo. Per Apple, MP3 is compressed so `bytes_per_packet`, `bytes_per_frame` and `bits_per_channel` are conventionally 0; only the channel count is required.
3. **`log_if_broken_audio_format`** — skip the PCM-shape sanity check for MP3 so we don't spam "non-sensical values" on every valid MP3 ASBD.
4. **`decode_buffer`** — add an MP3 branch that decodes each enqueued buffer through the existing `audio::symphonia_formats::decode_symphonia_to_pcm` helper (already used for AudioFile/ExtAudioFile MP3 sources). Promoted the `symphonia_formats` submodule from private `mod` to `pub mod` so `audio_toolbox` can reach it.

MP3 packets in `AudioQueueEnqueueBuffer` are typically frame-aligned (that is the contract of `AudioFileStreamParseBytes` / `AudioFileReadPackets`), so feeding the slice as a raw MP3 stream to symphonia works in practice. Partial frames at buffer boundaries are dropped by symphonia's recoverable decode-error path, which is far better than letting `AudioQueueStart` outright refuse to start the queue.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Confirm BlockPuzzle (or whichever MP3-using app you have on hand) actually plays audio after this change, not just stops printing the "Unsupported format" warning.
- [ ] Verify that apps already using LinearPCM / IMA4 audio queues still play correctly (regression check); this PR doesn't touch those code paths but they share the same `decode_buffer` dispatch.
- [ ] Inspect the symphonia output for any MP3 streams that produce >2 channels — those will be downmixed to mono with a warning. If you encounter a real app that does this, we may want to add a real downmix instead of dropping channels.

### Notes

- The PR only adds an `MPEGLayer3` decode branch; the existing handler for `kAudioFormatMPEG4AAC` (AAC) in the AudioQueue path is unchanged — symphonia already supports AAC in `decode_symphonia_to_pcm`, so a follow-up PR can wire that up with one extra match arm if any app needs it.
- Each enqueued buffer is decoded independently. If you encounter an app that splits a single MP3 frame across two `AudioQueueEnqueueBuffer` calls, we'd need a stateful per-queue decoder; we can layer that on if such an app shows up.

author: ericcogen
body:
# 19 - Architectural Access Control Drop (Security Regression)

**Expected verdict:** 🔴 CRITICAL - GauntletCI should flag removal of `[Authorize]` attribute.

## What changed
A legacy billing controller endpoint is being refactored to use a clean `MediatR` messaging pipeline. During the conversion, the `[Authorize(Roles = "BillingAdmin")]` attribute is accidentally stripped from the `ProcessRefund` method.

**File:** `src/OrderService/Billing/BillingController.cs`

- **Baseline (main):** Method is decorated with `[Authorize(Roles = "BillingAdmin")]`
- **Inbound PR:** Authorization attribute completely removed during refactoring
- **No compilation error:** The code compiles cleanly; no unit test catches this because the test still mocks the service.

## Why GauntletCI catches this

Traditional tools miss this because:
- **SonarQube:** Snapshot metrics don't detect attribute removal (no syntax violation)
- **StyleCop/Roslyn:** Don't enforce security attribute presence
- **CodeQL:** Doesn't track structural authorization mutations in diffs
- **Unit tests:** Still pass because the refactored method executes the business logic; test setup doesn't verify authorization

**GauntletCI detection:** Compares `IMethodSymbol` models between baseline and PR compilation contexts. The `ProcessRefund` method loses an `AuthorizeAttribute` sub-type with no fallback class-level or handler-level authorization mapping.

**Rule:** Behavioral Change Detection (GCI0003) - Structural mutation of security-critical attributes.

## Risk

A public HTTP endpoint that previously required `BillingAdmin` role is now accessible to any authenticated (or unauthenticated) user. This is a critical security regression that would go undetected in production until exploited.

## Test Coverage

- Integration test validates that unauthorized callers receive 403 Forbidden on baseline
- Same test FAILS on PR code (endpoint returns 200 OK to unauthorized users)

author: ericcogen
body:
# 20 - Failure-Path Audit Log Inversion (CFG Mutation)

**Expected verdict:** 🔴 HIGH - GauntletCI should flag control flow reordering where audit logging bypasses exception paths.

## What changed
An order fulfillment coordinator method is being performance-optimized. The developer moves the audit logging invocation from the start of the method to the end, to minimize response delays. However, this creates a critical behavioral regression: if the core fulfillment engine throws an unhandled exception, the audit log is never recorded—breaking compliance requirements.

**File:** `src/OrderService/Fulfillment/Services/FulfillmentCoordinator.cs`

- **Baseline (main):** Audit logging happens BEFORE `ProcessAsync` is called
- **Inbound PR:** Audit logging moved AFTER `ProcessAsync` is called
- **Silent failure:** The code compiles cleanly; exceptions still bubble up; but the audit trail is lost

## Why GauntletCI catches this

Traditional tools miss this because:
- **SonarQube:** Reordering statements is not a code smell (no violation flagged)
- **CodeQL:** Doesn't track execution sequence mutations or compliance-critical code ordering
- **Unit tests:** Still pass if they don't simulate exceptions in `ProcessAsync`
- **Linters:** See no syntax violations

**GauntletCI detection:** Runs `ControlFlowAnalysis` on both method bodies. Baseline shows `LogActionAsync -> ProcessAsync` edge flow. PR shows `ProcessAsync -> LogActionAsync` edge flow. This is flagged as an un-synchronized sequence regression that violates control-flow integrity.

author: sentry[bot]
body:
This PR addresses the `KeyError: 'secretsmanager'` occurring in `ddpui/utils/aws_client.py`.

**Problem:**
The `AWSClient._get_client` method was susceptible to a `KeyError` when multiple concurrent requests attempted to initialize an AWS client (e.g., 'secretsmanager'). The `_clients` dictionary was initialized as empty. If a thread failed to acquire the service-specific lock within the 10-second timeout, it would proceed to access `cls._clients[service_name]` without `service_name` being guaranteed to exist in the dictionary, leading to a `KeyError`.

**Solution:**
1.  **Pre-initialize `_clients`:** The `_clients` class variable is now initialized with `None` values for all `SUPPORTED_SERVICES`. This ensures that all expected service keys are present in the dictionary from the start, preventing `KeyError` when attempting to access `cls._clients[service_name]`.
2.  **Fail fast on lock timeout:** If `threading.Lock().acquire()` times out, a `RuntimeError` is now explicitly raised. This prevents the execution from proceeding with an uninitialized client and provides clearer error messaging.
3.  **Update `reset_instance`:** The `reset_instance` method now also re-initializes `_clients` with `None` values for all supported services, maintaining consistency with the class's initial state.

Fixes DALGO-BACKEND-2AJ

author: ericcogen
body:
# 21 - Unsynchronized Static State Mutation in Async Flow (Concurrency Regression)

**Expected verdict:** 🔴 CRITICAL - GauntletCI should flag unsynchronized static field mutation inside async method.

## What changed
A telemetry counter is being added to track shipment processing. The developer introduces a static field `_globalShipmentCount` and increments it at the start of the `HandleAsync` method. The code compiles perfectly and single-threaded tests pass. However, under multi-threaded asynchronous load, the counter experiences lost increments due to race conditions.

**File:** `src/OrderService/Telemetry/Handlers/ShipmentHandler.cs`

- **Baseline (main):** No shared mutable state
- **Inbound PR:** Introduces `private static int _globalShipmentCount = 0`
- **Mutation:** Bare `_globalShipmentCount++` without synchronization
- **Context:** Inside an async `Task` method with no synchronization wrapper

## Why GauntletCI catches this

Traditional tools miss this because:
- **SonarQube:** Static fields are common; doesn't flag unsynchronized mutation without explicit linting rules
- **StyleCop:** Allows static fields; mutation inside async methods is not flagged
- **Roslyn Analyzers:** Generic rules don't detect this concurrency anti-pattern
- **Unit tests:** Pass because tests are single-threaded; race condition doesn't manifest
- **Compiler:** Compiles cleanly (no type safety violation)

**GauntletCI detection:** Analyzes `IIncrementExpressionOperation` targeting an `IFieldSymbol` with `IsStatic = true`. Because the operation resides inside a method returning `Task` without a corresponding `Interlocked.Increment` or thread-safe wrapper, a race condition warning is raised.

**Rule:** Behavioral Change Detection (GCI0003) - Unsafe concurrency pattern introduced.

## Risk

Under production load with multiple concurrent requests, the telemetry counter will lose increments. This manifests as silent data corruption in metrics, making observability unreliable and masking operational issues.

## Test Coverage

- Single-threaded unit test PASSES on both baseline and PR (doesn't catch the issue)
- Concurrent integration test with 100 parallel tasks:
  - **Baseline:** Telemetry counter is 0 (no state to corrupt)
  - **PR:** Expected count = 100, actual count < 100 (lost increments due to race condition)

- Atmos currently uses go-git v5, so this branch keeps a narrow local compatibility shim for `extensions.worktreeConfig` until the dependency path can rely on upstream support.

author: ericcogen
body:
# 22 - Breaking Public Package Contract (No Version Bump)

**Expected verdict:** 🔴 CRITICAL - GauntletCI should flag removal of public API parameter without major version increment.

## What changed
An enterprise notification integration framework interface is being simplified. The developer removes the `CancellationToken` parameter from the public `BroadcastAsync` method. The code compiles cleanly in the local monorepo because all consumers are updated. However, this creates a breaking change for external downstream consumers who have taken a dependency on the NuGet package—their implementations implementing the old interface signature will fail at runtime when called with the new package version.

**File:** `src/OrderService/Contracts/Interfaces/INotificationDispatcher.cs`

- **Baseline (main):** `Task BroadcastAsync(string headline, string payload, CancellationToken ct = default)`
- **Inbound PR:** `Task BroadcastAsync(string headline, string payload)` (parameter removed)
- **Version:** No major version increment in `.csproj` (still 1.x)

## Why GauntletCI catches this

Traditional tools miss this because:
- **SonarQube:** Interface simplification is not a violation
- **CodeQL:** Doesn't track semantic versioning vs API contract changes
- **Compilation:** Internal monorepo compiles because all consumers are updated
- **NuGet publish:** Will publish successfully; breaking change only surfaces when external consumers upgrade

**GauntletCI detection:** Extracts public API contracts via Roslyn symbol comparison. The inbound PR shows a structural contraction of `INotificationDispatcher.BroadcastAsync` parameter list. Package metadata (`.csproj` version) does not indicate a major release increment (e.g., 1.0.0 → 2.0.0), violating semantic versioning rules for public APIs.

**Rule:** Breaking Changes Detection (GCI0012) - Public API structural mutation without version bump.

## Risk

External packages consuming this as a NuGet dependency will break when they upgrade to the new version. Implementation classes that implement the old signature will no longer match the interface definition, causing runtime binding errors. This is silent in CI but catastrophic for consumers in production.

## Test Coverage

- Unit test validates interface contract on baseline (PASS)
- External consumer simulation test:
  - **Baseline:** Calling `BroadcastAsync(headline, payload, cancellationToken)` works
  - **PR:** Same call fails with method signature mismatch (no such overload exists)

author: uqio
body:
## Summary

Replaces the flat `SubtitleCue { range, text, language, confidence, raw_payload }` wire message with a polymorphic shape mirroring the domain `SubtitleCue<Id, D>`. Adds a complete buffa bridge for the new shape plus all 5 per-track sibling aggregates.

## Wire shape

- `kind` (closed `SubtitleCueKind`) + `data` oneof carrying the per-format payload (`SrtData` / `VttData` / `AssData` / `LrcData`).
- PTS only on the wire (`span_start_pts` / `span_end_pts`) — timebase lives on the parent `SubtitleTrack` per the timebase-dedup rule; decoder takes an explicit `parent_timebase` (default-timebase convenience constructor also provided).
- 13-arm `SubtitleCueKind` enum stable from day one (1:1 with the domain `repr(u8)`: Srt=0, …, EbuStl=12); reserved discriminants decode to `BuffaError::UnimplementedSubtitleCueKind` (tracked under #56).

## New wire messages

- Per-format payload: `SrtData` (unit marker), `VttData`, `AssData`, `LrcData`.
- Per-track aggregates: `VttRegion`, `VttStyleBlock`, `AssStyle`, `LrcMetadata`.
- Child of LRC cue: `LrcWord`.
- Four VTT cue-setting enums: `VttVertical`, `VttLineAlign`, `VttPositionAlign`, `VttTextAlign`.

## Domain additions

- `SubtitleCueDetails<Id>` — runtime-tagged union over every implemented payload (`Srt` / `Vtt` / `Ass` / `Lrc`), used by `SubtitleCue<Id, SubtitleCueDetails<Id>>` as the polymorphic decode landing point.

## Buffa bridge (`src/buffa/subtitle.rs`)

- Per-format infallible `From<&SrtCue/VttCue/AssCue/LrcCue> for wire::SubtitleCue`.
- `From<&SubtitleCue<Uuid7, SubtitleCueDetails<Uuid7>>> for wire::SubtitleCue`.
- `subtitle_cue_from_wire(w, parent_timebase)` — fallible decode; validates ids, span, dispatches kind ↔ data oneof match.
- Convenience `TryFrom<&wire::SubtitleCue>` using `1/1000` timebase.
- All five sibling aggregates round-trip 1:1.
- New error variants: `UnimplementedSubtitleCueKind(i32)`, `MissingSubtitleCueData(kind_name)`, `SubtitleCueKindOneofMismatch(kind, data)`, `SubtitleNumericOutOfRange(field, value)`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --all-features` clean
- [x] `cargo test --all-features` — 634 lib tests + 58 roundtrip + 5 subtitle_completion all pass
- [x] +16 new buffa::subtitle tests (per-format round-trip; sibling-aggregate round-trip; kind/oneof mismatch; missing oneof; reserved kind; polymorphic encode dispatch; default-timebase TryFrom)
