author: frenchie4111
body:
## Summary

An Electron Harness client built after v2.9.3 crashes the renderer when it connects to a remote `harness-server` running v2.9.3 or older:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'find')
  at findCustom (useActiveTheme.ts)
  at resolveTheme
  at useActiveTheme
```

**Repro.** Commit `99262b2` (light/dark/system theme mode + custom themes from disk, 2026-05-22) added `customThemes: CustomTheme[]` to `SettingsState`. v2.9.3 was released the day before (2026-05-21), so its snapshot's `settings` object has no `customThemes`. The renderer's `setSnapshot` did a **top-level shallow merge** (`{...initialState, ...state}`) — that only protects against entirely-missing slices. Because the v2.9.3 server *does* send `settings`, the merge wholesale replaced `initialState.settings` (including the `customThemes: []` default) with the partial wire object, and `useActiveTheme` → `resolveTheme` → `findCustom(...customs.find)` blew up on `undefined`.

## The fix

- **Per-slice merge.** New shared helper `mergeWireSnapshot(state)` in `src/shared/state/index.ts` walks every slice and merges `{ ...initialState[slice], ...state[slice] }`. Fixes both skew cases — missing slice *and* missing field inside a slice — uniformly.
- **Type the wire boundary.** New `WireSnapshotState = { [K in keyof AppState]?: Partial<AppState[K]> }` is what `setSnapshot` now accepts. Stops the wire boundary from lying about completeness. `StateSnapshot.state` stays as `AppState` because the *sender* (main process) genuinely produces a full shape; the structural-subtype path lets existing `setSnapshot(snapshot.state)` callers keep working without churn.
- **Bonus compile-time guard.** `mergeWireSnapshot` returns `AppState`, so any future PR that adds a slice to `AppState`/`initialState` and forgets to add a line to the merge function gets a TypeScript build failure (the merge object literal won't satisfy `AppState`). Same forced-update story as adding to `initialState`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npx electron-vite build`
- [x] `npx vitest run src/shared src/renderer` — 634 tests pass, including 4 new ones in `src/shared/state/wire-merge.test.ts` covering: (1) old server missing `customThemes`, (2) old server missing entire slice, (3) full snapshot pass-through, (4) explicit empty array from mid-version server.
- [ ] Manual: launch Electron Harness from this branch, add a v2.9.3 remote backend, confirm the chip activates without the `findCustom` crash.

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The `envsubst '${PORT}'` call in `docker-entrypoint.sh` was silently failing to substitute the `${PORT}` placeholder in the nginx config, leaving nginx with a literal `listen ${PORT};` directive. Nginx cannot bind to that, so external traffic gets a 502 while the localhost healthcheck still passes (it probes a port that happens to be open from a previous default binding).

## Solution

Replaced the `envsubst` call for PORT with `sed -i "s/\${PORT}/${PORT}/g"`, which performs an in-place substitution directly on the config file without relying on the variable being exported into the `envsubst` environment. The `VITE_BACKEND_URL` substitution is unchanged since it uses the safe `< input > output` redirect pattern. With this fix nginx correctly renders `listen 80;` at startup and binds to port 80 for external traffic.

### Changes
- **Modified** `frontend/docker-entrypoint.sh`

author: rxbynerd
body:
Completes issue #222 by adding the three reliability controls Waves 2–5 left unbuilt: **parallel-tool-call policy**, **input examples**, and **tool annotations**. (Tool-choice, strict mode, and structured results already shipped via #230/#228/#231 through other channels.)

## Design
- `types.ToolDefinition` gains a `Presentation *ToolPresentation` neighbour carried as `json:"-"`, so the nil zero value is byte-identical to the pre-#222 wire shape on every adapter — critical because the Anthropic adapter serialises `ToolDefinition` verbatim. `ToolPresentation` holds `InputExamples` and MCP-style `Annotations`.
- `StreamParams.ParallelToolCalls *bool` (nil = omit, mirroring `Temperature`).
- Two cross-provider quirks capabilities: `ParallelToolCallsCapability` and `ToolExamplesCapability`, gated per (provider, model) like the existing tool-choice/structured-result capabilities.

## Per-provider wire mapping
- **OpenAI Chat / Responses**: top-level `parallel_tool_calls`; examples folded into the JSON-Schema `examples` keyword **only for non-strict tools** (the structured-outputs subset rejects `examples`). Responses gains parallel + examples support (it previously had no tool_choice/parallel wiring).
- **Anthropic**: parallel-disable rides on a synthesised `tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use`; examples fold into `input_schema`.
- **Gemini / Bedrock**: deliberate no-op (no native control; Gemini's dialect rejects `examples`, so the #227 description text remains the carrier).
- **MCP**: server-declared annotations are now parsed and carried (advisory only — the conservative WorkspaceMutating/RequiresApproval gating still governs).

Built-in tool examples migrated from inline description text to structured `InputExamples`, pinned byte-for-byte to the descriptions by drift-guard tests. Contract tests cover every adapter; `provider-quirks.md` documents the per-provider matrix. `just test` + `just lint` green; the offline tool-use replay gate passes.

Closes #222.

author: prajwolrg
body:
## Description

Drops the `#[async_trait(?Send)]` opt-out on `ZkVmRemoteProver` so the futures returned by `start_proving` / `get_status` / `get_proof` are `Send`.

**Why:** downstream consumers that drive multiple proof workers want to `tokio::spawn` these futures directly on a multi-threaded runtime. With `?Send`, they're forced into a `LocalSet` + dedicated-thread wrapper just to co-host two `!Send` workers, which is purely an artifact of this trait bound rather than anything the impls actually require.

Both in-tree impls (`NativeHost`, `SP1Host`) were already `Send`-clean — neither holds an `Rc`/`RefCell` across `.await`, and the SP1 SDK client is built for multi-threaded use. Only the trait/impl attributes change; no impl bodies are touched. `cargo check --all-features` on `zkaleido`, `zkaleido-native-adapter`, and `zkaleido-sp1-host` is clean.

### Type of Change

- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Refactor

## Notes to Reviewers

The breaking change is for **external** `ZkVmRemoteProver` impls only: they must now keep their state `Send` across `.await` (no `Rc`/`RefCell`/raw pointers in scope at suspension points). For impls backed by a typical async HTTP / RPC client this is already the case.

In-repo impact is just the attribute change on the two impls — see the diff.

author: micalevisk
body:
# Type-narrow workflow state + make module global

Improves the public type surface of `@duraflows/core` and `@duraflows/nestjs` so consumers with a typed `WorkflowDefinition` can drop `as` assertions on `currentState`, `fromState`, and `toState`. Also marks `WorkflowModule` as global so downstream feature modules can inject `WorkflowService` without re-importing the dynamic module. Bundled with a minor dep bump.

All changes are **backwards compatible**: every new generic parameter has a `string` default, and the new methods are additive.

Origin: ported from a vendored copy of `@duraflows/*` v1.1.0 used in a internal project. Each commit here has a 1-to-1 mapping to the corresponding vendored commit referenced in the body.

## Summary

- **`feat(nestjs): mark WorkflowModule as global`** — `forRoot` / `forRootAsync` now return `{ global: true, ... }`. Downstream feature modules can inject `WorkflowService` (and other exported tokens) without re-importing the dynamic module.
- **`feat(core,nestjs): generic TState on definition + createInstanceFor`** — parametrises `WorkflowDefinition`, `WorkflowStateDefinition`, `WorkflowEventDefinition`, `WorkflowOnEnterDefinition`, and `WorkflowInstance` over `TState extends string = string`. Adds `WorkflowService.createInstanceFor<TState>(definition, input)` — derives `workflowName` from the definition and narrows the returned instance's `currentState` to `TState`.
- **`feat(core,nestjs): generic TState on result + triggerEventFor`** — parametrises `WorkflowExecutionResult` over `TState`. Adds `WorkflowService.triggerEventFor<TState>(definition, input)` — narrows the result's `fromState` / `toState` to the definition's state union. Lets callers use the existing `outcome` discriminator and stop comparing `toState !== EXPECTED`.
- **`chore(deps): bump kysely 0.28→0.29 and @nestjs/* to 11.1.21`** — `kysely: ^0.28.17 → ^0.29.2` (in `@duraflows/kysely`), `@nestjs/{common,core,testing}: ^11.1.19 → ^11.1.21` (in `@duraflows/nestjs`).

## Motivation

In the consumer (`emx-talleres-pma`) we had to write things like:

```ts
const instance = await workflowService.createInstance({ workflowName: pmaCaseWorkflowDefinition.name });
const status = instance.currentState as PmaCaseStatus; // ← brittle cast

const result = await workflowService.triggerEvent(input);
if (result.toState !== PmaCaseStatus.READY_TO_BUY) throw new Error("unexpected state"); // ← brittle comparison
```

With this PR:

```ts
const instance = await workflowService.createInstanceFor(pmaCaseWorkflowDefinition, {});
const status = instance.currentState; // ← already PmaCaseStatus, no cast

const result = await workflowService.triggerEventFor(pmaCaseWorkflowDefinition, input);
switch (result.outcome) {
  case "success":        return { fromState: result.fromState, toState: result.toState }; // ← already PmaCaseStatus
  case "guard-rejected": throw new WorkflowGuardRejectedError(result.rejectedBy);
  case "failure":        throw new WorkflowCommandFailedError(result.commandResults);
}
```

The definition is the single source of truth for the state union; callers should only ask "did the transition commit?", not "did it land where I expected?".

## What changed (by file)

| File                                                       | Change                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/duraflows-core/src/types/definition.ts`          | 4 interfaces become generic on `TState extends string = string`.                                                |
| `packages/duraflows-core/src/types/runtime.ts`             | `WorkflowInstance` and `WorkflowExecutionResult` become generic on `TState extends string = string`.            |
| `packages/duraflows-nestjs/src/services/workflow.service.ts` | Adds `createInstanceFor<TState>` and `triggerEventFor<TState>`. One internal `as` cast in each, justified inline. |
| `packages/duraflows-nestjs/src/workflow.module.ts`         | Adds `global: true` to `forRoot` and `forRootAsync`.                                                            |
| `packages/duraflows-kysely/package.json`                   | `kysely`: `^0.28.17 → ^0.29.2`.                                                                                 |
| `packages/duraflows-nestjs/package.json`                   | `@nestjs/{common,core,testing}`: `^11.1.19 → ^11.1.21`.                                                         |

## Backwards compatibility

- All new generic parameters have `= string` defaults, so every existing consumer keeps compiling unchanged.
- The new methods (`createInstanceFor`, `triggerEventFor`) sit alongside the existing `createInstance` / `triggerEvent` — no signatures removed or renamed.
- The `global: true` change is opt-in at the consumer side: a module that wasn't previously imported transitively will still need to be imported once via `forRoot` / `forRootAsync`. The only behavioural change is that feature modules no longer need to re-import the dynamic module to inject the exported providers.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` — clean (both ESM and CJS targets).
- [x] `pnpm test` — all green
- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `commitlint` — all green via lefthook pre-commit / commit-msg hooks on every commit.
- [x] Type narrowing verified against the usage of this lib consumer: a `WorkflowDefinition<PmaCaseStatus>` flows through `createInstanceFor` / `triggerEventFor` with zero call-site assertions.

## Risk notes

- **`kysely 0.28 → 0.29`** is a minor bump but on a 0.x package; review the [Kysely 0.29 release notes](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely/releases) if you maintain a downstream that pins kysely. `@duraflows/kysely`'s own usage compiles and tests green against `0.29.2`.
- **`global: true`** makes `WorkflowService` and friends globally injectable. This is the standard NestJS pattern for shared infrastructure modules (matches `@nestjs/typeorm`, `@nestjs/config`, etc.), but it's a small behavioural change worth flagging for reviewers.

## Commits in this PR (squash-friendly)

1. `feat(nestjs): mark WorkflowModule as global`
2. `feat(core,nestjs): generic TState on definition + createInstanceFor`
3. `feat(core,nestjs): generic TState on result + triggerEventFor`
4. `chore(deps): bump kysely 0.28→0.29 and @nestjs/* to 11.1.21`

author: rickfelix
body:
## Summary
Fixes non-deterministic RED in `scripts/hooks/__tests__/pre-tool-enforce.test.js` (4-6 of 25 tests failing, growing on re-run).

## Root cause
The ENF-15 force-push tests (T3-T7, T10) spawn `pre-tool-enforce.cjs` repeatedly with the **identical** push command under a constant `session_id` (`enf9-test`). The RCA tiered repeat-invocation guard (ENFORCEMENT 11 / SD-LEARN-FIX-ADDRESS-PATTERN-LEARN-129) is **session-scoped and time-windowed** (`.claude/retry-state-enf9-test.json`, 10 min), so its counter accumulates across these cases **and across runs**, tripping a tiered block (`RCA TIERED ENFORCEMENT ... invoked Nx on the same target`) that pre-empts the `[ENF-15] BLOCKED` output the tests assert.

## Fix
Neutralize the orthogonal guard for `spawnHookEnforce` via `LEO_RCA_ENFORCEMENT=off` — mirroring the existing `LEO_NPM_INSTALL_GUARD=off`. Test-only; **production hook behavior unchanged**. No test in this file exercises LEARN-129 itself.

## Verification
`npx vitest run scripts/hooks/__tests__/pre-tool-enforce.test.js` → **25/25 pass deterministically** on repeated runs (was 4-6 failing).

## Notes
- Closes feedback `0fd4de4f`. **Corrects its disposition**: filed as '14 failing, git-environment-dependent'; the actual cause is 4-6 failing from repeat-guard state bleed, not git-env.
- Reduces the pre-existing-RED count that blocks the whole-suite QF completion gate (feedback `352f3cec`).

author: tl32rodan
body:
## Summary

Add daily learning log for 2026-05-25 documenting competitive analysis of two mature frameworks (`SuperClaude_Framework` at 20k★, `Serena` at 24.5k★) against All-Might's core design bets.

## Key findings

- **SuperClaude validates the role/persona abstraction** as mainstream (20k stars) while its stateless+global variant throws All-Might's memory-bearing, project-scoped, per-role design into sharper relief as the differentiator.
- **Serena independently re-derived markdown-based memory** (24.5k stars), directly vindicating the "No SQLite memory store" non-goal. claude-mem's heavy stack is now the outlier.
- **Per-role memory isolation is the widening moat**: the mainstream "persona framework + memory MCP" decomposition (SuperClaude+Serena) cannot structurally express it.
- **LSP-symbolic retrieval (Serena) vs SMAK vector retrieval (All-Might) are complementary, not competing**: they solve different problems (code navigation vs semantic domain-knowledge retrieval).

## Concrete actions

- [ ] Add scope-boundary note in README positioning Serena MCP as complementary code-navigation tool; clarify `database` is semantic domain-knowledge retrieval, not code navigation.
- [ ] Verify oh-my-opencode → oh-my-openagent rename impact on README/CLAUDE.md references (Q7).
- [ ] Add SuperClaude_Framework + Serena to "already covered" skip list on next pass.

## Investment verdict

**No new feature clears the simplicity bar.** The two deep-dive competitors validate All-Might's riskiest design bets rather than challenge them. Single candidate worth rating: explicit `Triggers` metadata for weak-model routing (Q3) — **deferred at 2/5** pending first observed weak-model misroute in a multi-personality project.

All actions are documentation-only (≤30 min each); no code changes required.

author: vellum-apollo-bot[bot]
body:
## Summary

Fixes #29946 by tightening the reply-suggestion prompts so the ghost text always predicts what the **user** would type next, not what the assistant would say.

Re-roll of #30834 with the post-hoc regex filter dropped. We try the prompt-only fix first per the AGENTS.md "Assistant-Driven Judgement" rule — judgement calls belong to the LLM, not hardcoded heuristics. If the prompt changes alone don't resolve the issue in observation, the follow-up is a daemon-routed LLM judge, not a regex list.

## Changes

- System prompt grows a `CRITICAL` section pinning user-voice: anti-pattern list (`I can help`, `Here's what`, `Let me`, `I'd suggest`), and a framing nudge ("if you were the user reading the assistant's reply, what would you ask next?").
- User prompt restates the user-voice constraint inline so it's not buried in the system slot.
- No new code paths, no new filters, no new dependencies. Single file, ~14 lines added.

## Why no regex filter

The original PR (#30834) added an `isAssistantVoiceSuggestion()` post-processing filter backed by a regex array. Multiple reviewers flagged it:

- **Devin (🔴):** violates the "Assistant-Driven Judgement" rule — a scoring function via string matches to approximate a model's judgement about tone is exactly the pattern that rule forbids.
- **Devin (🟡) and Codex (P2):** the `/^(I think|I see|I know|I believe|…)/` pattern rejects perfectly normal user-voice openings ("I think Tuesday works", "I see, that makes sense"), degrading availability of the chip.

Land the soft fix, observe. Escalate to a daemon judgement call if the prompt changes prove insufficient.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Checklist

- [x] Single file, ~14 lines
- [x] No new dependencies
- [x] Backward compatible

author: edwin-zvs
body:
Closes #230.

## Root cause

Zoom / unzoom / list hide-show change the view pane **width**. vt100 can't reflow soft-wrapped lines on `set_size`, so `replay_cached` rebuilds the parser at the new width — and re-fed the **entire** session history synchronously on the UI thread. A non-tool session accumulates its whole (unbounded) history in one `pending_chunk`, so on a long session every width change re-parsed megabytes → the freeze.

## Fix

Re-feed only the **scrollback tail**. The parser keeps just `SCROLLBACK_MAX` (5000) lines; everything older produces lines the ring discards immediately, so re-feeding it is pure waste. `reflow_tail_offset` finds the byte offset of the last `SCROLLBACK_MAX + viewport + warmup` lines and the rebuild feeds only from there → cost is constant regardless of history size. A 1024-line warmup margin before the retained window re-establishes terminal state (SGR/cursor) so the visible scrollback isn't parsed cold from an arbitrary cut.

**Alt-screen apps (codex / vim / htop)** are handled separately: their grid has no scrollback to reflow and the app repaints on the resize SIGWINCH, so the width-change branch just `set_size`s the grid in place. Bounding their re-feed would be **unsafe** — the `ESC[?1049h` enter escape lives at the very start of the stream, and a truncated tail would render into the normal screen. (This was a correctness trap I hit while building it; the alt-screen test guards against it.)

## Measured

Release, e2e `zoom_latency` benchmark, 200k-line shell session:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| zoom | 25.2ms | 2.3ms |
| unzoom | 18.2ms | 2.3ms |

~11×, and now **flat** vs history size (was linear: 40k→6.6ms, 200k→25ms, so 500k≈60ms; ~10× worse in debug). The freeze is gone.

## Regression guards (timing-free, run on CI)

- `reflow_tail_offset_bounds_long_buffer` / `_keeps_short_buffer_whole` — the tail-offset logic.
- `resize_long_history_renders_correct_tail` — the bounded re-feed still shows the true newest lines (no dropped content).
- `resize_in_alt_screen_keeps_alt_grid` — a long alt-screen stream stays in alt-screen across a resize; **fails if the bound is applied unconditionally**.
- `resize_long_history_rebuild_is_bounded` — timing budget (generous, debug-safe) that fails by multiples if the bound is removed.

Plus `crates/e2e/tests/zoom_latency.rs` (`#[ignore]`): drives the real TUI in a PTY, floods a deep history, times the zoom toggle (the measurement above).

## Scope

Fixes the `replay_cached` path — shell / codex / claude, the sessions that flood huge output and where the freeze bites. Tool-block sessions (zarvis, `replay_full`) re-feed via the `items` list and aren't bounded here; their histories are typically much shorter (chat turns, not command floods). Follow-up if it bites — `replay_full`'s item-layout positioning makes a safe bound more involved.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --workspace` clean.
- [x] 180 cli unit tests pass (5 new), incl. existing resize/zarvis budget tests.
- [x] e2e `tui_smoke` (2) + `restart` (3) pass — no regression.
- [x] Before/after benchmark (table above).
- [ ] Hands-on: zoom/unzoom/list-toggle on a long codex + long shell session feels instant.

author: biagiodistefano
body:
## Summary

Completes the audit from #442. With `ATOMIC_REQUESTS=True`, every HTTP request runs in one DB transaction that commits only when the view returns. A bare `.delay()` pushes to the broker **immediately**, so a worker can pick the task up and read a row created in the same request *before* it commits → intermittent `DoesNotExist`. The fix is to defer such dispatches with `transaction.on_commit(...)`.

## Audit result

~69 production `.delay()` sites classified by execution context (HTTP-request vs Celery-task vs bot/management). Most were already wrapped (including a named-closure pattern the issue's grep-based suspect list missed) or are legitimately bare task-to-task chains. **25 HTTP-request-context dispatches** were newly wrapped across `accounts`, `common`, `events`, `notifications`, `questionnaires`, and `telegram`.

## Two subtleties worth a look in review

1. **`register_user` anti-enumeration paths** — it's `@transaction.atomic` and dispatches an activation/verification email *then* `raise HttpError(400)`. The inner savepoint rollback **discards** the `on_commit` callback, so a blanket wrap would silently stop those emails **in production**. Kept bare via `send_verification_email_for_user(defer=False)` / `_send_activation_email_for_guest`; the new-user success path keeps `on_commit`.
2. **VIES 503 retry** looks similar but has **no inner `@transaction.atomic`** — Ninja turns `HttpError(503)` into a *response*, so the request commits and `on_commit` correctly fires (and is the right choice: it stops the retry racing the freshly-set `vat_id`).

The distinguishing rule (inner atomic → rollback discards `on_commit`; none → Ninja response → commit) is documented in `CLAUDE.md`.

Other notes:
- `notifications/admin`: `functools.partial` binds `batch_ids` eagerly inside the loop (a lambda would re-dispatch the last batch).
- `user_preferences`: dispatch in a single `on_commit` closure over a materialized id list (loop-variable capture).

## Tests

- Dispatch-asserting tests marked `@pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True)` per the #441 precedent.
- Tests that read `mail.outbox` use `django_capture_on_commit_callbacks(execute=True)` instead — `transaction=True` would commit the fixture's event-open notification and pollute the outbox.
- `make check` clean; full `make test` green.

author: arnausb
body:
Reworks the `deploy-to-cloud-run` masterclass demo into a self-contained progressive-canary pipeline you can drive entirely from `git push`.

## What changed

- **Progressive canary in Cloud Build.** Replaces the single 10% `update-traffic` step with an inline ramp: `10% → bake 2 min → 50% → bake 2 min → 100% (graduate)`. During each bake the build samples the canary URL and reverts traffic + fails the build if `_MAX_5XX` is exceeded.
- **Vulnerability gate.** Enables Container Scanning, then polls the Container Analysis API after `docker push` and blocks the deploy on configurable severities (`_FAIL_SEVERITIES`, default `CRITICAL`, `NONE` disables).
- **Canary smoke test.** Resolves the `--tag=canary` URL and polls `/health` before any traffic shifts.
- **Multi-stage Dockerfile + `.dockerignore`.** Pinned Python version, non-root user (UID 10001), OCI labels, signal-safe `CMD`, build context trimmed to just `app/` + `requirements.txt`.
- **App refactor for the demo.** Two top-of-file knobs (`VERSION`, `FAIL_ROOT`) — flip them between pushes to walk V1/V2/V3/V4. Response now includes `K_REVISION` so you can see which revision served each request during the ramp.
- **README rewrite.** New "V1 → V4 walkthrough" with a successful canary (V2), an inline-revert demo (V3, `FAIL_ROOT=True`), and a recovery push (V4). All knobs (`_BAKE_SECONDS`, `_MAX_5XX`, `_FAIL_SEVERITIES`) documented as Cloud Build substitutions.
- **`.gitignore` cleanup.** Removes entries that were excluding `app/`, `Dockerfile`, and `requirements.txt` — the pipeline couldn't actually build the image without them.

## Tunables (no code change needed)

| Substitution         | Default     | Purpose                                                  |
|----------------------|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `_BAKE_SECONDS`      | `120`       | Seconds to sample the canary URL between promotions      |
| `_MAX_5XX`           | `2`         | 5xx tolerance per bake window before in-build revert     |
| `_FAIL_SEVERITIES`   | `CRITICAL`  | Scan severities that fail the build; `NONE` disables     |

author: cristobalgomez-pp
body:
## Resumen

Fase 1 del rediseño de `/surf` como **Surf Hub**: arregla los datos incorrectos que se mostraban en vivo, añade **marea real**, e introduce un **motor de veredicto** que responde de un vistazo "¿está bueno para surfear ahora, y si no, cuándo?".

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-24-surf-page-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-24-surf-hub-fase-1.md`

## Cambios

**Bugs de datos en vivo (corregidos):**
- 🌡️ Temperatura del agua: `78°C` (Fahrenheit con etiqueta °C) → normalizada a °C con sanity-check.
- 🌊 Altura de ola: mostraba un rango falso `1.2 – 1.2 m` → ahora un valor único.
- ⏱️ "actualizado hace minutos" era texto fijo → ahora tiempo relativo real desde `updatedAt`.

**Nuevo:**
- 🌙 **Marea real** desde Stormglass (`/tide/extremes` + `/tide/sea-level`) con `TideChart` (SVG inline, sin dependencias) — antes la marea era un placeholder `Baja · 0 m`.
- 🏄 **Motor de veredicto** (`features/surf/lib/rating.ts`): combina viento (offshore/onshore), swell (altura×periodo) y marea contra los ideales de Cerritos → rating 1–5, veredicto en texto, nivel recomendado, y **mejor ventana del día**. Ideales calibrados con conocimiento local (offshore = E, periodo ideal 12–16s, marea media).
- `SurfVerdictHero` como bloque principal de la página.
- 🕐 Horas en **hora local de Cerritos** (`America/Mazatlan`, UTC-7) vía `Intl`, no UTC.

**Arquitectura:** transforms y motor son funciones puras (testeadas con vitest, sin red); cada fetch externo degrada por separado (si Stormglass falla, el resto de la página renderiza); todo el texto vía i18n (ES/EN). Sin dependencias nuevas.

## Verificación

- [x] `npm test` → **371/371** (50+ archivos)
- [x] `npm run build` → exitoso
- [ ] **Preview de Vercel**: validar veredicto, marea y horas locales con datos reales de Stormglass (la key vive en el entorno de Vercel)

## Notas

- Rama rebaseada limpia sobre `main` (solo commits de surf; el trabajo de hoteles ya entró por #73).
- Fuera de alcance (Fase 2/3): CMS editable de la guía del spot, puntuación por dirección de swell, recomendaciones longboard/shortboard, webcam y mapa del spot.

author: krisarmstrong
body:
## Summary

Ports niac's `invopop/jsonschema` generator pattern to seed. Adds `cmd/seed-schema/main.go`, a `make schema` target, and six committed JSON Schemas under `docs/schemas/api/`. Sets up the pipeline that #1104 (CI drift gate) and #1105 (TS codegen) will consume.

- Closes #1103
- Part of #1099 — Phase 3 of the boundary-validation hardening epic
- Reference: krisarmstrong/niac-go ADR 0001 (PR #688)

## What changed

- `cmd/seed-schema/main.go` — new generator. Configured per the ADR:
  - `FieldNameTag: "json"` — schemas reflect the wire format (HTTP DTOs use json tags)
  - `AllowAdditionalProperties: false` — matches `DisallowUnknownFields` in `decodeJSONStrict`
  - `Anonymous: true` — inline nested types, easier to consume
  - One schema file per DTO under `docs/schemas/api/`
- `mk/build.mk` — `schema` Makefile target
- `docs/schemas/api/*.json` — 6 generated schemas: login, setup-complete, recovery-complete, set-mtu, path, wifi-connect
- `go.mod` / `go.sum` — adds `github.com/invopop/jsonschema v0.14.0`

## Test plan

- [x] `make schema` runs clean
- [x] All 6 schemas write successfully
- [x] `go build ./cmd/seed-schema` clean
- [ ] `golangci-lint run ./cmd/seed-schema/...` — in flight

## Notes for reviewers

- **No validate-tag export.** `invopop/jsonschema` doesn't read `go-playground/validator` `validate:` tags. The schemas document shape (which fields, which types, required-ness from the json tag) but not constraints (min, max, oneof). Constraints stay enforced at runtime by `validateStruct` (#1102); the schemas mirror the wire contract. Adding constraint export is a follow-up if needed.
- **DTO list is explicit.** The `schemaTargets` slice in `cmd/seed-schema/main.go` is the only place to add a new DTO. Today's list mirrors the DTOs we already tagged in #1102. Easy to extend.
- **Stale `scripts/generate-types.sh` left as-is.** It points at the pre-rename `web/` tree and a `schemas/config.schema.json` that doesn't exist. #1105 (TS codegen) will replace it.
- **CI drift gate not included here.** That's #1104 — separate PR so the diff stays focused. Will land right after this.

author: michaeltrefry
body:
## Summary
`refreshData()` pulled **all 8** workspace collections (projects, jobs, workers, models, loras, presets, training targets/presets) after nearly every create/cancel/duplicate/retry — even on every "Generate" click — despite the SSE stream already pushing the relevant updates and the create paths already updating `jobs` optimistically.

Re-validated against the current code (post the sc-1651 App.jsx context refactor): every job-creation endpoint routes through `create_generation_job`, which `publish("job.updated")` + `publish_queue()` on creation, and `cancel/retry/duplicate/update_progress` publish too. So a created/changed job (and the queue/worker state) always arrives live via SSE.

Dropped `refreshData()` from every job-mutation path:
- App.jsx: `createImageJob`, `createVqaJob`, `createInterleaveJob`, `createVideoJob`, `createPlaceholderJob`, `jobAction` (cancel/retry/duplicate)
- `useModelsAndLoras`: `createModelImportJob`, `createLoraImportJob`, `createModelDownloadJob`, `createModelConvertJob`
- `usePersonTracks`: detect + track jobs
- `useTimelines`: timeline export + frame extraction
- `useCharacters`: character test job

Kept full `refreshData()` only for **genuine catalog changes** — model/LoRA import+download **completion** (SSE handler) and model/LoRA **delete** — plus the initial authenticated load. Removed the now-unused `refreshData` prop from `usePersonTracks`, `useTimelines`, and `useCharacters`.

Net: catalog data still reconciles where it actually changes; job/worker/queue state rides the SSE stream + optimistic updates instead of triggering an 8-collection refetch per click.

- [x] `vite build` — clean

author: l3von36
body:
## Summary
Generalizes the single-dataset (PEMS-BAY) imputation notebook into a multi-dataset benchmark with an ablation study, a sparsity-sensitivity sweep, parameterized evaluation metrics/units, and cross-dataset aggregation.

### Datasets
- `DATASET` switch: **PEMS-BAY**, **METR-LA** (speed; `.h5`/`.csv` + `adj_mx*.pkl`) and **PEMS04**, **PEMS08** (flow; `.npz` + `distance.csv` edge-list adjacency).
- Flow datasets impute channel 0 with synthetic masking (`valid`=all-ones); speed datasets keep the `0 == missing` convention.
- Run once per dataset → each writes `results_<DATASET>.json`; an aggregation cell stitches them into a cross-dataset table.

### Added analyses
- **Ablation** — V5 component leave-one-out (2-hop n_mean, soft_locf base, staleness, 1-hop n_mean, node embedding) + table + bar plot.
- **Sparsity sensitivity** — trained V5 / LOCF / HA evaluated at 50→95% + table + curve.
- **Units/labels** parameterized via `VALUE_UNIT` / `VALUE_NAME` (km/h ↔ veh/5min), and per-dataset value clamp (`CLAMP_LO/HI`) so flow values aren't clipped to the 0–120 speed range.

### No-leakage guarantees (preserved per dataset)
- A blind (masked) sensor never sees its own value — **verified**: perturbing a masked cell yields 0.0 prediction change.
- No future leakage (causal attention/LOCF/staleness), train-only stats, no self-loops in adjacency (including the new `distance.csv` graphs).
- Added a per-timestep **anchor guard** to `make_eval_mask_np` to prevent all-blind-timestep NaNs at extreme sparsity. It is a **no-op at 80%/large-N**, so existing PEMS-BAY masks and results are byte-identical.

### Validation
- All 30 cells compile; CPU smoke test (ablation model across all toggle configs + anti-leak check) and an end-to-end integration run of the new cells passed on synthetic data.
- Not executed on real datasets here (no GPU / large downloads) — loaders run against real files on Kaggle.

body:
## Summary

Implements the Flutter side of Feature 3 of [`docs/features-may-25.md`](../docs/features-may-25.md) — Veriff identity verification for walkers.

- **`veriff_flutter ^4.6.0`** installed; Android Kotlin DSL bumped to `minSdkVersion 26` with multidex; iOS `Info.plist` gets `NSCameraUsageDescription`, `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`, `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription`, `NFCReaderUsageDescription` (all in Spanish).
- **`WalkerVerificationService`** wraps `Veriff().start(config)` and maps `Status.done|canceled|error` to a typed `VerificationOutcome`.
- **Walker verification screen** with the full state-machine UI: `not_started` → `session_created` → `submitted` → `verified | resubmission_needed | rejected | expired | abandoned | manual_review`. Subscribes to Postgres realtime updates on `walkers` so the UI refreshes when the backend webhook lands.
- **Walker discoverability gated on verification** — `home_screen.dart`, `alternative_walkers_screen.dart`, and `walker_service.dart` all add `.eq('verification_status', 'verified')` to their walker queries (defense in depth alongside the SQL filter in `nearby_walkers`).

Plan: [`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-25-walker-id-verification.md`](../docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-25-walker-id-verification.md). Companion backend PR: benzzdan/Pawgo#ralph/walker-id-verification.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter pub get` resolves Veriff SDK; `pod install` succeeds; `flutter analyze` zero new issues
- [x] 4 new unit tests on `WalkerVerificationService` (`submitted`, `canceled`, `error message`, const factories)
- [ ] Real-device build and Veriff flow with Customer Portal test integration (requires API key — see backend PR `.env.example`)
- [ ] Permission denial paths on a physical device
- [ ] End-to-end: walker submits onboarding → verification screen opens → completes Veriff test flow → `Status.done` shows "submitted, awaiting review" → backend webhook fires `approved` → realtime UI flips to "Verified ✓" → walker now appears in owner search

## Notes

- Plan called for `languageCode`; `veriff_flutter` 4.6 actually uses `languageLocale`. `Result.error` is an enum, not a String — `errorString()` extracts the message.
- Verification strings ship as a typed `_VerificationStrings` class keyed by `Locale.languageCode`. After the companion dog-profile PR merges (which adds `flutter_localizations`), these should be folded into `app_en.arb` / `app_es.arb` for consistency.

author: posthog[bot]
body:
## Problem

PostHog's own error tracking was surfacing `TypeError: Failed to fetch` issues whose stack traces blamed `URLTriggerMatching._urlTriggerStatus` (a synchronous property read that does no network work). The real source was the patched `fetch` in `packages/browser/src/entrypoints/tracing-headers.ts`: an `async function` wrapper that called `originalFetch(req)` and let the rejection propagate through. In minified bundles the async wrapper's frame sits next to unrelated replay code, so source maps misattribute the throw site to the replay function — making end-user network failures (offline / CORS / DNS) look like SDK bugs.

## Changes

- `patchFetch` now uses a plain (non-async) function named `posthogPatchedFetch` that returns `originalFetch(req)` directly. The wrapper is no longer on the stack when the underlying promise rejects, so the rejection is attributed to the caller's call site rather than misattributed to nearby SDK frames in the minified bundle.
- Behavior is otherwise unchanged: the request is built synchronously, tracing headers are added, and the original fetch's promise (resolve or reject) is forwarded verbatim.
- `patchXHR` is unchanged — `XMLHttpRequest.open` is synchronous and was never part of the misattribution.
- Added unit tests verifying rejection forwarding and the success path.
- Added a `posthog-js` patch changeset.

author: eric-cielo
body:
## What

Adds a **DEEP** review tier to the `/flo-simplify` (`/distill`) classifier that runs a 3-agent **Opus** review automatically for genuinely architectural diffs, plus an `escalate.suggested` signal that offers a handoff to Claude Code''s built-in `/simplify` on the most extreme diffs. The Opus pass always runs as the floor; the handoff is a prompt, never an auto-switch.

Previously distill capped at NORMAL (3 Sonnet agents) and hard-banned Opus. The rationale "code review is breadth-bound" holds for ordinary review but not for *architectural* review, which is depth-bound — judging whether a large refactor picked the right abstractions is reasoning, not surveying.

## Tuning: gated on net-new-logic, never raw volume

Opus only escalates on genuine new-logic evidence, measured *net of churn*:
- **TS/JS** -> net-new declarations (`>1500 LOC + >=10 net decls` for DEEP)
- **other languages** -> net-new lines (`>1200 net-new lines`)
- noise (lockfiles, snapshots, `dist/`, `vendor/`, min/maps) and docs/data are stripped before measuring

Negative-guard tests prove the bar holds — a lockfile bump, a reformat, a non-TS/JS relocation, and a big markdown doc all stay off Opus.

## Escalation ladder
| Tier | Agents | Model | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| TRIVIAL | 0 | — | gate stamp |
| SMALL | 1 | haiku/sonnet | |
| NORMAL | 3 | sonnet | cross-cutting |
| **DEEP** | 3 | **opus** | architectural — auto |
| **DEEP + handoff** | 3 | opus | + suggests built-in /simplify |

## Files
- `bin/simplify-classify.cjs` (+ byte-identical `.claude/helpers/` twin) — DEEP tier, `escalate` field, per-language family stats
- `.claude/skills/flo-simplify/SKILL.md` — DEEP docs, reversed "opus never" rule, handoff phase
- `docs/blog/distill-vs-simplify.md` — updated for bidirectional calibration
- `tests/bin/simplify-classify.test.ts` — 9 new cases (positive + negative guards)

## Dogfooding
Ran `/distill` on this branch (classified NORMAL). Its own review caught that the new-subsystem triggers used global decl counts instead of TS/JS-scoped — fixed in the third commit, plus the previously-uncovered new-subsystem test.

## Testing
- Classifier: 27/27
- Full suite Pass 1: 7981 passed / 0 failed; gate-helpers 256/256, gate-snapshot 14/14
- One unrelated pre-existing isolation flake (`daemon-lock-orphan`, a fork-contention timeout) passes 8/8 alone.

author: mousebrains
body:
## Summary

`_internal/`'s "Recent CSP violations" table was flagging **every** report in the production log as **"Same-origin (our code)"** — prompting the question "is our own code violating CSP?". It isn't. The 43 reports in `csp.log` were a single 2-second burst from Google's `google-proxy-*.google.com` transcoding fleet (one headless-Chrome UA) injecting inline `<script>` into the homepage. Our served HTML ships only external `<script src=>` and our JS never evals — verified.

## Root cause

For `blocked = inline`/`eval`/`wasm-eval` there is no real script file, so the browser sets `source-file` to the **document URL**. The old `csp_classify()` bucketed any `source_file` on our origin as "our code" — so injected inline (proxy / extension / translator / AV) was indistinguishable-by-`source_file` from authored code and got mislabeled.

## Changes

- **New "Injected (proxy/extension)" bucket**: `blocked ∈ {inline, eval, wasm-eval}` (or blank) with `source_file == document_uri` (query/fragment aside) → injected. Genuine same-origin code keeps "Same-origin (our code)" (a real asset path like `/static/foo.js:42`).
- **Key-mismatch fix**: `csp-report.php` normalizes to `blocked`/`violated`, but the classifier read `blocked_uri` (always empty) and the table's Violated/Blocked columns read `violated_directive`/`blocked_uri` (always rendered `—`). Now read the normalized keys, raw Reporting-API names as fallbacks.
- **Extracted** `csp_classify()` → `php/includes/csp_classify.php` (mixed-cast-clean via `is_string` narrowing) so it's unit-testable, mirroring `svg_plot.php` / `review_logic.php`.
- **Tests**: `tests/php/CspClassifyTest.php` — 9 cases incl. the exact production burst as a regression.

## Verification

- `composer analyse` → **0** (level 9 + strict); baseline **shrinks** 221→218 (`index.php` `cast.string` 9→6, nothing added).
- `composer fix-check` clean; `composer test` → **181 pass** (172 + 9 new).
- Replayed the real `csp.log` through the new classifier: all 43 → **"Injected (proxy/extension)"**.

author: jadb
body:
## Summary

Annotate every wsm command leaf with kit v0.4's Layer-A metadata (`kit/side-effect`, `kit/idempotent`, `kit/top-level-verb`, `kit/hierarchical`, `Long`), mount the kit-shipped `status` subcommand, and add group-level `Long` descriptions. Bumps kit to v0.4.0-alpha.5 with the lipgloss fork that closes the last NO_COLOR honor gap. Includes fixes for the three pre-existing Linux-CI flakes (`TestNoColorEnv`, `TestInteractiveCompletion/bash`, `TestWorkspaceRemove`).

Tracks: `wsm-kit-12fcc-conformance` (T-0133..T-0141).

## Validator bucket diff

| Bucket | Pre-conformance | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `kit/side-effect` missing | 28 | **0** |
| `kit/idempotent` missing | 8 | **0** |
| `Long` missing | 31 | **0** |
| reserved `status` subcommand | 1 | **0** |
| `kit/top-level-verb` missing | 9 | **0** |
| `kit/hierarchical` chain missing | 1 | **0** |
| flag collisions | 0 | 0 |
| passthrough | 0 | 0 |
| `TooManyTopLevelVerbs: 11 > 10` | 0 | **1** ⚠ |

The only remaining validator failure is `TooManyTopLevelVerbs`: mounting the reserved `status` subcommand brings depth-1 runnable verbs to 11, over kit's default cap of 10. **Deliberately left for a follow-up task** to decide whether to (a) raise `MaxTopLevelVerbs`, (b) demote a verb, or (c) accept the verb count as documented.

`DisableValidate: true` therefore stays on. A separate task owns the gate-flip after the verb-count decision lands. The rationale comment in `cmd/wsm/commands/root.go` spells out exactly what flipping it would block.

## Dependency changes

- **kit alpha.4 → alpha.5**: ships hop-top/poly-kit PR #88 — gates header `Bold(true)` on `TableStyle.Header` being non-nil. Resolves the second of three ANSI sources in `TestNoColorEnv`. (T-0828)
- **Temporary lipgloss replace**: pin `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` to `github.com/jadb/lipgloss/v2 @5250cba` carrying [charmbracelet/lipgloss#692](https://github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss/pull/692). That PR gates the compat package's init-time `HasDarkBackground` query on `NO_COLOR`, resolving the third ANSI source (OSC 11 + CSI DA terminal probes leaking into stdout before `main()` runs). Remove the replace once #692 merges and a lipgloss release ships the fix. (T-0829)
- **wsm-side patch**: clobbers kit's process-wide default `TableStyle` with a zero value when `NO_COLOR` env is set (at root construction) or when `--no-color` is parsed (PersistentPreRunE). Resolves the first ANSI source — the 24-bit color SGRs that kit's styled renderer emits per cell.

With all three layers in place, `TestNoColorEnv` passes.

## Linux CI flake fixes

Three pre-existing failures (present on every wsm branch since 2026-03-23, including main) addressed in this PR:

- **`TestNoColorEnv`** (T-0139) — resolved via the 3-layer fix above.
- **`TestInteractiveCompletion/bash`** (T-0140) — root cause was a misnamed probe: cobra generates `__start_wsm` but the test checked `type -t _wsm_completion`. macOS quietly skipped the bash subtest because bash-completion v1 wasn't installed at the well-known paths; Linux CI runs it. Fix: probe the correct function name. Validated via `Dockerfile.ubuntu-test` Docker run.
- **`TestWorkspaceRemove`** (T-0141) — root cause was lipgloss/fang's `HasDarkBackground` query at startup consuming the harness's pre-buffered stdin `y\n` during its 2s read window, so wsm's `bufio.ReadString` then blocked forever and the harness killed the process (exit -1). Fix: replaced the `script(1)` shell-out in `execTTY` with go-expect PTY console + new `runTTYExpectingPrompt` helper that waits for the `[y/N]:` prompt before sending input. Validated locally + Docker.

## Structure

```
* Merge fix/workspace-remove-flake   → PTY harness with prompt-wait
* Merge fix/completion-interactive-flake → probe correct cobra function name
* Merge bump-kit-alpha-5             → kit alpha.5 + lipgloss fork + NO_COLOR wsm patch
* test(cli): lock Layer-A annotation coverage + top-level verb count
* fix(cli): apply Layer-A annotation review feedback
* Merge 12fcc-misc          → root: init, version, tui, upgrade preamble, config show
* Merge 12fcc-space-device  → space + device leaves
* Merge 12fcc-event         → event leaves
* Merge 12fcc-snapshot      → snapshot leaves
* Merge 12fcc-workspace     → workspace leaves + workspace config hierarchical chain
* feat(cli): annotate groups with Long descriptions and top-level-verb
* feat(cli): mount kit-shipped status subcommand
```

## Regression locks

Two tests in `cmd/wsm/commands/root_test.go`:

- **`TestLayerAAnnotationsPresent`** — walks the command tree, asserts every runnable depth-1 verb has `kit/top-level-verb` and every runnable leaf has `kit/side-effect`. Catches annotation deletion before the gate flip runs.
- **`TestTopLevelVerbCountLock`** — pins depth-1 runnable verb count at 11 so a 12th verb can't sneak in unobserved.

## Annotation conventions discovered

Documented as a package-level doc block in `cmd/wsm/commands/root.go`. Summary:

- `cli.SetSideEffect(cmd, cli.SideEffectRead|Write|WriteLocal|Interactive)` — picked per verb semantics; `Interactive` for `tui`, `WriteLocal` for filesystem-scoped writes like `init`, `upgrade`, `upgrade preamble --install`.
- `cli.SetIdempotency(cmd, cli.IdempotencyYes|No|Conditional)` — explicit only when `defaultIdempotency` doesn't cover. `Conditional` for `tui` and `upgrade` (depend on user input / external state).
- `cli.SetTopLevelVerb(cmd)` — on every depth-1 leaf/group.
- `cli.SetHierarchical(cmd)` — on every non-root, non-leaf ancestor of a depth≥3 leaf.
- `cli.WithStatus(cli.StatusConfig{})` — root option providing kit's default `status` implementation.

## Side effects of the conformance

- `wsm init --help` and `wsm upgrade preamble --help` now show kit's auto-registered "Dry-run support: this command honors --dry-run." footer.
- `wsm status` is a new top-level subcommand (kit-shipped).

## Test plan

- [x] `make build` clean
- [x] `make fmt` clean
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `make verify-no-ui-leak` clean
- [x] `go test ./cmd/wsm/commands/` — pass (incl. 2 new annotation-lock tests)
- [x] `go test ./...` — **all packages pass** locally (was 453/1/1 before kit alpha.5 + lipgloss fork + flake fixes; now all green)
- [x] Validator bucket counts verified at every slice with `DisableValidate: false` toggle
- [x] All 3 pre-existing Linux CI flakes fixed and validated via Docker (`Dockerfile.ubuntu-test`)
- [ ] CI re-run after merge
- [ ] Follow-up: resolve `TooManyTopLevelVerbs` + flip `DisableValidate: false`
- [ ] Follow-up: verify `--format` inheritance under kit alpha.4+ defer fix (T-0132)
- [ ] Follow-up: destructive-confirmation alignment with kit's `--confirm` policy (T-0122)
- [ ] Follow-up: remove the temporary `replace charm.land/lipgloss/v2` directive once charmbracelet/lipgloss#692 ships in a release

## Branch shape

Foundation contains the full conformance stack + review-fix follow-ups + the bump + NO_COLOR work + 2 flake fixes. Slice branches (`12fcc-workspace`, `12fcc-snapshot`, `12fcc-event`, `12fcc-space-device`, `12fcc-misc`, `bump-kit-alpha-5`, `fix/completion-interactive-flake`, `fix/workspace-remove-flake`) remain on the remote as historical pointers reachable as second parents in foundation's merge history. Base: `kit-runtime-adoption-cli-parity`.

## Summary
- implement updated cooling safety/modulation behavior without adding new user settings
- move cooling soft-stop confirm timing to a shared substitution with default 30s
- make dew hard-stop threshold dynamic from existing safety margin
- add confirm timing for dew hard-stop to avoid reacting to short spikes
- derive dew restart threshold from the effective hard-stop plus hysteresis
- keep level-1 hold behavior so demand does not drop to 0 while raw buffer gap is still positive (except real safety/fallback)

## Implemented Logic
- effective_hard_stop = 0.15 + 0.30 * clamp(safety_margin, 0..2)
- hard_dew_restart_gap = effective_hard_stop + 0.20
- hard dew stop is applied only when raw dew_gap stays below effective_hard_stop for the confirm window (30s default)
- soft-stop near target uses the same confirm window and remains substitution-driven

- openquatt/oq_cooling_strategy.yaml
  - dynamic dew hard-stop and restart thresholds
  - dew hard-stop confirmation state/timer
  - soft-stop confirm timer now substitution-driven
- openquatt/oq_substitutions_common.yaml
  - add oq_cooling_limiter_stop_confirm_s (default 30)

## Why
This reduces strict stop-restart chatter near dewpoint, especially at low safety margins, while preserving a clear condensation safety boundary.

body:
## What

First **adopters** of the C1 (`apiAssertions`) and C2 (`metadata.routeStubs`) Spec CI capabilities shipped in #275. #275 landed the capabilities with **zero specs using them** — this PR moves real nightly-Playwright **functional** coverage onto the on-PR Spec CI gate (the adoption step toward retiring Playwright; no Playwright is retired here).

Built on `main` (which carries the merged #275 capabilities). #275 was already merged, so this lands as a follow-up PR rather than an extension of that branch.

## C1 — API-contract assertions (ports `frontend/tests/e2e/ui-bridge-search.spec.ts`)

`specs/pages/ui-bridge-states/state-machine.derived.json` gains a top-level `apiAssertions` block with two read-effect checks:

| Ported from | Check | Assertions |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-bridge-search.spec.ts:23` | `POST /api/ui-bridge/control/discover` headless | `status_code==503`, `$.success==false`, `$.code=="NO_BROWSER_CONNECTED"` |
| `ui-bridge-search.spec.ts:63` | `GET /api/ui-bridge/health` envelope | `status==200`, `$.success==true`, `$.data.responsive==true`, `$.uiBridge.appId=="qontinui-web"` |

Issued through the same-origin Next proxy (the page's auth path). In CI no relay client is attached, so the proxy short-circuits `discover` to the canonical `NO_BROWSER_CONNECTED` 503 envelope (`src/app/api/ui-bridge/[...path]/route.ts:258`).

**Value-level only — no `conforms_to`.** Verified via an ajv probe that the proxy 503 envelope (`{success,code,message}`) and the SDK health envelope both **lack** the required `requestId`/`type`/`timestamp` fields of the runner's canonical `UiBridgeResponseEnvelope`, so `conforms_to:"UiBridgeResponseEnvelope"` would (correctly) red them. No corpus type models the proxy/SDK HTTP envelope shape yet → corpus-promotion follow-up (below), not a blocker per the plan's Resolved decision.

## C2 — per-spec route stubs (ports `frontend/tests/e2e/pages/admin.spec.ts:455`)

`specs/pages/coord-agent-detail/state-machine.derived.json` gains `metadata.routeStubs` fulfilling `GET /api/v1/operations/agent-logs/by-agent/spec-ci-sentinel-agent` with three canned log rows, plus a new `coord-agent-detail-populated` state asserting `coord-agent-log-list` + `agent-log-row`.

Previously this spec could only reach the **empty-state** chrome (the sentinel agent has no logs in the ci-bot tenant — noted in the spec's own description). The stub flips it to the **populated list** state the e2e `by-agent` test exercised. The stub is load-bearing: remove it and both populated assertions red.

## Corpus-promotion follow-up (non-blocking)

No backend `/api/v1/*` type was needed for these ports, but `conforms_to` wanted (and could not use) canonical types for:
- the UI-Bridge **proxy** error envelope `{success, code, message}` (the `NO_BROWSER_CONNECTED` 503 shape) — not in the corpus.
- the UI-Bridge SDK **HTTP health** envelope `{success, data:{responsive,...}, uiBridge:{appId,...}}` — distinct from the runner's `UiBridgeResponseEnvelope` (which is the WS/relay envelope requiring `requestId`/`type`/`timestamp`).

Promoting these into the `qontinui-schemas` corpus would let these two C1 checks upgrade from value-level to full schema-conformance.

## Verification
- Both checks reasoned provable-both-ways (green on current contract; red on wrong status / dropped `code` / non-conformant body / missing stub).
- Spec CI dispatched on this branch — corpus must stay whole-corpus `full_match`, `apiAssertionPassRate >= 0.999`, `serverErrors == 0`.

author: laithsakka
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #185327
* #185165
* #185161
* __->__ #185154
* #184853
# What

Adds support for derived expressions (e.g. `A * 2 + 1`) as leaf specs in
`TensorSpec` and `ParamsSpec`. The dim/arg must equal the expression at
runtime; violation raises via the standard deferred-runtime-assert mechanism.

```python
B = ShapeVar("batch")
torch.compile(
    fn,
    shapes_spec={
        "x": TensorSpec([B, None]),
        "y": TensorSpec([B * 2, None]),   # y.shape[0] = 2 * x.shape[0]
        "n": B * 2 + 1,                   # scalar arg: n = 2 * x.shape[0] + 1
    },
)
```
### How
IntVar/ShapeVar are special SymInts that represent spec variables. They're backed by a singleton "spec ShapeEnv" used only for shape specs; this env blocks all public APIs used for reasoning (evaluation, guard recording, deferred asserts) so accidental misuse like if A > 1: or torch._check(A > 1) outside assumptions fails loudly.

A = ShapeVar()
A + 1   # → SymInt representing the derived expression `A + 1`

When an input with a derived-SymInt spec is processed:

A fresh unbacked symbol u is allocated for the input.
The assumption u == subst(A + 1) is appended to _shape_spec_pending_assumptions.
Pending entries are emitted as runtime asserts (via guard_or_defer_runtime_assert) once all their free spec symbols are bound to real unbacked symbols (drained on each new bare-IntVar binding).
At end-of-trace, _finalize_spec_wiring raises if any pending entry still references unbound IntVars — i.e. the spec is unresolvable.
The same _shape_spec_pending_assumptions machinery is reused in a follow-up PR for user-provided ShapesSpec.assumptions=[A + B > 10].

### Tests
TestDerivedDimSpec in test/dynamo/test_dynamic_spec.py covers: correct + violating shapes (basic + multi-var), orphan-IntVar error, derived scalar args, foreign SymInt rejection at construction, misuse at spec-definition time, order independence (composite-before-bare), identity dedup via shared derived expression.

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
## Problem

The full document agent (`agent_definitions/document.yaml`) burns $0.03–$0.04 and 500+ seconds on internal-only tickets (model changes, plumbing, refactors) performing classification that requires zero tool calls. The agent is provisioned with `explore`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `list_dir`, and `edit_file` tools and a `request_limit=8` — but internal-only diffs need none of this. Worse, the agent sometimes hits its `request_limit` and exhausts `UsageLimitExceeded` retries before producing a simple "internal-only" verdict.

Three real tickets exhibit this:
- `20260524T112124Z` (test-gap unit tests for config.py): ~10,729 input tokens, $0.0042, zero tool calls used.
- `20260524T235832Z` (forbid refactoring prompt change): $0.0062, 73.5s, 30 obs, zero tool calls.
- `20260525T092428Z` (board_id on Ticket model): $0.0368, 551.3s, 125 obs, 2× `UsageLimitExceeded`.

## Scope

### 1. Classifier output model (`src/robotsix_mill/agents/documenting.py` lines 21–33)

`DocClassifierResult(BaseModel)` — a separate type from `DocResult` because the classifier only classifies; it never edits docs:
- `user_facing: bool` — same semantics as `DocResult.user_facing`.
- `classification: str` — a one-line human-readable classification (e.g. `"internal-only — model field rename"`, `"user-facing — new CLI flag"`). `min_length=1`.

`DocResult` (lines 35–63) is unchanged.

### 2. Classifier YAML definition (`agent_definitions/doc_classifier.yaml`)

Follows the existing `triage.yaml` pattern:
- `name: doc_classifier`, `category: pipeline`
- `tools: []`, `web: false`, `report_issue: false`, `skills: []`
- `model: "${MILL_DOC_CLASSIFIER_MODEL}"` — resolved via `os.environ.get()` in `yaml_loader.py`; falls back to `settings.doc_classifier_model` in Python when the env var is unset.
- `output_type: DocClassifierResult`
- `retries: 2`
- `module: documenting` (same module as `DocResult`).
- System prompt: inspect the diff + spec, classify as user-facing or internal-only. Conservative bias: when uncertain, classify as user-facing.

### 3. Classifier function (`src/robotsix_mill/agents/documenting.py` lines 65–110)

`run_doc_classifier(*, settings, diff, spec) -> DocClassifierResult`:
- Loads `agent_definitions/doc_classifier.yaml` via `load_agent_definition`.
- Builds agent via `build_agent_from_definition` with `tools=[]`, `model_name=definition.model or settings.doc_classifier_model`.
- User prompt: `<ticket_spec>…</ticket_spec>` + `<git_diff>…</git_diff>`.
- Passes `UsageLimits(request_limit=settings.doc_classifier_request_limit)`.
- Wraps in `call_with_retry(…, what="doc classifier")`.
- Closes agent in `finally` via `_safe_close`.

### 4. Config fields (`src/robotsix_mill/config.py` lines 228–237)

After `doc_request_limit` (line 228):
- `doc_classifier_model: str = Field(default="openai/gpt-4o-mini", alias="MILL_DOC_CLASSIFIER_MODEL")` — line 232.
- `doc_classifier_request_limit: int = Field(default=3, alias="MILL_DOC_CLASSIFIER_REQUEST_LIMIT")` — line 235.

### 5. Env-var mapping (`src/robotsix_mill/config_loader.py` — `_YAML_PATH_TO_ALIAS`)

Already present:
- `"core.models.doc_classifier": "MILL_DOC_CLASSIFIER_MODEL"` — inserted after `"core.models.doc": "MILL_DOC_MODEL"`.
- `"core.limits.doc_classifier_requests": "MILL_DOC_CLASSIFIER_REQUEST_LIMIT"` — inserted after `"core.limits.dedup_requests": "MILL_DEDUP_REQUEST_LIMIT"`.

### 6. YAML defaults entries (`config/mill.defaults.yaml`)

**Gap:** The following entries are missing from `mill.defaults.yaml` and must be added so these settings can be overridden via YAML config layers (`mill.local.yaml`, `mill.production.yaml`):
- Under `core.models`, after `doc: *default_model` (line ~40): add `doc_classifier: *cheap_model` — reusing the existing `&cheap_model` anchor (`openai/gpt-4o-mini`).
- Under `core.limits`, after `dedup_requests: 4` (line ~49): add `doc_classifier_requests: 3`.

Without these entries, `doc_classifier_model` and `doc_classifier_request_limit` can only be set via actual environment variables (or their Python defaults) — they cannot be set via YAML config layers. The feature works correctly without these entries (Python defaults apply), but the config surface is incomplete.

### 7. Two-phase document stage (`src/robotsix_mill/stages/document.py` lines 55–120)

After computing the diff (and confirming it's non-empty), `DocumentStage.run()` runs the lightweight classifier *first*:

1. Call `self._run_doc_classifier(settings=s, diff=diff, spec=spec)` → `DocClassifierResult`.
2. Record the classifier's verdict in ticket history: `ctx.service.add_comment(ticket.id, f"classifier: {result.classification}", author="doc_classifier")`.
3. **If `user_facing=False`**: return `Outcome(State.DELIVERABLE, f"no user-facing changes ({result.classification})")` — skip the full doc agent entirely.
4. **If `user_facing=True`**: proceed to the existing `_run_doc_agent(…)` call, unchanged.

Classifier call is wrapped in its own try/except with warn-and-pass semantics: if the classifier raises, a warning is logged (`exc_info=True`) and the stage falls through to the full doc agent.

Two internal helper methods (lines 122–174):
- `_run_doc_classifier(self, *, settings, diff, spec) -> DocClassifierResult` — thin wrapper calling `run_doc_classifier`.
- `_run_doc_agent(self, *, settings, repo_dir, diff, spec, model_name=None, extra_roots=None) -> DocResult` — thin wrapper calling `run_doc_agent` (extracted from inline code).

### 8. Tests (`tests/stages/test_document.py` lines 254–370)

Four new classifier-specific tests, all using `monkeypatch` to mock the classifier helper:
- **`test_classifier_internal_skips_full_agent`** — classifier returns `user_facing=False` → stage returns DELIVERABLE, full doc agent never called, no commit.
- **`test_classifier_user_facing_runs_full_agent`** — classifier returns `user_facing=True` → full doc agent runs, commits doc changes.
- **`test_classifier_exception_falls_through_to_full_agent`** — classifier raises → full doc agent still runs (warn-and-pass).
- **`test_classifier_verdict_recorded_in_history`** — verify `ctx.service.add_comment` is called with `author="doc_classifier"` and the classifier's classification string.

All 13 tests (9 existing + 4 new) pass (`pytest tests/stages/test_document.py -v`).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Internal-only fast path**: A ticket whose diff is purely internal completes the document stage with a single cheap LLM call. The full doc agent is never invoked.
2. **Cost & latency**: The classifier call completes in <15s and costs <$0.005 for internal-only diffs (target: ≤$0.002 based on `openai/gpt-4o-mini` pricing of $0.15/1M input + $0.60/1M output for a ~10K-token prompt).
3. **User-facing path unchanged**: When the classifier returns `user_facing=True`, the full document agent runs exactly as it does today — same tools, same model, same `request_limit`.
4. **Auditability**: The classifier's verdict is posted as a ticket comment with `author="doc_classifier"` containing the `classification` string, visible in ticket history.
5. **Classifier failure is non-blocking**: If the classifier call raises (model unavailable, parse error after retries), the stage logs a warning and falls through to the full doc agent — no tickets are blocked by classifier issues.
6. **Empty diff unchanged**: Empty diffs still skip both classifier and full agent, returning DELIVERABLE immediately.
7. **Existing tests pass**: All 13 `test_document.py` tests pass.
8. **YAML defaults present**: `config/mill.defaults.yaml` includes `doc_classifier` under `core.models` and `doc_classifier_requests` under `core.limits` so these settings are overridable via YAML config layers.

## Out of scope / constraints

- The classifier's output type (`DocClassifierResult`) is **not** shared with the triage classifier — they have different output schemas (`TriageResult` vs `DocClassifierResult`).
- The full document agent's YAML (`agent_definitions/document.yaml`), tools, and prompt are **not

## Summary

- Adds an **`All Checks`** aggregator job to `ci.yml` that depends on the four existing CI jobs (`markdown-lint`, `schema-validate`, `link-check`, `conventional-commits`).

author: shaggywize63
body:
## Summary
Backend half of the Phase 3 client-admin UI for the per-client org hierarchy.

Every endpoint (except the lightweight `/enabled` probe) returns **404** when the active client hasn't opted in to hierarchy RBAC. **Tata Tiscon never sees this surface** — the dashboard hides the menu entry too, but the gate is enforced server-side regardless.

### Routes (all under `/api/v1/crm/hierarchy`)
- `GET /enabled` → `{ enabled: boolean }` — used by the dashboard nav to decide whether to render the entry.
- `GET /levels` → list levels for the active client (sorted by `level_order`).
- `POST /levels` → create a new level. Validates `name` + `level_order`.
- `PATCH /levels/:id` → rename, reorder, change parent / capabilities.
- `DELETE /levels/:id` → **409 IN_USE** when any user is still assigned to the level.
- `GET /members` → users in the active client + their `hierarchy_level_id` / `supervisor_id`.
- `PATCH /members/:id` → set `hierarchy_level_id` and/or `supervisor_id`. Refuses **self-loop** and **cycle that would re-parent a user onto their own descendant** (subtree check via the `user_subtree_ids` RPC from #55).

### Files
- `src/routes/crm.routes.ts` — additive only. No existing routes touched.

### Tata Tiscon impact
Zero. The middleware gate evaluates to false on every request, so each endpoint returns 404 exactly the same way it does for any unknown URL.

## Test plan
- [ ] As **Tata Tiscon** user: `GET /api/v1/crm/hierarchy/enabled` → `{ enabled: false }`. Every other hierarchy URL → 404.
- [ ] As **Kinematic** user: `GET /api/v1/crm/hierarchy/enabled` → `{ enabled: true }`. CRUD on levels works. Members listing populates. Self-loop / cycle attempts return 400 CYCLE.
- [ ] `DELETE /levels/:id` while a user is assigned → 409 IN_USE.

author: duljamarin
body:
## Summary
Fixed an issue where the exchange rate was being unnecessarily re-fetched when editing an existing transaction with a non-EUR currency. The problem was caused by comparing a state value against a regular variable, which would always be stale on subsequent renders.

## Key Changes
- Converted `initialCurrency` from a regular variable to a `useRef` hook (`initialCurrencyRef`)
- Updated the comparison in the exchange rate effect to use `initialCurrencyRef.current` instead of `initialCurrency`
- Added `useRef` to the imports from React

## Implementation Details
The issue occurred because `initialCurrency` was assigned the value of `currencyCode` on every render, making it impossible to compare against the initial currency value in the effect. By using `useRef`, the initial currency value is now captured once and persists across renders, allowing the effect to correctly skip the auto-fetch when editing an existing transaction that already has an exchange rate set.

author: chemaclass
body:
## 📚 Description

Auto-engaged perf mode for big terminals (ultrawides, full-screen 4K, etc.) so the play loop stays responsive at sizes like 400×60. Standard terminal sizes (80×24, 120×30, 180×40) are untouched — exact 1:1 60fps render path stays the default.

**Threshold**: `cols >= 200` OR `cols * rows > 12000`. Pure function of terminal dimensions, read per frame from `term-size`.

## 🔖 Changes

Three commits, smallest impact / simplest first:

1. **`perf(render): cap minimap absolute width at 40 cols`** — `max(8, min(40, cols/3))` instead of `max(8, cols/3)`. A 133-col minimap on a 400-col terminal is not useful. No-op on small terminals (vw/3 already < 40).

2. **`perf(loop): adaptive 30fps cadence on big terminals`** — introduces `phel-doom.modules.core.perf` with `perf-mode?` + `target-frame-us`. Game loop measures iter-start, renders, then `adaptive-sleep!` yields whatever's left of the per-iteration budget (16.67ms small / 33.33ms big). Physics + input still tick once per loop so gameplay stays responsive.

3. **`perf(render): virtual-width 2x emit on big terminals`** — `cast-frame` grows an optional `scale` arity (default 1, exact 1:1 path). With `scale=2` one ray is cast every 2nd output column and replicated across the pair; halves cast + downstream wall-shade work. Sprites + HUD still emit at full vw so the chunky look is contained to the wall band.

## 🧪 Test plan

- [x] `composer ci` — format, lint, 823 tests, build (all green)
- [x] New tests: `perf-test.phel` (13 cases) — threshold predicates, cadence, scale factor
- [x] New tests: `engine-test.phel` — `cast-frame` `scale=2` arity, odd-width leftover, scale=1 matches default
- [x] Manual smoke on a small terminal (80×24 / 120×30) — verify no visual change
- [ ] Manual smoke on a wide terminal (300+ cols) — verify chunky-but-readable walls, smooth 30fps motion, smaller minimap

author: alextorq
body:
## Summary
- Cosmetic logging fix. `backgroundSync` logged "Фоновая синхронизация источников запущена" (INFO) from a goroutine launched **before** `settingsModule.HydrateAll()` applied the persisted `log_level`. With `log_level=WARN` the "started" line slipped through at the default INFO while the matching "finished"/"filter refreshed" lines (logged after hydrate) were suppressed — making a healthy sync look stuck.
- Move the `go backgroundSync(...)` launch to after `HydrateAll()`, so its lifecycle log lines all honor the effective log level. Still non-blocking and still before `dnsServer.Serve()`; no functional change to the sync itself.

## Problem

The root package.json had a "build" script set to "node backend/migrate.js". Railpack detects this script and executes it during the build phase, where the database is not yet accessible, causing the build to fail with "getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND postgres.railway.internal".

## Solution

Removed the "build" script from the root package.json. Migrations require a live database connection and must not run at build time. The nixpacks.toml already defines the correct build and start commands, and migrations can be run manually via "npm run migrate" in the backend directory when needed.

The feature is visible through authenticated self-serve workspace settings and first-login onboarding. It is not added to the public J&J demo seed because OAuth setup requires private provider credentials, customer accounts, and provider-console approvals that are unsafe to seed publicly.

author: karanbalani
body:
## Summary

When we deploy a new SigNoz version, all cloud deployments call Zeus at the same instant. Then every 6 hours after that, they all call again together. This creates large traffic spikes on Zeus that scale with our fleet size.

This PR spreads those calls evenly across time so Zeus sees a manageable rate instead of synchronized bursts.

## How it works

A single `Jitter` value controls the randomness applied to both the first call after startup and every subsequent cycle:

```
First fire = startup + random(0, Jitter)
Next fire  = previous + (Interval − random(0, Jitter))
```

- The first call after startup is delayed by a random amount in `[0, Jitter)` — different on every pod.
- Each subsequent cycle takes `Interval − random(0, Jitter)`, so the time between any two consecutive reports is between `Interval − Jitter` and `Interval`.
- The strict upper bound is still `Interval`, so every deployment is guaranteed to report at least once in any rolling `Interval`-sized window.
- A failed cycle (Zeus down, network blip, single collector failure) does **not** stop the loop — the next cycle still fires on schedule, and the existing checkpoint + backfill machinery catches up any missed sealed days.

## New config

| Field | Default | Bounds | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meterreporter.interval` | `6h` | `[10m, 24h]` | How often each deployment reports |
| `meterreporter.jitter` | `min(Interval, 2h)` | `[10m, Interval]` | Randomness on first run and per cycle |

`Jitter` defaults are derived from `Interval` at use time — you don't need to touch it. Override `Interval` alone and the jitter scales to a sensible value automatically.

### What you get for common configurations

| You set | Resulting `Jitter` |
|---|---|
| (nothing) | 2h (= min(6h, 2h)) |
| `INTERVAL=10m` | 10m (capped at Interval) |
| `INTERVAL=1h` | 1h (capped at Interval) |
| `INTERVAL=24h` | 2h |
| `INTERVAL=6h`, `JITTER=1h` | 1h (explicit) |

### Env var names

`jitter` has no underscores in the field name.

```bash
SIGNOZ_METERREPORTER_INTERVAL=10m
SIGNOZ_METERREPORTER_JITTER=10m
```

## Why this is safe

Correctness is unchanged — only *when* reports are sent changes, never *what* is sent. Three existing mechanisms cover any deferral or repetition:

- **Idempotency key** per (org, day) — Zeus dedupes duplicate calls within the same UTC day
- **Backfill** — any sealed day that gets missed is shipped on the next cycle
- **Checkpoint API** — Zeus tells us what's already been received, so we never re-ship accepted days

## Impact

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Peak Zeus calls/minute after a rolling deploy | ~1500 | ~12.5/min for 2h |
| Sustained Zeus call rate (after ~1.7 days) | spike + 0 + spike | ~4/min uniform |
| Total daily traffic | unchanged | ~20% more (idempotent, deduped by Zeus) |

That's roughly a **120× reduction** in worst-minute load on Zeus, with no change in correctness. After the fleet has diffused into a uniform distribution across the interval (~1.7 days post-deploy), Zeus sees the same steady rate as the no-spike theoretical ideal.

## Files changed

- `pkg/meterreporter/config.go` — single `Jitter` field, sentinel-based default that scales with `Interval`, `ResolvedJitter` helper
- `ee/meterreporter/httpmeterreporter/provider.go` — jittered `time.Timer` scheduler + observability logs

## Test plan

- [x] Verify defaults: with only `Interval=6h` set, `ResolvedJitter()` returns `2h`; with `Interval=10m` set, it returns `10m`
- [x] Confirm the "scheduling first meter collect" log shows a non-zero `delay` and `delay_ns` on startup
- [x] Confirm the "scheduled next meter collect" log appears after each cycle with delay between `Interval − Jitter` and `Interval`
- [x] In staging with `INTERVAL=10m`, observe at least 3 cycles to confirm per-cycle jitter is varying as expected
