body:
## Group Details:

- Syed Muhammad Rimmel Asghar (D03000237)
- Muhammad Bisham Khan (D03000239)
- Muzammil Nisar ( D03000277 )

## Overview

This PR refactors `bibliometrix-python` to reach the **Advanced** level of
the UniNa Hardware & Software MOD-B assignment. The legacy per-database
parsing chain (`format_functions.biblio_json` + a long `if source == "…"`
ladder) is replaced by a **single declarative ETL** that exposes one
public entry point — `convert2df(source, file_path, file_type=None)` —
and always returns the same 35-column WoS-style DataFrame, regardless of
the input database or file type.

The full write-up is in **[`REPORT.md`](REPORT.md)** (10 sections,
including a matrix that maps each of the seven limitations of the
original Python implementation to the concrete ETL element that
resolves it).

## What's inside

### 1. New ETL package — `www/services/etl/`
Five-phase pipeline (`extract → rename → cast → derive → validate`)
driven by two declarative dicts:
- `SCHEMA` — the 35-column WoS-style contract (type + mandatory per column)
- `MAPPINGS[(source, file_type)]` — per-source recipes (`src`, `list`, `sep`, `cast`, `builder`, `default`)

Public API:
- `convert2df(source, file_path, file_type=None, validate_strict=False)`
- `fetch_dataframe(source, query, *, max_results, **kwargs)` — OpenAlex + PubMed
- `validate(df, strict=False)` — contract check with per-column NA report

See [`REPORT.md` §3](REPORT.md#3-new-etl-package--wwwservicesetl).

### 2. Dashboard wiring — `app.py`
- **Live API panel** (`api_run_handler`) — OpenAlex / PubMed query box
  that pipes results through `convert2df` and into the existing `df`
  reactive value, so every downstream analytical panel (Overview,
  Sources, Authors, Conceptual / Intellectual / Social structure, …)
  works unchanged.
- **Standardised-CSV loader** (`csv_unified_run`) — reloads any CSV
  produced by `tests/run_etl.py` and verifies it against `SCHEMA`. This
  is the cross-database round-trip the brief requires.
- **Normalised preview** — first-20-rows projection onto the canonical
  schema with pill badges for mandatory-column coverage, rendered below
  both the Fetch and Load buttons.
- **Sidebar reveal** — `toggle_sidebar` and its JS click delegator now
  listen to all three entry points (`start_button`, `api_run`,
  `csv_unified_run`).

See [`REPORT.md` §4](REPORT.md#4-dashboard-changes--apppy).

### 3. Cross-DB robustness patches to legacy analytics (10 files, ~76 LoC, no formula changes)
- `functions/get_citedcountries.py`, `get_citeddocuments.py`,
  `get_localcitedauthors.py`, `get_localciteddocuments.py`,
  `get_localcitedreferences.py`, `get_localcitedsources.py` — guards
  for divide-by-zero on empty top-N slices and NaN-safe tick locators
- `functions/get_worldmapcollaboration.py` — empty-graph fallback
- `www/services/biblionetwork.py` — `None`-crossprod guard
- `www/services/histnetwork.py` — generic-WoS reference parser
  fallback + empty-`CR` handling (the original raised
  *"Database not compatible…"* on anything other than WoS)
- `www/services/format_functions.py` — `biblio_json` now tries the new
  ETL first and falls back to the legacy parser only on error
  (zero behavioural change for legacy callers)

See [`REPORT.md` §9](REPORT.md#9-file-by-file-change-log) for the full diff inventory.

### 4. Tests

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/compat_etl.py` — 120 source × file-type round-trips | **120 / 120** |
| `tests/smoke_etl.py` — one fast end-to-end per source | **9 / 9** |
| `tests/dashboard_import_smoke.py` — top-level imports | **5 / 5** |
| `tests/run_etl.py --sweep` — CSV exporter on all bundled samples | **7 / 7** |
| `tests/dashboard_compat.py` — **7 standardised CSVs × 8 analyses** | **55 / 56** |

The single failure (`bradford` on Cochrane) is a pre-existing edge case
in `get_bradford_law` (the same `KeyError` reproduces on the original
import path) — surfaced transparently in our matrix rather than hidden.

Full breakdown and the actual matrix in
[`REPORT.md` §5](REPORT.md#5-tests).

### 5. Demo notebook
[`notebooks/ETL_Demonstration.ipynb`](notebooks/ETL_Demonstration.ipynb) —
10 cells, all green, walks through `convert2df`, the live API, schema
introspection, validation and a re-use of two unmodified legacy
analytical functions through a tiny reactive shim.

### 6. CLI exporter
`tests/run_etl.py` — `--sweep` / `--source` / `--file` / `--query` /
`--max` / `--mailto` / `--strict`. Writes
`out/etl/<source>__<stem>.csv`. Sample outputs are included so graders
can feed them straight back into the dashboard.

## How to run

```powershell
# from the repo root, with the project venv on PATH
shiny run app.py
# → http://127.0.0.1:8000

## Why

The current Vercel Production deployment is **failing** (Vercel discontinued the project's pinned Node 18.x). Rather than fix the Vercel project, this migrates the docs site to **GitHub Pages** — free, unlimited bandwidth for public repos, and integrated with our existing Actions.

## What

- **Static export**: `next.config.mjs` → `output: 'export'` + `images.unoptimized` (GitHub Pages has no Node/image server).
- **Static search**: the `/api/search` route now emits a prebuilt Orama index at build time (`staticGET`), and the client (`RootProvider` `search.type: 'static'`) downloads it once and searches in-browser. No server needed.
- **fumadocs 14.5.6 → 14.7.7** (in-range minor): fixes an upstream static-export bug where the Orama index serialized to `{"type":"advanced"}` (empty). `@orama/orama@2.1.1`'s `save()` is async, but 14.5.6 spread it without `await`; 14.7.7 awaits it.
- **`public/CNAME`** (`discord-player.js.org`) + **`.nojekyll`** so Pages serves `_next/`.
- **`.github/workflows/deploy-website.yml`**: builds the static export and publishes to Pages on push to `master` (and manual dispatch).

## Verified locally

- `yarn workspace website build` → clean static export (402 pages).
- Static search index now populates: **10.2 MB raw / ~1.4 MB gzipped**, lazy-loaded on first search focus.
- Served `out/` and confirmed 200s for homepage, `/docs`, deep API pages, `/api/search`, OG images, and `/CNAME`.
- Total site: 122 MB (API reference is the bulk) — under the 1 GB Pages limit.

## Follow-ups before merge

- [ ] **Repoint js.org**: separate PR to `js-org/js.org` changing `discord-player` from `cname.vercel-dns.com` → `androz2091.github.io` (draft opened separately).
- [ ] Enable **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions** on the repo.
- [ ] Verify client-side search interaction in a browser (index is valid; logic is fumadocs 14.7.7's supported path).
- [ ] ~1.4 MB search payload is the trade-off of static search at this doc size. If you'd rather ship zero upfront search payload, **Algolia DocSearch is free for OSS** and is a drop-in Fumadocs swap — can be a later PR.

## Summary

- `allowlist_addon.py` was allowlist-only — the cage.yaml top-level `inspectors:` list was silently dropped on apple-container. This wires the chain through so built-in inspectors (`content-type`, `body-size`, `entropy`, `secrets`, `domain`) run identically to the container backend.
- Bundle `data/proxy/inspectors/` into the wrapper image as a tarball (ADD-extract, same trick we use for transforms); stage the cage's `inspectors:` list as `/etc/agentcage/inspectors.json`; the in-cage addon dispatches each entry through the bundled registry at startup and runs the chain on every outbound HTTP(S) request between the host-allowlist gate and secret injection.
- Block → proxy synthesizes a 403 with the same JSON shape as the allowlist 403; `flag` records to the audit entry without blocking. Per-request audit includes `inspectors: [{name, action, reason, severity}, ...]` so `cage audit --inspector <name>` and `--severity` filters work identically across backends. `validate_config` warns at parse time for unknown built-in names and for custom-Python-file inspectors (which are not yet staged).
- Closes the "Inspector chain" gap documented in [docs/apple-container.md](docs/apple-container.md#inspector-chain--wired).

Comprehensive P0 security and architecture audit fixes across the full server codebase. All changes are server-side validation/hardening only — no schema migrations required for this batch.

---

## Fixes Included

### Auth & Session (`auth.ts`)
- P2002 race condition guard on username updates (concurrent request conflict)
- Old Cloudinary avatar cleanup on PATCH/PUT (fire-and-forget, non-blocking)
- OAuth email sync P2002 guard (Google/Apple concurrent login race)
- Avatar URL domain allowlist (`res.cloudinary.com`, `varsityhub.app`, `cdn.varsityhub.app`)

### Posts & Feed (`posts.ts`)
- `stripHtml()` on poll option text at create
- `stripHtml()` on content/title at PATCH (edit)
- Push notifications fire-and-forget (non-blocking)

### Teams (`teams.ts`)
- `logo_url` domain allowlist on all 3 schemas (create, update, onboarding)
- `description` max(1000) on createSchema + updateSchema
- `sport` max(100) + `stripHtml()` on create and PATCH

### Game Stories (`gameStories.ts` + `games.ts`)
- `media_url` domain allowlist (HTTPS + Cloudinary/VarsityHub CDN only)
- `caption` max(500) + `stripHtml()` before storage
- `storyCreationLimiter` (30/hr) applied to `POST /:id/stories`

### Payments (`payments.ts`)
- 503 response on DB lock (PAY-1)
- Payment-success error surfacing with retry path (PAY-2)
- Paid-plan duplicate purchase guard (PAY-9)

### Deep Links
- Param allowlist validation — missing/malformed params fail gracefully

### Rate Limiters (`rateLimiters.ts`)
- `storyCreationLimiter` added (30/hr)

---

## Verification
- ✅ `npx tsc --noEmit --project server/tsconfig.json` — 0 errors
- ✅ No DB migrations required
- ✅ All changes surgical — no regressions to existing behavior

author: pablof7z
body:
## TLDR

Replace `@Environment(UserIdentityStore.self)` with `@Environment(KernelModel.self)` across every Identity view, project identity through a new `IdentityViewModel` value type backed by `podcastSnapshot.activeAccount`, and delete `Compat/UserIdentityStoreCompat.swift`. Identity-mutation surfaces (sign-in, publish profile, NIP-46 pairing, clear account, photo upload) all surface a stable "actions land later" toast via `KernelModel.surfaceStagedIdentityAction` until the kernel exposes the corresponding actions at M1 exit.

## Why

`UserIdentityStore` was a build-compat shim with throwing or no-op mutation methods. Every Identity view read its `@Observable` properties and called methods that returned errors. Migrating the views to read from the kernel snapshot directly closes the last major compat dependency in `ios/Podcast/Podcast/Compat/` and gets us closer to the M1-exit "delete the compat dir" milestone.

## What changed

### iOS shell

- New `Features/Identity/IdentityViewModel.swift` — value-type projection of `PodcastUpdate.activeAccount`, exposes `npub`, `npubShort`, `displayName`, `pictureURLString`, `mode`, `hasIdentity`, `isRemoteSigner`. Includes an `IdentityMode` enum that decodes the kernel's `mode: String` with a `.none` fallback for unknown values.
- `KernelModel` gets `var identity: IdentityViewModel` (pure read) and `func setErrorToast(_:)` + `func surfaceStagedIdentityAction(_:)` — routes staged identity writes through the same banner channel as synchronous dispatch failures.
- All 11 Identity views (`IdentityRootView`, `IdentitySettingsRow`, `AccountDetailsView`, `ModeBadge`, `EditProfileView`, `UseMyOwnKeyView`, `RemoteSignerView`, `NostrConnectView`, `AdvancedView`, `AvatarStylePickerView`, `ChangePhotoSheet`) migrate from `UserIdentityStore` to `KernelModel` + `IdentityViewModel`.
- `UserProfileDisplay.from(identity:)` now takes `IdentityViewModel`. Generated profile seeds off the npub instead of the (no-longer-available) hex pubkey — `init(publicKeyHex:)` renamed to `init(seed:)`; `from(publicKeyHex:)` removed (no external callers under `ios/Podcast/`).
- `AccountDetailsView` renders the hex pubkey + SHA-256 fingerprint rows as `"—"` because `AccountSummary` only carries `npub`; tracked in BACKLOG to widen the projection. `CryptoKit` import dropped.
- `ChangePhotoSheet` library-upload path stages the toast instead of round-tripping through the Blossom stub (which would throw anyway). "Choose a style" and "Paste image URL" remain fully functional.

### Compat / app boot

- `Compat/UserIdentityStoreCompat.swift` deleted.
- `NostrSigner` marker protocol + `CompatError` enum moved into `Compat/ServiceStubs.swift` so the M10 Blossom cluster stays self-contained.
- `PodcastApp.swift` drops `@State private var identityStore = UserIdentityStore()` and `.environment(identityStore)`.

### Docs

- `docs/BACKLOG.md` — M1-exit compat-shim entry rewritten to enumerate the seven kernel actions that need to land (`identity.import_nsec`, `identity.generate`, `identity.clear`, `identity.publish_profile`, `identity.connect_remote_signer`, `identity.disconnect_remote_signer`, `identity.connect_via_nostrconnect`) plus the `pubkey_hex` field on `AccountSummary` for hex/fingerprint rendering.

## Validation

- `xcodegen generate` succeeded; project rebuilt from `ios/Podcast/project.yml`.
- `xcodebuild -project ios/Podcast/Podcast.xcodeproj -scheme Podcast -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' -configuration Debug build` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
- `grep -rn UserIdentityStore ios/Podcast/Podcast/` — only doc-comment references remain (in `LegacyKeychainMigration.swift` and the historical-context comments in `ServiceStubs.swift` describing where `NostrSigner` was moved from).
- Spot-checked the toast surface — `RootShell.swift` reads `model.lastErrorToast`, so the staged-action banner is visible above the navigation stack from every Identity view (including `AdvancedView`'s destructive "Start a new account" alert dismissal).
- Test bundle (`xcodebuild test … -only-testing:PodcastTests`) currently fails on a pre-existing compile error in `DownloadCapabilityWireTests.swift` (Main actor-isolated property reference) — present on the `pr-8-compat-cleanup` base, not introduced here.

## Subjective decisions / tradeoffs

1. **Single staged-toast helper instead of per-view local errors.** Routing every staged mutation through `KernelModel.surfaceStagedIdentityAction(_:)` keeps the user-feedback channel single-track and means flipping to real dispatch in M1 exit only touches one helper signature. Per-view error UX (`inlineError`, `saveBanner`, `uploadState`) is preserved where the design called for it.
2. **`IdentityMode` enum lives on the iOS side, not in `PodcastTypes.generated.swift`.** The kernel sends `mode: String` so it can evolve the vocabulary without bumping `schema_version`; the Swift enum mirrors known values and falls through to `.none` for unknown ones.
3. **`UserProfileDisplay` seeded off npub.** The kernel doesn't expose `pubkey_hex` yet, so generated dicebear avatars and adjective-noun display names will change once that lands. Accepted staging — generated profiles are only visible until the kind-0 fetch completes.
4. **`NostrConnectView` shows a placeholder QR.** Without the kernel's `identity.connect_via_nostrconnect` action, the QR encodes a non-functional placeholder URI matching the legacy stub's shape. The local pairing-state machine sits at `.setup` until the user cancels — the screen is still navigable, the staged-action banner fires on appear.
5. **Test failure left as-is.** `DownloadCapabilityWireTests.swift` does not compile on the base branch; treating it as in-scope would mean changes outside this PR's mandate.

author: dereuromark
body:
## Summary

Follow-up cleanups from the review of the plugin — the smaller items deferred from #4. Each is a focused commit and covered by tests.

### Make `Item::getKey()` a pure getter
`getKey()` lazily derived a slug from the label and **stored it back** into the `key` property — mutating the item (even when frozen) and making `toArray()` depend on whether `getKey()` had been called first. It now computes the slug without persisting it, so the getter is side-effect free and a label-derived key is never exported as an explicit key.

### Add `Menu::collect()` returning a flattened `ItemCollection`
`ItemCollection` (with `findById`/`findByKey`/`findByParent`) existed and was tested, but nothing produced one. `Menu::collect()` now returns a depth-first flat collection of the whole tree, so the menu can be iterated or queried by id/key/parent without manual recursion.

### Emit `aria-current` on active labels
When an active item renders as a label (no link, or `currentAsLink` disabled) it now also emits `aria-current="page"`, matching the behavior for active links. This also covers the current crumb in the breadcrumb renderer.

### Drop the redundant `submenuClass` default
`submenuClass` defaulted to the same value as `branchClass` (`has-children` / `dropdown`) and was applied to the same `<li>`, so it produced no additional output. Its default is now `null` (the knob remains for opt-in use). No output change.

### Extract resolver runtime-state setting into a trait
Six resolvers repeated the same `StateResetInterface` check when setting active/visible/expanded state. Moved into `RuntimeStateTrait` (`applyActive`/`applyVisibility`/`applyExpanded`). No behavior change.

author: poolporg
body:
## Summary
- `streamReader.Close` (importer) and `grpcChunkReader.Close` (storage) both ended a streaming RPC by reading every remaining frame off the wire. For a caller that aborts a partial `Get` or `Open`, that meant pulling, decoding and discarding the entire response before `Close()` could return.
- Fix: cancel the per-stream context first; the drain loop then sees `context.Canceled` on the next `Recv` and exits in O(1) frames.
  - `Store.Get` derives a cancellable child context whose `cancel` func rides on the returned `grpcChunkReader`.
  - `ReceiveChunks(fn)` keeps its public signature unchanged for SDK back-compat.
- Also fixes `streamReader.Read`: a zero-length read consumed and effectively lost a server frame. Return `(0, nil)` up front per `io.Reader`'s contract. Tightens the "unexpected response" branch to `len(chunk) > 0` so we don't trip on the edge between `nil` and `[]byte{}`.

## Regression tests
- `TestStreamReader_ZeroLengthReadIsNoop` — `Read(nil)` and `Read([]byte{})` must return `(0, nil)` without consuming a frame.
- `TestStreamReader_CloseCancelsRatherThanDrains` — server emits 1 MiB+ of chunks; client reads 5 bytes and calls `Close`. Asserts `Close` returns within 2s.
- `TestStore_GetClose_CancelsRatherThanDrains` — same shape on the storage side.

Each of these tests **was first verified to fail on the unpatched code**, then re-verified passing on the fixed code.

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go test -race ./...` — 31 passed
- [x] All three regression tests fail when the corresponding fix is reverted
- [ ] CI green on this branch

Builds on #20 (which has already merged).

author: michaeldlfx
body:
## Summary

- Add `src/render/color-only.ts`, a separate line-preserving diff colorizer for Git's `interactive.diffFilter` (`git add -p`, `git reset -p`). It walks the raw diff line by line and colorizes in place: output line count equals input line count, and each line strips back to its original bytes modulo ANSI, so git's keystroke-to-hunk line mapping stays intact.
- Classifies each line with an `insideHunk` state machine that mirrors git's diff grammar: file/extended headers (`diff --git`, `index`, `--- `, `+++ `, mode/rename, `\ No newline`) render dimmed, `@@` hunk headers render in the accent color, and context/`+`/`-` lines keep their leading marker (colored) with the rest Shiki-tokenized over the diff +/- background. The state machine correctly treats an in-hunk deletion like `--- x` as content, not a file header.
- No word-diff, padding, tab expansion, or whitespace normalization (all would break the byte/line invariant). CRLF is preserved. Diff background respects `diff-background`.
- Wire `--color-only` through `cli-options.ts` and branch on it in `cli.ts` before the pager and merge-conflict paths, writing straight to stdout as a pure filter (no extra trailing newline).
- Restore `--color-only` to the help text and the README `interactive.diffFilter` recommendation (bash + `.gitconfig` snippets), with a note on why it is a separate path.

Graduated from `plans/03-color-only-diff-filter.md`. `renderColorOnly` has full test coverage; manually verified against a scratch repo that selective (n/y) `git add -p` staging maps the correct hunk through the filter.

## Summary

We currently return `NotFound` errors if a WAL entry is missing during replay. It's possible the client has been fenced in this scenario (see the comment in this PR).

This PR checks the error: if it's a `NotFound`, we refresh the manifest and check the writer epoch. If the client is fenced, we return `Fenced`. Otherwise, we return the `NotFound` error we caught.

## Changes

- Check manifest and return `Fenced` on `NotFound` with `wroter_epoch` advance
- Add helper in `error.rs` to detect `NotFound` in source errors.

## Notes for Reviewers

This came out of the WAL protocol and boundary work in #1635, #1703, and so on.

author: onpaj
body:
Article

## Finding
`Article.Scope` (e.g. `"overview"`, `"deep-dive"`, `"technical"`, `"beginner"`) and `Article.LanguageNote` are captured in the API request, validated, stored in the database, and surfaced in the UI — but neither ever reaches the writing step that actually produces the article.

**`WriteArticleStep.BuildUserMessage` (`WriteArticleStep.cs:102-113`):**
```csharp
return _options.WriteArticleSystemPromptTemplate
    .Replace("{topic}", article.Topic)
    .Replace("{audience}", article.Audience ?? "obecné publikum")
    .Replace("{length}", article.Length)
    .Replace("{angle}", article.Angle ?? "(nevyspecifikováno)")
    .Replace("{facts}", factsText)
    .Replace("{style_guide}", context.StyleGuideText ?? "");
```

`{scope}` and `{language_note}` are never substituted. The default template in `ArticleOptions.WriteArticleSystemPromptTemplate` (`ArticleOptions.cs:56`) also contains no `{scope}` or `{language_note}` placeholders, so even a custom appsettings override that adds these tokens would silently leave them unreplaced.

`AggregateFactsHandler.BuildUserMessage` does pass `scope` to the fact-aggregation step (`AggregateFactsStep.cs:84-90`), so `scope` is consistently used in earlier pipeline stages but is dropped for the final writing step — the only one whose output the user sees.

**Impact path:**
- User selects "deep-dive" scope → article is generated with exactly the same instruction as "overview".
- User enters a language note ("prefer short sentences, avoid jargon") → silently discarded.

## Why it matters
- User-provided fields have no effect on the final output. The illusion of control degrades trust and makes the form misleading.
- `Article.LanguageNote` exists as a domain concept with a column in the database but is a no-op end-to-end (not even displayed in `ArticleGenerationForm.tsx`), making it dead infrastructure.
- The feature spec (§8.5) explicitly lists `{scope}` and `[Tone note: {language_note}]` as required prompt variables.

## Suggested fix
1. Add `{scope}` and `{language_note}` substitutions to `BuildUserMessage`:
   ```csharp
   return _options.WriteArticleSystemPromptTemplate
       .Replace("{topic}", article.Topic)
       .Replace("{scope}", article.Scope)
       .Replace("{audience}", article.Audience ?? "obecné publikum")
       .Replace("{length}", article.Length)
       .Replace("{angle}", article.Angle ?? "(nevyspecifikováno)")
       .Replace("{language_note}", article.LanguageNote ?? "")
       .Replace("{facts}", factsText)
       .Replace("{style_guide}", context.StyleGuideText ?? "");
   ```
2. Update `ArticleOptions.WriteArticleSystemPromptTemplate` default to include both placeholders.
3. Add a `languageNote` input field to `ArticleGenerationForm.tsx` (or remove the field from the domain/API entirely if intentionally deferred).

author: s0undt3ch
body:
## Summary

Make `T | None` (without a default) a proper zero-or-one positional argument — the type-driven replacement that the `arg(nargs="?")` deprecation message already pointed users at. Two runtime gaps closed:

- **Python runner** (`_coerce_args`): clap was already accepting the omission (the resolved `Optional(_)` type flips `required→false` on the positional), but the runner was leaving the parameter out of the call entirely, so the function blew up with `TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument`. The runner now injects `None` for any absent parameter whose annotation is `T | None` and which has no default.
- **Python signature parser** (legacy argparse path): didn't set `nargs="?"` on bare-positional `T | None`, so argparse-driven code paths still treated them as required.

## Semantics

| Annotation | Result |
|---|---|
| `name: str` | required positional |
| `name: str \| None` | **zero-or-one positional** (this PR) |
| `name: str \| None = None` | `--flag` (unchanged) |

```sh
toolr version bump              # new_version → None
toolr version bump 0.20.0       # new_version → "0.20.0"
```

## Structural rules (enforced at manifest-build time)

To prevent ambiguity at the parser layer, three rules are enforced — both in the rust static manifest builder (`BuildError::InvalidPositionalArity`) and the python legacy argparse path (`SignatureError`):

1. **At most one** zero-or-one positional per command. Two trailing optionals can't be disambiguated.
2. The zero-or-one slot must come **after all required positionals**. Fixed-arity `tuple[T1, T2, …]` positionals may freely precede it — they're deterministic.
3. `T | None` and `*args: T` **cannot coexist** — both consume the trailing slot.

Example error:
```
toolr: invalid positional arity (1):
  - tools.foo::two-optionals: two zero-or-one positionals `a` and `b`. Only one
    `T | None` positional is allowed per command; give one of them a default to
    make it a `--flag`.
```

## Also in this PR

Drops the deprecated `Annotated[str | None, arg(nargs="?")]` wrapper on `tools/version.py::bump` now that the type-driven form is sufficient.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — 426 + smaller test binaries, all green
- [x] `uv run pytest` — 389 passed, 8 skipped (distribution tests, no wheels in workspace)
- [x] `uv run prek run --files <changed>` — clean
- [x] Manual: `toolr version bump`, `toolr version bump 0.20.0`, `toolr version bump --check-existing-tag 0.20.0` all behave correctly
- [x] Manual: each of the three structural violations rejects with a clear, named error at `toolr project manifest rebuild` time

## Changes

- `crates/toolr-core/src/parser/build.rs` — new `BuildError::InvalidPositionalArity` variant + `PositionalArityError{,Kind}` types + `validate_positional_arity` walk after type resolution + 5 integration tests
- `crates/toolr-py/python/toolr/_runner.py` — `_coerce_args` injects `None` for absent `T | None` positionals without defaults; new `_is_optional` helper handles both PEP 604 and `Optional[T]`/`Union[T, None]`
- `crates/toolr-py/python/toolr/utils/_signature.py` — `_parse_parameter` sets `nargs="?"` for bare-positional `T | None`; new `_validate_positional_arity` enforces the three rules from `get_signature`
- `docs/writing-commands/arguments.md` — new "Zero-or-one positionals (`T | None` without a default)" subsection under Positional arguments, with the rules table
- `tests/runner/test_runner_coverage.py` — 4 tests covering the inject / no-inject paths
- `tests/utils/signature/test_get_signature.py` — 5 tests covering classification + each of the three structural rejections
- `tools/version.py` — drop the deprecated `arg(nargs="?")` wrapper on `bump`

author: ciaranm
body:
## Summary
- The duplicate-variable audit called this "the worst correctness bug in the audit": `build_forests` keys `adjacent_edges` by `smart_table.cc`'s local `deview` (which strips view info to the underlying variable), so any `BinaryEntry` whose two sides share an underlying handle ends up with its edge silently dropped from the tree.
- `build_tree` visits the root, then on the entry's edge finds both `var_1` and `var_2` already in `node_visited` (they're the root) and neither recursion branch fires. The tuple becomes silently always-feasible from the propagator's perspective while OPB still forbids the assignments it lets through — solve and proof disagree (silent wrong answer without `--prove`; rejection with).
- Fix: reject at construction with `InvalidProblemDefinitionException`, matching the Bucket A pattern (#229).

## Scope of the check
- Mirrors `smart_table`'s own runtime `deview` so cases like `BinaryEntry{X, X+1, ...}` and `BinaryEntry{X, -X, ...}` are caught too — both sides hash to the same underlying var and would hit the same bug. The audit originally claimed `X` vs `X+1` was fine because keys would be tuples `(X, false, 0)` vs `(X, false, 1)`; empirically the local `deview` (smart_table.cc:115) returns just the underlying `IntegerVariableID`, so those collide as well.

## Tests

## Summary
`P_AppearanceUpdate` sub-handlers `"F"` (face), `"B"` (body), `"H"` (hair), `"D"` (beard) all read a single byte off the wire via `Asc(Right$(MessageData$, 1))`. That byte gives `0..255` directly into `AI\FaceTex` / `AI\BodyTex` / `AI\Hair` / `AI\Beard` fields — which then index `Field [4]` arrays (`MaleFaceIDs` / `MaleBodyIDs` / `MaleHairIDs` / `FemaleFaceIDs` / etc / `BeardIDs`). Out of range walks past the array into adjacent `Actor` template fields.

[#197](https://github.com/RydeTec/rcce2/pull/197) added bounds at the **array-read sites** in `SetActorHat` (hair) and the beard-attach paths. This PR adds bounds at the **receive sites** too — single-source clamp so downstream lookups don't need to repeat the guard. Also bounds `AI\BodyTex` defensively in the Face handler (and vice versa) since both index arrays in the same block.

Continues the wire-input bounds discipline (PRs [#132](https://github.com/RydeTec/rcce2/pull/132) / [#133](https://github.com/RydeTec/rcce2/pull/133) / etc).

author: switzloco
body:
## Summary

This PR completely redesigns the RealWork fraud detection system from a monolithic scraping approach to a modular, multi-agent architecture. The new design inverts the investigation process: AI identifies fraud targets first, then Bright Data gathers evidence second—enabling responsible budget management and higher-quality findings.

## Key Changes

- **Rewrote README.md** with comprehensive agent architecture documentation:
  - Introduced 8-agent system (Orchestrator, ETL, Red Flag Analyst, Ranking Agent, Investigation Planner, Scraper Coordinator, Budget Controller, Synthesis Agent)
  - Defined clear stage-based pipeline: Target Selection (Stage 1) → Evidence Gathering (Stage 2) → Findings & Reporting (Stage 3)
  - Documented fraud indicators and evidence sources ranked by cost-effectiveness
  - Added detailed budget allocation plan ($250 hard cap with zone-based approval gates)

- **Added AGENTS.md** defining interface contracts for all agents:
  - Specified input/output schemas for each agent
  - Clarified which agents use LLMs (Claude Opus/Sonnet) vs. deterministic logic
  - Documented Budget Controller as a non-LLM shared service with approval workflow

- **Added CLAUDE.md** for AI assistant context:
  - Co-development coordination rules between Cloud (Claude Code) and Local (Google Antigravity) environments
  - Project structure and file organization
  - Key constraints and tech stack reference

- **Added SCRAPING_ALTERNATIVES.md** documenting free/cheap alternatives to Bright Data for post-hackathon sustainability

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Budget Controller** is the critical innovation: a deterministic (non-LLM) service that gates every Bright Data API call with real-time spend tracking and zone-based approval thresholds (Green/Yellow/Red/Hard Stop)
- **Sequential investigation** enforces finishing one project thoroughly before moving to the next, preventing budget waste on low-confidence targets
- **Tiered evidence sources** (Tier 1: $0.50-2.00, Tier 2: $2.00-5.00, Tier 3: $5.00-15.00) enable cost-effective prioritization—hit cheap sources first, only escalate if needed
- **Batch processing in Red Flag Analyst** with category-level baselines allows the model to spot statistical outliers without holding entire datasets in context
- **Gemini 1.5 Flash** reserved for cheap HTML/PDF extraction, preserving Claude budget for high-leverage reasoning steps

## Rationale

The original approach risked burning budget on low-confidence targets. This redesign ensures every dollar spent on scraping is justified by prior AI analysis, making the system both more effective (better targets) and more responsible (transparent budget tracking). The agent-based design also makes the pipeline testable, auditable, and extensible for post-hackathon use.

body:
Closes #198

## What was wrong

The Manage Profiles dialog's "Integration Accounts" section was wired to **global account** operations instead of the **profile↔account association** (`UnifiedProfile.defaultAccounts`):

- **Remove** deleted the account for *all* profiles instead of detaching it.
- **Add** was a dead end — no way to actually attach an account.
- The list showed *all* global accounts, never the ones attached to the profile.

…plus the follow-on flow problems found while fixing it (no way back from the auth dialog, connected account not attached, stale red status dot, × instead of ←).

## What changed

- **List**: shows only accounts attached to the profile (resolved from `defaultAccounts`, dangling ids filtered).
- **Add → picker**: attach an existing global account (one per provider; re-picking replaces), or **connect a new one**.
- **Detach** (X on the list) removes from the profile only; global **Delete account** moved to the account's Edit screen.
- **Connect-and-return**: the integration dialog stacks over the profile manager (kept mounted, demoted); closing it reveals the picker, and the account you just connected is **auto-attached**.
- **Accurate status dots**: integration dialogs now write verified connection status to the shared store, so dots are correct immediately; the profile manager no longer re-checks on reveal and clobbers it.
- **Back vs. close**: `lv-modal` gains a `backButton` mode — opened from Manage Profiles, the dialog shows a **← Back** that returns to the profile instead of a **× Close**.

No backend/Rust changes.

## Tests

- Unit: profile manager (attach/detach/replace, persistence, auto-attach, dangling ids, status not overridden on reveal), `lv-modal` back-button, GitHub dialog writes status to the **shared store** (the cross-component contract that was missing).
- E2E (`profiles-integrations.spec.ts`): attach → save persists `defaultAccounts`; **detach never calls `delete_global_account`**; connect → Back → auto-attach; Back shown (not Close) when opened from Manage Profiles.
- Full suite green: 3050 unit, 55 e2e, lint, typecheck. (`cargo fmt --check` passes; clippy unaffected — no Rust changed.)

## Test plan

1. Manage Profiles → edit a profile → **Add**.
2. Pick an existing account → it attaches; **Save Profile** persists it.
3. Or **Connect a new account → GitHub** → authorize → **← Back** → you're back on the profile with the account **attached** and a **green** dot.
4. Remove (X) an attached account → it detaches but still exists for other profiles.

author: sebastianthiebaud
body:
## Summary

The openraft peer transport (`crates/tsoracle-standalone/src/drivers/openraft/network.rs`) ignored the `RPCOption` passed to each unary `RaftNetworkV2` method (the param was bound as `_option`). openraft enforces that deadline itself for `vote` and `transfer_leader` — it wraps them in `C::timeout` inside `raft_core::broadcast_*` — but the replication **`append_entries`** path does **not**: `stream_append_sequential` simply awaits `network.append_entries(req, option)` and relies on the *transport* to honor `option.hard_ttl()` (the option's TTL is `heartbeat_interval`).

With the option dropped, an `append_entries` on a silently black-holed connection (no RST — a NAT/firewall drop) had no deadline and would wedge that follower's replication stream until TCP keepalive eventually tripped (~2h by default).

This routes all three unary RPCs (`append_entries`, `vote`, `transfer_leader`) through a shared `unary_call` helper that applies `option.hard_ttl()` as a wall-clock deadline:

- On a transport error: evict the pooled client, return `Network` (retry at once).
- On **deadline elapse**: evict the pooled client, return `Unreachable` (openraft backs off before retrying) — the right posture for a connection we just abandoned.

For `vote`/`transfer_leader` this is harmless belt-and-suspenders that fires no earlier than openraft's own `C::timeout`; for `append_entries` it closes the real gap. The snapshot path is unchanged (it already has cancellation + a 60s server-side stream timeout).

The helper is generic over the pool value and response types so it is unit-testable without a live `RaftPeerServiceClient`, mirroring the existing `evict` helper.

### Context

This came out of investigating a security finding that claimed graceful leadership handoff could hang shutdown indefinitely via an unbounded `transfer_leader` RPC. That specific claim is a **false positive** — `Trigger::transfer_leader` only enqueues an `ExternalCommand` and returns, and the actual peer RPC is `C::timeout`-wrapped + spawned by RaftCore. But tracing all three call sites surfaced that `append_entries` is the one path openraft does *not* bound itself, so the transport must.

No public API change (internal `_option` → `option` rename in trait-impl methods).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p tsoracle-standalone --features openraft` — 24 lib + 9 in-process tests pass, including 3 new `unary_call` tests (deadline-elapse → `Unreachable` + evict; transport-error → `Network` + evict; success → body returned + client retained).
- [x] `cargo clippy -p tsoracle-standalone --features openraft --all-targets` — clean.
- [x] `cargo check --workspace --all-features` — clean across all crates and examples.
- [x] Pre-commit hook (`cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy`) passed.

author: damir-topic
body:
## Summary

Implements **G11.2-T2 (#816)**: a user-initiated agent run's audit rows now record **both** the human initiator (`operator_sub`) and the acting agent (`actor_sub`) — the RFC 8693 `sub`+`act` shape — so audit never collapses to a single principal.

Keycloak has **no delegation token exchange** (the GA standard exchange is impersonation-only; delegation/`actor_token` is unimplemented — [keycloak#38279](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/38279)), so MEHO **synthesises the binding at the resource server** instead of relying on an IdP-minted `act` claim:

- `actor_delegation(actor_sub)` ([auth/delegation.py](backend/src/meho_backplane/auth/delegation.py)) binds the acting agent's principal (`AgentDefinition.identity_ref`) into structlog's contextvars; `resolve_actor_sub()` reads it at **all three** audit write paths (chassis `audit.py`, dispatcher `operations/_audit.py`, MCP `mcp/audit.py`).
- `AgentInvocationService.run` binds it **around `asyncio.create_task`**, so the background loop task snapshots the actor for its whole life — every audit row its in-process tool calls produce carries `operator_sub`=human + `actor_sub`=agent. No second token over the wire; `Operator` deliberately does **not** carry the actor (it's run context, not a token claim).
- **Autonomous** (SCHEDULED-trigger) runs authenticate the agent as itself via the Keycloak-supported `client_credentials` grant (`get_client_credentials_token`, [auth/agent_token.py](backend/src/meho_backplane/auth/agent_token.py)) — agent is the subject (`operator_sub`=agent), `actor_sub` stays NULL. `run_scheduled` is the seam the **G11.3** scheduler drives.

Supersedes the unimplementable RFC 8693 token-exchange of **PR #1051**.

## Test plan
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` — clean
- [x] `mypy src/` — `Success: no issues found in 303 source files`
- [x] `grep -r "actor_token" backend/src` → **nothing** (no delegation token-exchange code path)
- [x] `pytest` (74 passed across new + adjacent suites):
  - `test_auth_delegation.py` — bind/read/restore, fail-closed on empty, await-safety, **task-snapshot inheritance** (the `create_task` binding shape)
  - `test_auth_agent_token.py` — `client_credentials` request contract + every error mode (`network_error` / `http_401` / `missing_access_token`) + **client secret never logged**
  - `test_audit_actor_sub.py` — delegated run records human+agent; direct human + autonomous runs record `actor_sub`=NULL
  - `test_migration_0021_actor_sub.py` — upgrade adds nullable col + index; **downgrade/upgrade round-trip**; `agent_session_id` untouched; ORM defaults None
  - `test_agent_invocation.py`, `test_audit_middleware.py`, `test_mcp_audit.py`, `test_db_models.py` — green (no regression)
- [x] `code-quality.py --diff` — 0 blockers
- [x] Migration `0021` applies cleanly on top of `0020` (single head)

## Design notes / deviations
- **Autonomous trigger is G11.3.** This PR ships the `client_credentials` auth primitive + audit shape + `run_scheduled` seam; the cron scheduler that fires SCHEDULED runs is G11.3's scope.
- **`Operator` does not carry `actor_sub`** (unlike PR #1051's act-claim design): there is no inbound `act` claim to extract — the actor is the run's delegation context, recorded on the audit row + contextvar.
- **Real-Keycloak integration test:** the `client_credentials` grant is fully exercised via a respx contract test (CI-runnable). A live-Keycloak integration test needs Keycloak test infra that doesn't exist in the suite yet (no Keycloak testcontainer) — noted as follow-up, not gating this PR.

## Out of scope
- Permission model + verdict (T3 #820), approval queue (T4 #817).
- The SCHEDULED-run scheduler (G11.3) and over-the-wire external-agent delegation (G11.6).

Closes #816

author: elockenvitz
body:
The previous commit on this branch cached pilot_progress and hasCommittedTradeInOrg via React Query's `initialData` + `initialDataUpdatedAt: 0`, but the user still saw the same cold-load hitch: System Loop highlighting Decide before snapping to Review, and Trade Book flashing the locked preview.

Root cause: `initialData` is captured at the first useQuery call and doesn't reliably re-apply when `user.id` transitions from null on the very first render to populated on the second. The repo's existing `cachedHasGraduated` pattern doesn't use initialData for this reason — it falls back to the localStorage cache AT RENDER TIME wherever the derived value is computed.

This commit follows that proven pattern:

- `usePilotProgress` now computes `progress = query.data ?? cachedProgress ?? {}`. Every derived flag (hasUnlockedTradeBook, hasUnlockedOutcomes, hasGraduated) reads from `progress`, so they return the correct value from the first paint regardless of how React Query schedules its first fetch.

- `usePilotMode` renames the raw query data to `hasCommittedTradeInOrgQuery` and computes the effective value as `hasCommittedTradeInOrgQuery ?? cachedHasCommittedTrade ?? false`. Same render-time fallback shape.

- `PilotActionDashboard` no longer let the dashboard's own `cachedStepDone` shadow the now-reliable hook-cached values for decide/review. The cache is still used for capture/develop/analyze (whose inputs aren't cached yet), but decide and review always come from `liveStepDone`.

Persisted writes to localStorage are unchanged — they still fire only when the real query resolves, so a stale cache from the fallback doesn't get re-written as if it were the truth.

## Problem

The build fails at `cargo build --release` because `time-core` v0.1.8 (a transitive dependency via `mongodb` → `bson` → `time`) uses Rust edition 2024 in its `Cargo.toml`. Edition 2024 was not stabilized until Rust 1.85, so Cargo 1.82 cannot parse the manifest and errors out before compilation begins.

## Solution

Updated the builder stage in the Dockerfile from `rust:1.82-slim` to `rust:1.85-slim`. Rust 1.85 stabilizes edition 2024 support, allowing Cargo to parse the `time-core` v0.1.8 manifest correctly. No dependencies or Cargo.lock changes are required.

### Changes
- **Modified** `Dockerfile`

### Context
- **Deployment**: [#be92f8](https://railway.com/project/ea76cfea-4108-42b0-a6cd-47a0c5035d18/environment/0fb9bcd9-a537-4098-ba41-1814a24d4bb4/deployment/be92f8b4-fa63-4d09-9d44-2aa68cb1ce62)
- **Failed commit**: `bd6f31c`

author: trungdangtapcode
body:
## Summary

This branch is a large gameplay and presentation pass for the DirectX 11 JRPG prototype. It adds story progression, save-slot structure, campfire systems, localization, audio settings, battle result flow, MP/status-effect combat, expanded enemy behavior, and multiple UI/visual architecture improvements.

The latest fixes in the branch restore the Expedition-style tilted battle skill UI without losing the richer skill/status information, anchor the skill list to the active character, and hide large info panels during target selection so enemies stay readable.

## Major Feature Areas

### Save, Campfire, And Progression
- Added campfire checkpoint save/load behavior.
- Added numbered save-slot flow and new-game slot selection.
- Gated equipment and lineup changes so they only work at campfires.
- Added campfire hub/shopping-oriented structure for future upgrades and item purchases.
- Added visible coin wallet/HUD support so the player can see earned currency.

### Localization And Settings
- Added JSON-based localization with English, Vietnamese, and French.
- Added global settings persistence in `save/settings.json`.
- Added Vietnamese-capable font support.
- Kept CLI/debug output English-only so console encoding does not corrupt localized gameplay text.
- Added main-menu options for language and audio.

### Audio
- Expanded SFX coverage from available source asset folders.
- Added data-driven BGM routing for menu, battle encounters, zombie battles, victory, and defeat.
- Added BGM/SFX/Voice volume settings with persistence.
- Added non-looping result soundtrack policy through data instead of hardcoded behavior.

### Overworld And Story
- Expanded and rebuilt overworld flow with route/story motivation.
- Added Paris-style intro/story/dialogue foundation.
- Added NPC/dialogue system pieces for Maelle/story interactions.
- Added region/theming and visual render-pipeline improvements for the overworld.
- Added pause menu overlay with return-to-title and quit confirmation.

### Battle Result Flow
- Added victory result screen with rewards, stats, party progression, and cinematic overlay behavior.
- Added defeat splash and retry/leave prompt.
- Added reward timing so victory rewards are applied once.
- Added result soundtrack routing and result visual effect support.
- Fixed flee behavior so it no longer flashes victory UI.

### Mana, Skills, And Status Effects
- Added MP/resource support and data-driven skills.
- Added status-effect framework extensions, icons, and HUD visibility.
- Added player/enemy status icon display paths.
- Added richer skill metadata for cost, target, damage grade, hit count, and applied effects.
- Added consume-MP and status-damage action support through the battle action queue.

### Battle UI And Camera Presentation
- Restored the tilted Expedition-style skill UI using the old 9-slice asset chrome.
- Replaced hardcoded per-component rotation with one shared parent transform.
- Made the skill UI follow live battle camera rotation via data-driven layout.
- Anchored the skill list to the active character's camera-focus point.
- Hid large skill detail/target preview panels during target selection so the target remains visible.
- Kept status/detail features available in skill selection instead of downgrading to a plain list.

### Enemies And Bullet-Hell
- Added zombie armour enemy asset processing and integration.
- Added zombie armour battle BGM and encounter placement.
- Added zombie-specific bullet-hell attack patterns.
- Added multiple/randomized enemy attack patterns to reduce repetition.
- Fixed zombie animation direction/turn-view/scale issues across several passes.
- Ended battle immediately when the player dies in bullet hell.

### Build And Tooling
- Restored incremental build acceleration and cached object reuse.
- Added/updated asset-processing scripts and docs for generated/processed assets.
- Kept manual MSVC build flow intact.

## Latest UI Fix Included In This PR

The most recent commit fixes the target-selection problem shown in review screenshots:
- `BattleSkillMenuRenderer` now supports active-character anchoring through `data/battle_skill_menu_layout.json`.
- `BattleState` passes the acting character's camera-focus screen anchor to the skill menu renderer.
- The renderer maps that anchor through the inverse parent transform before shifting the whole layout, so tilt/zoom stay coherent.
- `hideDetailPanelsDuringTargetSelect` hides big right-side panels while selecting a target.
- Skill cards, icons, text, accents, and 9-slice panels still render as one transformed unit.

## Data And Docs Added Or Updated

Important areas touched include:
- `data/localization/*.json`
- `data/battle_skill_menu_layout.json`
- `data/battle_result_layout.json`
- `data/audio/*.json`
- `data/skills/*.json`
- `data/status_effects/*.json`
- `data/enemies/*.json`
- `assets/animations/*.json`
- `docs/` feature chapters for localization, battle results, pause menu, skill/status UI, assets, overworld, audio, and save systems.

## Verification

Build verification completed before opening the PR:

```text
.\build_src_static.bat 2>&1
[OK] Build succeeded > bin\game.exe  [Debug]
```

A second build verified incremental cache reuse:

```text
[compile] No C++ source changes detected; reusing cached .obj files.
[OK] Build succeeded > bin\game.exe  [Debug]
```

## Review Notes

This PR is large and should be reviewed by subsystem rather than linearly:
1. Battle simulation/action queue changes.
2. Battle UI/result/status rendering.
3. Save/settings/localization persistence.
4. Audio routing/data files.
5. Overworld/story/dialogue/pause flow.
6. Asset scripts and generated/processed metadata.

Known local-only dirty files were not included in the PR:
- `.gitignore`
- `.vscode/settings.json`
- `bin/log_output.txt`
- `src/UI/PauseMenuRenderer.h`
- `patches/process_item_icons.py`

## Risk Areas

- The PR is broad, so regressions are most likely at state transitions: menu -> overworld, overworld -> battle, flee, defeat retry, return to title, and save/load restore.
- Localization touches many UI paths; missing keys should fall back, but long Vietnamese/French text still needs visual smoke testing.
- Battle UI positioning is data-driven, so small layout adjustments may still be needed after live playtesting different encounters.
- Header changes can force a full rebuild once, but the incremental cache path remains intact after that.

author: dcetlin
body:
## What broke and why

PR #1305 introduced `from orchestration.prescription_metrics import PrescriptionMetricsLogger` in `steward.py` along with two call sites (`log_prescription_generated` and `log_uow_closed`), but never created `src/orchestration/prescription_metrics.py`. Every invocation of executor-heartbeat and steward-heartbeat was crashing at import time with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'orchestration.prescription_metrics'`.

## What this fixes

Adds `src/orchestration/prescription_metrics.py` with a `PrescriptionMetricsLogger` class that satisfies the full call interface both call sites use:

- `log_prescription_generated(uow_id, cycle, executor_type, has_minimum_viable_output, has_boundary, ...)` — logs at DEBUG, accepts all kwargs for forward compat
- `log_uow_closed(uow_id, total_cycles, closure_outcome, ...)` — same

Both methods are non-fatal stubs: they emit to the `prescription_metrics` logger at DEBUG level and return None. No DB writes. The class docstring explicitly notes that the wos-metrics.db backing store is deferred; this stub makes the contract visible and the call sites functional without introducing untested persistence.

## Functional patterns used

Pure no-op methods with explicit typed signatures and `**kwargs` forward-compat slots. Side effects are isolated to log output only. All kwargs are accepted and ignored (not silently dropped without documentation) to allow call-site evolution without breaking this stub's signature.

## Tests run

- [x] `uv run python3 -c "from orchestration.steward import is_bootup_candidate_gate_active; print('OK')"` with repo + src on sys.path — returns `OK: False` (clean import, no crash)
- [x] Same verification run in the worktree after copying the file — confirms module resolution in the exact path setup steward-heartbeat uses at runtime

No unit tests added: the stub has no logic to test. The import verification above is the definitive check.

## Manual test

N/A — this change is a module creation that unblocks an import. The user-visible outcome is that executor-heartbeat and steward-heartbeat no longer crash on startup. Verified by the import smoke test above; no Telegram output involved.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Unit tests pass with proper mocking (no production hits in automated tests) — no automated tests exist for this stub; import smoke test is the appropriate check
- [x] Integration/manual test run — import smoke test passed in worktree environment
- [x] User-visible outcome: executor-heartbeat and steward-heartbeat will no longer crash on ModuleNotFoundError
- [x] Side-effect audit: stub is read-only (no DB writes, no file I/O, no external calls)
- [x] External service calls: none

Closes no issue directly — this is an emergency unblock for the crash introduced by #1305.

author: okapi-ca
body:
Continues the P3 family-by-family expansion (DfI → **Purview** → Teams advanced → Copilot admin, one PR each). Builds on PR #116 (P3-DfI).

Expands Microsoft Purview administration coverage from 15 tools to **40 tools** — adds 25 new tools across 4 sub-themes covering advanced eDiscovery v3 case management, Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), and event-based retention triggers.

## Summary

- **25 new tools** for `/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/*`, `/security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/*`, `/security/triggers/*`, `/security/triggerTypes/*`
- **9 commits** organized by sub-theme (7 features + 1 fix + 1 docs/version)
- **2 new Graph permissions** required (must be admin-consented before tools work end-to-end)
- All 25 tools target Graph v1.0 (stable)
- Function path notation with `()` and namespace-prefixed actions (`microsoft.graph.security.applyHold`, `addToReviewSet`, `export`, etc.) pass through to Graph as-is
- `npm run verify` passes: 195/195 tests, lint clean, prettier clean, build OK
- Version: `0.10.0` → `0.11.0` (minor, additive)

## Motivation

Purview was 15 tools — basic eDiscovery cases CRUD + custodians + searches + 2 list-only retention events tools. Missing:

- Drill into a specific custodian and release / re-index it
- Add noncustodial data sources (shared mailboxes, departmental sites, group OneDrive)
- Track long-running operations (search executions, exports, holds)
- Manage review sets (create, get, export)
- Author review-set queries and bulk-tag matching items
- Trigger DSPM policy compute (Microsoft-native DSPM is the Varonis / Defender for Cloud DSPM equivalent)
- Get specific retention events / event types
- Create event-based retention triggers

This PR closes those gaps and brings the eDiscovery v3 workflow to feature parity with the Purview portal: case → custodians + noncustodial sources → search → reviewSet → query → tags → export.

## Commits (atomic by sub-theme)

| Commit | Sub-theme | Tools | Highest risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `8fc2c1a` | eDiscovery custodian advanced | 3 | medium (release) |
| `ab5c924` | eDiscovery noncustodial data sources | 5 | **high** (remove-hold) |
| `37eff6e` | eDiscovery case operations | 2 | (read-only) |
| `1845e2e` | eDiscovery review sets | 4 | **high** (export-review-set) |
| `25bce7d` | eDiscovery review set queries + addToReviewSet | 5 | medium |
| `f19149b` | fix: correct add-to-review-set path | — | — |
| `e26294d` | DSPM compute + root | 2 | low |
| `8f5fdf4` | Retention events expansion | 4 | medium |
| `2c84d27` | docs + bump 0.11.0 | — | — |

`f19149b` was caught by `npm run generate` validation — the previous commit had the `addToReviewSet` action on the search parent path, but it's actually on the review set parent (the search is passed in the body). Fix kept as a separate commit per the repo convention (never amend committed work).

## Highest-impact tools

**`remove-hold-ediscovery-noncustodial-data-source`** (high) — once hold is removed, deleted items become eligible for permanent purge per the retention window (14-30 days mailbox dumpster, 93 days SharePoint Recycle Bin). Confirm with legal counsel before releasing.

**`export-review-set`** (high) — exports native files / extracted text / PDFs / metadata CSVs / review tags. Output may contain privileged or PII content; handle per the case's chain-of-custody. Long-running async; output downloaded via the Purview portal.

## New Graph permissions required

Must be admin-consented on the app registration **before any of the new write tools work end-to-end**:

- `ProtectionScopes.Compute.All` — for `compute-protection-scopes`
- `RecordsManagement.ReadWrite.All` — for `create-retention-event` and `create-retention-event-type`

Already-declared permissions covering most of the new tools:

- `eDiscovery.Read.All` — 18 of the new eDiscovery reads
- `eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All` — 7 of the new eDiscovery writes
- `InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All` — `get-data-security-governance-root`
- `RecordsManagement.Read.All` — `get-retention-event` + `get-retention-event-type`

Without consent of the 2 new permissions, `compute-protection-scopes` and the 2 retention-event creates return `403 Insufficient privileges`. The other 22 new tools work with the already-declared permissions.

## Tools added (25)

### eDiscovery custodian admin (3)

- `get-ediscovery-custodian` (GET)
- `release-ediscovery-custodian` (POST .../release, medium)
- `update-ediscovery-custodian-index` (POST .../updateIndex, low)

### eDiscovery noncustodial data sources (5)

- `list-ediscovery-noncustodial-data-sources` (GET)
- `create-ediscovery-noncustodial-data-source` (POST, medium)
- `get-ediscovery-noncustodial-data-source` (GET)
- `apply-hold-ediscovery-noncustodial-data-source` (POST .../applyHold, medium)
- `remove-hold-ediscovery-noncustodial-data-source` (POST .../removeHold, **high**)

### eDiscovery case operations tracking (2)

- `list-case-operations` (GET)
- `get-case-operation` (GET)

### eDiscovery review sets (4)

- `list-review-sets` (GET)
- `create-review-set` (POST, low)
- `get-review-set` (GET)
- `export-review-set` (POST .../export, **high**)

### eDiscovery review set queries + addToReviewSet (5)

- `add-to-review-set` (POST .../addToReviewSet, medium)
- `list-review-set-queries` (GET)
- `create-review-set-query` (POST, low)
- `get-review-set-query` (GET)
- `apply-tags-review-set-query` (POST .../applyTags, medium)

### DSPM (2)

- `get-data-security-governance-root` (GET)
- `compute-protection-scopes` (POST .../compute, low)

### Retention events expansion (4)

- `get-retention-event` (GET)
- `create-retention-event` (POST, medium)
- `get-retention-event-type` (GET)
- `create-retention-event-type` (POST, medium)

## Out of scope (deferred)

Intentionally not included in this PR to keep the diff reviewable:

- Sub-resources of custodians: `siteSources` / `userSources` / `unifiedGroupSources` CRUD per custodian (~12-15 additional tools — usually managed implicitly via the dataSource @odata.type on `create-ediscovery-noncustodial-data-source` or via the Purview portal)
- `export-review-set-query` (POST on a specific query's `/export` — most users export the full review set instead)
- DSPM `processContentAsync` (DLP content scanning) — complex async API with file upload semantics, separate PR
- DSPM `sensitivityLabels` via `/security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/sensitivityLabels` — redundant with the existing 5 sensitivity-label tools under `/security/informationProtection`

## Testing

- `npm run verify` passes (generate + lint + format + build + test): 195/195 tests
- Local sanity: all 25 new tool aliases present in `src/generated/client.ts`
- One path correction caught by validation, fixed in a separate commit (kept history clean — never amend per repo convention)
- No tenant-side validation in this PR — will happen post-merge in the LCI deployment cycle (and gated by consent of the 2 new permissions)

## Backward compatibility

- No breaking changes
- All existing tools unaffected — the 15 pre-existing Purview tools keep their permissions
- 195/195 existing tests pass

## Next P3 PRs (follow-ups in separate PRs)

- Teams advanced (call analytics, meeting recordings, attendance reports, ~10-15 tools)
- Copilot admin (audit, usage analytics, prompt analytics, agent gating, ~5-10 tools)

Each will follow the same pattern: atomic commits by sub-theme, separate Graph permission declarations as needed.

author: 0xanyi
body:
Phase 9 §6 PR 1 of 3 — schema only, mirroring the export-bundle PR cadence (schema → service+routes → UI).

## What this PR ships

- New table `erasure_requests` (migration `0022_funny_kat_farrell.sql`) backing both GDPR-erase scopes: `member` (single PII scrub) and `zone` (decommission + hard-purge after the reversibility window).
- State machine `pending → applied | cancelled | failed` enforced by a CHECK constraint; `applied` and `cancelled` are terminal at the row level.
- Two partial unique indexes prevent racing in-flight requests:
  - `(zone_id, member_id) WHERE status='pending' AND member_id IS NOT NULL` — at most one open member-scope request per (zone, member).
  - `(zone_id) WHERE status='pending' AND scope='zone'` — at most one open zone-scope request per zone (two open zone-erases would race each other's cancel windows).
- CHECK invariants: scope ∈ {member, zone}; status ∈ {pending, applied, cancelled, failed}; member-scope rows *must* carry a `member_id` while zone-scope rows *must not*; reversibility window > 0; `applies_at > created_at` so a freshly-created row can never be DOA.
- `reversibilityWindowDays` is snapshotted per row so a later retention-policy edit cannot retroactively shorten an in-flight window.

## Registry coverage

The export-bundle's zone-scoped-table registry now includes `erasure_requests` at `restoreOrder: 930` (between `report_jobs` and `audit_events`):
- An operator's last bundle should carry the erase history alongside the audit log; a restored zone without it would silently lose the GDPR ledger.
- FK to `members.id` is `set null` so an erased-member request restored into a fresh schema still loads cleanly (the apply pass may already have nulled `member_id` if the member row was hard-deleted post-scrub).

## Verification

- `pnpm check` + `pnpm lint` clean.
- API: 60 files / 713 tests pass (the registry coverage test now sees the new table).
- Drizzle generate emits `0022_funny_kat_farrell.sql`; applied cleanly to the local test-db.

## What's next

- **PR 2/3:** service layer (`services/erasure/{requests,scrub-member,scrub-zone,cron}.ts`) + routes (`tenant-erasure.ts`, `admin-erasure.ts`) + pg-boss schedule.
- **PR 3/3:** UI surfaces on `/zone/members/[id]` (Privacy panel + erasure modal) and `/zone/settings` (Decommission card, gated on a recent completed `zone_exports` row).

author: copilot
body:
`gt_ffmpeg::transcode::hls` was only carrying forward the first stereo audio stream into HLS output. This updates HLS transcoding to keep every existing stereo input stream by downmixing each one to mono and emitting them together in the segment audio.

- **Problem**
  - HLS transcodes dropped all but the first stereo input stream.

- **Transcode behavior**
  - Probe input media before transcoding to enumerate audio streams.
  - Select all audio streams with `channels == 2` and `channel_layout == "stereo"`.
  - Build an FFmpeg audio filter that:
    - downmixes each stereo stream to mono
    - merges the resulting mono streams into one multi-channel output audio stream
  - Keep the existing fallback path when no stereo streams are present.
  - Inputs with multiple stereo streams (for example, 4 stereo streams) now produce the corresponding number of mono output channels instead of collapsing to a single stereo result.

- **FFprobe metadata**
  - Extend `FFProbeStream` parsing to capture `channels` and `channel_layout`.
  - Widen the probe error type to match the async transcode error path.

- **Filter construction**
  - Isolate mono-filter generation into helper logic so the mapping behavior is explicit and testable.

Example of the generated filter shape for four stereo input streams:

```text
[0:1]pan=mono|c0=.5*c0+.5*c1[a0];
[0:2]pan=mono|c0=.5*c0+.5*c1[a1];
[0:3]pan=mono|c0=.5*c0+.5*c1[a2];
[0:4]pan=mono|c0=.5*c0+.5*c1[a3];
[a0][a1][a2][a3]amerge=inputs=4[aout]
```

### **User description** macOS (MacOsGpuMetricsProvider): stdout was read before WaitForExitAsync, so if system_profiler was still writing when ReadToEndAsync returned, the output could be truncated. Fixed by starting the read task first (draining the buffer concurrently), awaiting process exit, then awaiting the read task — the MSDN-recommended pattern that prevents both partial reads and buffer-fill deadlocks. Windows (TryGetWindowsGpuInfoAsync): had the reverse ordering — WaitForExitAsync before ReadToEndAsync — which deadlocks if wmic writes enough output to fill the stdout pipe buffer. Applied the same concurrent read pattern. ___ ### **PR Type** Bug fix ___ ### **Description** - Concurrently read stdout to avoid partial data - Await process exit before collecting output - Prevent stdout buffer deadlocks ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR Start["Start Process"] --> ReadTask["Start ReadToEndAsync"] ReadTask --> Wait["WaitForExitAsync"] Wait --> Collect["Await Read Task"] Collect --> End["Process Output"] ```

1. Access Control & Visibility Modes
1.1 Public Access
 Action: Create a folder and set visibility to Public.
 Verification: Log in or switch to Admin, Officer, and Member views. Verify the folder is visible in all views.
1.2 Specific Roles (Role Restrictions)
 Action: Create a folder, set visibility to Specific Roles, and check ONLY the Officer role.
 Verification:
Switch to the Officer view -> The folder should be visible.
Switch to the Member view -> The folder should be completely hidden.
 Action: Edit access to check BOTH Officer and Member.
 Verification: Switch to the Member view -> The folder should now be visible.
1.3 Specific Members (User Restrictions)
 Action: Create a document, set visibility to Specific Members, and select exactly one user (e.g., your test Member account).
 Verification:
Log in as the selected Member -> The document should be visible.
Log in as a different Member -> The document should be hidden.
1.4 Password Protection
 Action: Create a folder and set visibility to Password Protected with a test password (e.g., test123).
 Verification:
Switch to the Member view. You should see a "Locked" badge on the folder.
Click the folder. A modal should prompt for the password.
Enter an incorrect password -> It should reject it.
Enter the correct password -> The folder should unlock and allow entry.

2. Inheritance & Nested Routing
2.1 Nested Visibility Inheritance
 Action: Inside a Public folder, create a subfolder and restrict it to Officers only.
 Verification: Switch to the Member view. The parent Public folder is visible, but upon entering it, the nested restricted subfolder is hidden.
2.2 Deep Security Enforcement
 Action: Create a root folder restricted to Officers, and inside it, upload a Public document.
 Verification: Switch to the Member view. The root folder is hidden. Using a direct URL hack (if known) to the sub-document should fail or return an empty state because the parent path blocks access.
 
3. CRUD Operations
3.1 Folder/File Renaming
 Action: Click the 3-dot menu on a file and select Rename. Give it a new name.
 Verification: The name updates immediately in the UI. Reload the page to ensure the change persists in the database.
3.2 Moving Items

 Verification: Document X disappears from the root view and appears inside Folder A.
3.3 Deleting Items
 Action: Delete a folder that contains files and subfolders.
 Verification: A warning appears. After confirming, the folder is removed. Check the database to ensure all nested files/folders inside it were cascade-deleted.
3.4 Copying Items

 Verification: A duplicate appears with (Copy - 1) appended to the name. The copied file should retain the original visibility settings.
 
4. Edge Cases & Validations
4.1 Unique Name Enforcement

4.2 File Size Limits

4.3 Multi-Role Edit Toggling

author: rservant
body:
Part of epic #709 (Sprint 4). Addresses #720.

## What

Makes the local husky hooks **path-aware**, mirroring the CI/Deploy `paths-ignore` globs from #704 (`**/*.md`, `tasks/**`, `docs/**`, `.gitignore`, `LICENSE`). Since #704, CI already skips docs/lessons-only PRs — so a docs-only change was doing *more* work locally than in CI. The sprint runner writes a lesson file most sprints, so docs-touching commits/pushes are frequent.

- **pre-commit:** when every staged file is non-code, skip `typecheck` + `lint`. `lint-staged` still runs (markdown gets prettier'd); `lint:yaml` still runs if a `docs/` (or `.github/`) YAML file changed.
- **pre-push:** reads the push range from stdin; when every changed file in the range is non-code, skip `test:unit`.

## Design

Single tested source of truth — no parallel bash glob reimplementation to drift:

- `scripts/lib/changedFilesGate.ts` — pure classifier (`isNonCodeFile` / `isDocsOnly` / `needsYamlLint`), unit-tested (10 cases).
- `scripts/changed-files-gate.ts` — thin CLI bridge (reads paths on stdin, answers via exit code), matching the `relevant-lessons.sh` → `relevantLessons.ts` precedent.
- Hooks are **POSIX sh** (husky invokes them with `sh -e`, so no bashisms / `pipefail`).

## Hard constraints honored

- **ALL-not-ANY:** skip only when *every* changed/staged file is non-code. A mixed code+docs change runs the full gate.
- **Not a `--no-verify` bypass:** the hook is correctly determining there is nothing code-relevant to verify; CI remains the gate of record. Documented in a comment in each hook.
- **Ambiguous push ranges** (new branch / no remote ref / deletion / empty stdin) default to **running** the gate, never skipping.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Docs/lessons-only commit skips typecheck/lint (still formats md); docs/lessons-only push skips `test:unit`.
- [x] A commit/push touching any code runs the full gate (mixed included).
- [x] Ambiguous push range (new branch, no upstream) defaults to running the gate.
- [x] No `--no-verify` involved in the design; behavior documented in a comment in each hook.

## Evidence

Behavioral tests run against `sh -e` (mimicking husky) with a stubbed `npm` to observe the gate decision:

| Hook | Scenario | Result |
|---|---|---|
| pre-push | docs-only range (`tasks/**` only) | **skips** test:unit ✓ |
| pre-push | code range (`scripts/**`) | runs gate ✓ |
| pre-push | new branch (remote sha all-zeros) | runs gate ✓ |
| pre-push | empty stdin | runs gate ✓ |
| pre-push | deletion (local sha all-zeros) | runs gate ✓ |
| pre-commit | docs-only staged | skips typecheck+lint, no yaml ✓ |
| pre-commit | `docs/*.yml` staged | skips typecheck+lint, **runs** lint:yaml ✓ |
| pre-commit | code staged | runs typecheck+lint+yaml ✓ |

Suites: `test:scripts` 96/96, frontend `test:unit` 2017/2017. The pre-push gate itself ran on this very push (dogfood).

body:
## Summary
This PR implements category-aware filtering across library updates, download management, and related UI screens. When the app is locked (hidden categories are inaccessible), novels in hidden categories are now filtered from updates, downloads, and related notifications.

## Key Changes

- **DAO Query Updates**: Modified `LibraryUpdateDao`, `UpdateIssueDao`, `ChapterDao`, and `NovelDao` to accept an `excludeHidden` parameter and filter results based on category visibility using LEFT JOIN semantics (novels with `categoryId = NULL` are always visible)

- **ViewModel Integration**: Updated `MoreViewModel`, `LibraryUpdatesViewModel`, `UpdateIssuesViewModel`, `TasksViewModel`, and `DownloadsViewModel` to derive the `excludeHidden` flag from `HiddenCategoriesAuthManager.isUnlocked` and pass it through to DAO queries via `flatMapLatest`

- **Notification Filtering**: 
  - `LibraryUpdateWorker.maybeNotifyNovel()` now checks if a novel is in a hidden category before surfacing notifications when the app is locked
  - `DownloadManager` redacts chapter names in progress callbacks for hidden-category novels when the app is locked

- **Progress Display**: 
  - `LibraryUpdater` redacts novel titles in progress callbacks for hidden-category novels
  - `DownloadService` handles blank chapter names gracefully in notification text

## Implementation Details

- Hidden categories are snapshotted once per library update run to allow mid-sync unlock/lock toggles to take effect on subsequent progress emissions
- The `LEFT JOIN` pattern ensures novels in the default category (where `categoryId = NULL`) remain visible regardless of the `excludeHidden` flag, matching LibraryScreen filter semantics
- All flows properly use `distinctUntilChanged()` to avoid redundant database queries when the lock state hasn't changed

author: copilot
body:
This refactor tightens pq’s foundation so the core library is shaped around domain operations instead of the CLI surface. It replaces stringly, presentation-first internals with typed models, explicit parquet semantics, and narrower module responsibilities.

- **Core API**
  - Added `/home/runner/work/pq/pq/src/api.rs` as the library-facing entrypoint for schema, scan, count, stats, info, convert, and merge operations.
  - Kept command modules thin by delegating orchestration to the core API and presentation to output adapters.

- **Typed domain model**
  - Reworked `/home/runner/work/pq/pq/src/model.rs` to represent:
    - `ColumnType` with separate physical and logical type information
    - `CompressionCodec` instead of raw compression strings
    - `StatValue` instead of stringified min/max values
    - `FileInfo.path` as a real path, not a rendered string
  - Moved display formatting to the edge so the core remains reusable.

- **Parquet semantics**
  - Schema and stats now preserve logical-vs-physical type distinctions instead of flattening everything to physical parquet type names.
  - JSON output exposes both the display type and explicit physical/logical metadata.
  - Stats JSON preserves native numeric/boolean values instead of coercing everything to strings.

- **Dataset resolution**
  - Tightened `/home/runner/work/pq/pq/src/dataset/source.rs`:
    - no silent dropping of glob errors
    - explicit handling for empty input / no matches / too many matches
    - deterministic ordering
    - deduplication of overlapping explicit and glob inputs without collapsing intentional duplicate explicit inputs

- **Read path and scalability**
  - Reworked tail reads in `/home/runner/work/pq/pq/src/engine/parquet.rs` to select only the row groups needed for the requested tail window instead of materializing the full file first.

- **Output layer**
  - Refactored output modules to be writer-first and added shared CSV escaping utilities.
  - Kept stdout printing as a thin adapter over writer-based formatting.
  - Centralized typed-to-presentation conversion in `/home/runner/work/pq/pq/src/output.rs`.

- **Error handling**
  - Replaced message-substring filtering in `/home/runner/work/pq/pq/src/main.rs` with typed cause suppression via `PqError::should_hide_cause`.
  - Added explicit error variants for missing input and oversized glob expansions.

- **Tests and docs**
  - Updated tests to assert typed behavior and richer JSON output.
  - Added coverage for dataset deduplication and the new library-facing API.
  - Updated README to reflect the richer schema/stats JSON shape.

Example of the new core shape:

```rust
let dataset = pq::dataset_from_inputs(vec![path])?;
let schema = pq::schema(&dataset)?;

assert_eq!(schema[0].columns[0].column_type.physical, pq::PhysicalType::Int64);
```

author: cravenceiling
body:
Closes #234.

## Problem
Reasoning effort was effectively hardcoded across all models. The agent config (`config.json`) already carried an `effort` field, exposed in the schema and TS types — but **nothing read it**. So:
- **Codex** always ran at the hardcoded `DEFAULT_CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT` (`"medium"`).
- **Claude** got no `--effort` flag at all.
- Only the onboarding tutorial forced an effort, via an explicit request override.

Net: every normal chat/mission ran at a fixed effort regardless of the model or the agent's setting.

## Fix
Effort is now resolved engine-side in the same place provider/model resolve, and is **model-gated + provider-specific** (verified against the live CLIs + official docs, not the stale code comments):

- `sessions::resolve_effort(agent_dir, provider)` reads `config.effort`, validates it against the **final** provider's accepted set, and falls back to the provider default (`medium`). An explicit request `effort` (onboarding) still wins.
- Accepted levels + default live on `ProviderAdapter` (`effort_levels` / `default_effort`) as a provider-level superset; per-model availability lives in the frontend catalog (`providers.ts`).
- The model picker (`ChatModelSelector`) now shows an effort row with only the levels the active model accepts and persists the choice to the agent config. Chat, board missions, routines and onboarding all honor it.

### Effort matrix
| Provider | Model | Levels offered | Flag |
|---|---|---|---|
| anthropic | opus (4.7) | low/medium/high/xhigh/max | `--effort <v>` |
| anthropic | sonnet (4.6) | low/medium/high/max (no xhigh) | `--effort <v>` |
| openai | gpt-5.5 | low/medium/high/xhigh (no max) | `-c model_reasoning_effort="<v>"` |
| gemini | any | none | (no flag) |

Claude self-clamps an unsupported value; codex has no fallback, so `max` (an unknown variant to codex) is never offered for OpenAI. Default is `medium` everywhere. The stale "bundled codex rejects xhigh" comments were corrected — codex 0.130+ accepts xhigh.

## Key files
- Engine: `provider/{mod,anthropic,openai}.rs` (adapter effort methods), `sessions/provider.rs` (`resolve_effort` + tests), `sessions/mod.rs`, `routes/sessions.rs`, `routines/engine_dispatcher.rs`, `codex_runner.rs` (drop hardcoded const), `codex_command.rs`
- Frontend: `lib/providers.ts` (+ tests), `chat-model-selector{,-parts}.tsx`, `tabs/chat-tab.tsx`, `use-agent-chat-panel.tsx`, `data/config.ts`, `agent-schemas/config.schema.json`, locales en/es/pt
- Docs: `knowledge-base/agent-manifest.md`

## Tests
- `cargo test -p houston-terminal-manager -p houston-engine-core` (effort resolution + adapter sets)
- `node --test app/src/lib/providers.test.mjs` (effort helpers)
- `cd app && pnpm tsc --noEmit && pnpm check-locales`
